card_roles.text: Claim: For finite-dimensional H, any pure-state family F, and one full-domain channel C:H->H tensor H whose marginals approximate every family member within half-trace error b, the report constructs one EB channel with uniform half-trace error at most kappa(b)+(1-kappa(b))14b for 0<=b<=1/4096. Here delta=4 sqrt(b), eta=(3/2)((1-4delta)^(-1/2)-1), a=delta+eta, kappa=(sqrt(a eta)+sqrt(2b))^2, and f(b)=(208+16 sqrt(6))b+O(b^(3/2)); linear order is optimal.

Interface: Finite-dimensional input, arbitrary pure-state family, one full-domain channel, and a uniform two-marginal broadcasting promise for every family member. The conclusion is statewise half-trace reconstruction, not diamond closeness.

Proof spine: A Stinespring dilation yields an approximate Schur idempotence relation. A convergent binomial correction gives an idempotent Schur mask; its norm forces an equivalence-relation partition. One common POVM distinguishes blocks, and representative-state preparation gives the EB channel and modulus.

Costs: For an explicitly supplied rational list of n states in dimension d, overlap formation costs O(n^2 d^2); the SDP has O(k d^2) real variables and k PSD blocks of order d. Unknown-state acquisition and device costs are excluded.
Failure: Does not cover general mixed families or establish dimension-free runtime or experimental access. Supplied finite SDP checks are not proof validation or external review.
Closest comparator: The premise differs from the stronger complete near-idempotence condition of N533. Standard broadcasting SDPs predate this candidate.
Open verification: Reconstruct the Schur-partition and common-POVM steps independently, verify the modulus algebra, and obtain external proof and prior-art review.

card_roles.text: Claim: For each integer s>=1, h=4s^2, let B0=[[1/4,0],[0,0]] and B1=[[1/4,1/(4s)],[1/(4s),0]] define normalized pure Gaussian states. Both formulas are known but label i is hidden. For independent unconditional copies, an always-output procedure realizing exactly the second-mode count law conditional on first-mode count h for either source has minimum fixed budget N*=ceil(log Z_h/(-log F_h)), where A_j=product_{r=0}^{j-1}(1-2r/h)^2, Z_h=sum_{j=0}^{h/2} A_j/(2j)!, and F_h=sqrt(1-(8h-1)/(15h^2)) is the SQUARED pure-state overlap. N*/h -> (15/4)log(cosh 1)=1.626678... . P0=delta_0; P1(2j)=A_j/((2j)!Z_h).

Interface: Unknown label; copies are the only source-dependent resource. Arbitrary collective/adaptive measurements are allowed; label-bearing advice, preparation-unitary access and conditional-state oracles are excluded. Output law is assessed unconditionally, charging failures. TV(P,Q)=1/2 sum|P-Q| and quantum trace distance=1/2||rho-sigma||_1. Integer h is restricted to 4s^2.

Proof spine: The zero-output effect must fix source 0, forcing F_h^N<=1/Z_h. Vacuum/nonvacuum detection in mode 2 has no-click probability F_h^N under source 1; rebalancing positive output mass attains the criterion. Integer boundaries reduce to the rational inequality [1-(8h-1)/(15h^2)]^N Z_h^2<=1. Geometric proposals for the known positive law use rational acceptance 2^J A_J/(2J)!.

Costs: Unconditional input mean photon count <=1/4; conditional output mean <=sinh(1). With label supplied, exact sampling uses <=4/3 expected proposals and expected bit work polynomial in log h. Exact acquisition rebalancing setup is polynomial in h, with O(h log h)-bit operands; copy optimality is not classical-runtime optimality. At TV<=1/12 fixed copies need N>=5h/96; almost-sure termination with adaptive count needs max_i E_i T>=5h/9216. Exact fair-bit algorithms have no bounded worst-case random-bit claim.
Failure: One heralded attempt can use one copy; its success probability cannot be discarded. The fixed-budget exact optimum does not apply to expected-copy budgets or arbitrary devices without this promise. Sufficiency assumes ideal independent preparations and ideal vacuum detection. No quantum hardware or physical acquisition was demonstrated.
Closest comparator: Two-state quantum discrimination/fidelity mechanisms are established prior art. The exact Gaussian operational witness and complete interface have unresolved historical priority.
Open verification: Obtain independent expert or formal review of the exact fixed-copy criterion, algebraic rebalancing coin and expected-bit sampler; determine priority of the exact witness without claiming novelty of discrimination.

Interface: One physical herald, binary output counts, rational nonnegative K and ell, normalizability and physicality. X exchanges ket/bra blocks. No arbitrary complex/signed kernels or multiple herald modes. Supplied exact parameters are not acquired from a device. The zero-displacement baseline and displaced extension have distinct endpoint/error allocations.

Proof spine: Schur elimination leaves [[a,b],[b,a]] with singleton weights (c,c). Cross-count weights w(k)=b^k H_(h-k)(a,c)^2/k!, H_n=[z^n]exp(a z^2/2+c z). Each parity subsequence is log-concave, though the full law need not be. Approximate ratio anchors plus factor-two inflation combine two envelopes without parity normalizers, total envelope mass <=12 times target mass. Conditional own-pair laws have decreasing ratios. Source Poisson and aggregate reverse-Schur binomial/negative-binomial draws reconstruct counts; N537 supplies coefficient evaluation.

Costs: No enumeration of h photons. Graph/routing operations and scalar-call bound O(m^3); rational pivot and large-count bit lengths, precision, capped tickets, rejection/fallback events and TV budget are charged. Final displaced endpoint allocates epsilon/4 to tickets and 3epsilon/4 across at most max_scalar_calls+4 scalar draws. card_roles.text: Claim: For all rational a,c>=0, binary integer n>=0, p>=1, H_n=[z^n]exp(a z^2/2+c z) can be recognized as zero or log H_n enclosed with absolute width <=2^-p in deterministic bit work polynomial in rational input length, log(n+1), and p. An expanded exact rational coefficient is not promised; it may require Omega(n) bits.

Interface: Nonnegative rational coefficients and a logarithmic interval/scaled mantissa-exponent output; exact zeros and elementary a=0 or c=0 cases handled separately. The mathematical algorithm and the actual adaptive Arb implementation have distinct complexity statuses. Symbols a,c,n and center u below are local.

Proof spine: For a,c>0, d=c/sqrt(a), sigma=(-1)^n, u=(d+sqrt(d^2+4n))/2: H_n=a^(n/2)/(n!sqrt(2pi)) integral_0^infinity t^n exp(-(t-d)^2/2)[1+sigma exp(-2dt)]dt. Fold parity before approximation; odd factor uses -expm1(-2dt). Normalize at u, use a uniform positive integral lower bound, Gaussian tails, and bounded complex extension. Certified Taylor quadrature or independently justified rational interpolation gives polynomial precision/cost. Use u-d=n/u to control cancellation in log prefactors. Small n uses a short positive finite sum.

Costs: For retained radius R=O(sqrt(p)), rational panels width 1/2 and q+1 equally spaced nodes give pointwise error <=(128/3)(2/3)^(q+1), total weight <=2R(2e)^q; q=O(p+log R), polynomial guard precision. Cancellation in prefactors needs O(log n) extra precision. Does not promise a polynomial-sized expanded coefficient or uniform runtime of a particular library.
Failure: Signed saddle subtraction can lose tiny odd displacement; the positive folding route avoids that obstruction. Relative error for H_n and absolute width for log H_n need explicit precision conversion; they are not the same quantity. Source code/audits remain ordinary model-assisted numerical evidence, not formal/expert certification.

Here R=2sqrt(a)+2sqrt(b), D_k(r)=(b/(a+b))r^(2k+2)(1+r^2)/(1-r^(2k+2)), H_k(r)=3sqrt(D_k(r))/sqrt(a)+E_k(r), E_k(r)=r^(2k+1)(1+r^2)/(sqrt(a)(1-r^(2k+2))). At fixed a,b,r the bound is O(r^k). card_roles.text: Claim: Let P0=Bern(a)^d with 0<a<=1/2, target A={1}, p=a^d and integer 0<=k<d. Set D_k=sum_(j=0)^k binom(d,j)((1-a)/a)^j and K=p^-1-D_k. If D_k<=K, the source constructs nonnegative P* with every marginal on at most k coordinates exactly equal to P0, P*(A)=2p and chi-square(P*||P0)=1/K<=2p. This divergence is minimal among laws satisfying those marginal and event-mass constraints. An adaptive assay revealing at most k distinct coordinates from each fresh specimen has identical transcript laws under P0 and P*, even with unlimited specimens. A separate positive regime assumes known product structure and explicit polynomial-size DNF failure modes and composes established product-estimation/weighted-witness methods.

Interface: Known d,a,k and a rare conjunction under a Bernoulli product baseline. The negative pair is indistinguishable from supplied low-order marginals; the assay reveals at most k distinct coordinates per fresh specimen. Reusing a specimen to observe more coordinates changes the contract. The positive regime requires true product structure and explicit DNF representation.

Proof spine: In L^2(P0), split the point-evaluation reproducing kernel at the all-ones vector into degrees <=k and >k. The high-degree residual is orthogonal to every function of <=k coordinates. Adding it to the likelihood ratio doubles target-event mass while preserving all those marginals. Its squared norm gives the chi-square value; Cauchy-Schwarz proves optimality. Transcript coupling handles the stated adaptive fresh-specimen assay.

Costs: The source gives a full-vector relative-estimation lower bound of Omega(1/(epsilon^2 p)) under its stated conditions despite exact supplied marginals through order k. P* has a compact exact rejection sampler with reported acceptance 1/2; constructing it does not reveal which real-world law holds. The positive product/DNF regime charges measurements and arithmetic and uses known methods.
Failure: D_k<=K is required. The divergence optimum is not by itself a finite-sample minimax theorem for every assay. Product and explicit-DNF assumptions are essential to the positive regime. No real failure law or general rare-event capability is established.
Closest comparator: Astra N492 studies rare-event certificate acquisition under a different interface. This result supplies a moment-matching/k-coordinate construction; it does not imply all higher-order validation is impossible.
Open verification: Independently verify the reproducing-kernel optimality and adaptive-transcript quantifiers; price any escape through extra coordinates, specimen reuse, structure acquisition or conditional-law access.

card_roles.text: Claim: For the explicitly constructed rational, nonnegative, pure undisplaced Gaussian pair kernels with operator norm<1/2 and mean photon number<5/12, condition on one photon in every graph mode and leave two output modes unheralded. A classical conditional sampler with adjustable TV error and polynomial runtime in exact input length and inverse error is polynomially equivalent, under the stated reductions, to an FPRAS for perfect matchings of arbitrary unweighted simple graphs, including exact zero detection.

Interface: Restricted supplied Gaussian family and graph; one unit-photon herald in every original graph mode, two output modes remain. The sampler must work uniformly over every nonzero herald. The reductions charge precision, encoded bit length, conditional calls, zero heralds and sample budget.

Proof spine: Attach two leaves to an edge uv. The two remaining modes output only 00 or 11 with q=R^2 p_uv^2/(1+R^2 p_uv^2), where p_uv is a uniform-perfect-matching edge marginal. Dyadic calibration and self-reduction recover the count from conditional samples; approximate counting supplies the reverse direction. Source replays check finite graph/hafnian identities and support.

Costs: The reduction uses O(n^2 log(n/delta)+n^3 epsilon^-2 log(n/delta)) conditional samples plus a coarse-search term; the finest requested TV error is Theta(epsilon/n). Literal herald rejection costs at least (63/128)4^n preparations per accepted calibrated event. The direct sampler is not implemented; proof constants request about 7.3e8 samples already at n=2, epsilon=.1, delta=.01.
Failure: This is an equivalence, not an efficient conditional sampler, matching algorithm or complexity separation. It applies only to the stated family and herald pattern. Variable-subset GBS has a different output law and does not supply the required conditional guarantee.
Closest comparator: Astra N417/N419 cover Gaussian samplers/reductions at distinct interfaces. Hafnian graph encodings and variable-subset GBS are prior art; this result does not claim the broad Gaussian/matching connection as new.
Open verification: Find a proved direct conditional sampler or a materially different resource contract; otherwise obtain expert review of both reduction directions and retain the capability barrier.

card_roles.text: Claim: For a supplied rational ten-state generator Q, changed discrete-time chains P_e=I+eQ (e=1,1/2) have stationary six-label observed laws that are time-reversal invariant and pass the stated centered reflection complete-positivity tests, yet an explicit rational statistic W_e on five consecutive letters has nonnegative expectation under every stationary reversible hidden Markov model with deterministic emissions and negative expectation under P_e. The e=1/2 target additionally has positive observable spectrum [0,1], hence completely monotone scalar correlations. A certified empirical-Bernstein test for this half-step target has sufficient budget 2,057,310,156,600,085,612,368 independent stationary windows. This is sufficient for the stated test, not necessary sample complexity.

Interface: The construction changes the continuous-time source process; P_e is not claimed to sample the original CTMC. Competitors are stationary reversible hidden Markov models with deterministic emissions and arbitrary hidden cardinality. The finite test assumes independent stationary five-letter windows and stationary preparation; it is not a guarantee for one correlated trajectory under arbitrary mixing.

Proof spine: Exact rational one-step features and a five-marker left inverse define a bounded five-letter statistic. A universal inequality forces nonnegative expectation for each stated reversible hidden model; exact target algebra makes it negative. Outward dyadic rounding and exact five-word recursion enclose the half-step target second moment, and empirical Bernstein yields the stated iid-window sufficient count.

Costs: Source reports 82 rational seed/geometry checks and exhaustive enumeration of all 6^5=7,776 words. The half-step certificate requires about 2.06e21 independent stationary windows, over 10^22 observed letters plus independent stationary preparation. A separate original-CTMC variance bound is about 2e64 windows but conditional on inherited mean/gap/range premises. Both are impractical.
Failure: Not a necessary sample lower bound, not a single-correlated-trajectory guarantee, and not an experiment or explanation of a natural process. The finite-state rational seed is supplied. It does not establish a general thermodynamic estimator or historic discovery.
Closest comparator: Related to Astra N509/N511/N512 finite-support and hidden-equilibrium work but uses a distinct five-letter statistic and a changed discrete-time source; no common interface or proof transfer is inferred.
Open verification: Independently audit the universal hidden-model inequality and exact certificate; materially lower the certified range-to-gap ratio or prove improved acquisition under explicit preparation and trajectory assumptions.

card_roles.text: Claim: Under a fixed-period model with independent mean-zero division innovations, the report derives conditional within/across-division MSD formulas and an explicit causal delayed response h_l(t)=h_0(t-l). Numerically choosing l≈1.301 hours makes one defined continuous-lag aggregate ratio R=1/2 for T=10.2 hours and chosen integral memory 5.4 hours. The model also predicts suppressed short-lag changes across division, quiet within-cycle intervals and an upturn in growth averaged since birth late in the cycle. Synthetic measurements reportedly separate its first prediction from an OU comparator; a published age-variance curve is qualitatively in tension with the upturn. This is a falsification-oriented countermodel, not a biological explanation.

Interface: Centered log-growth fluctuation is driven only by independent division innovations through a specified continuous causal pulse. T=10.2 hours and integral memory 5.4 hours are chosen values, not measured parameters. Synthetic filtering uses the author's Matérn-3/2 covariance implementation, not the full experimental Julia pipeline. No raw experimental trajectory was acquired or reanalysed.

Proof spine: Exact phase identities give constant age variance and phase-averaged covariance for an inherited sine/plateau/cosine pulse. A time shift preserves those identities while changing alignment with division. Conditional MSD integrals yield a delayed-response root for one chosen aggregate statistic. Synthetic filtering tests further predictions, including a raw-log-mass second-difference covariance diagnostic; a late-cycle variance formula yields the qualitative published-curve tension.

Costs: Reported internal checks compare adaptive quadrature with closed forms and state-space outputs with dense calculations. Synthetic trials use 24 lineages by 10 cycles per condition and reused seeds; these are not empirical replications. Raw-data estimation, the full experimental pipeline, causal perturbation and molecular mechanism acquisition are absent. The specific analysis scripts/environment named in the report were not attached.
Failure: The delay matches a theoretical null and was not fitted to raw trajectories. The apparent age-variance mismatch is a qualitative warning, not formal rejection, because source trajectories and processing were not replayed. The response has no measured molecular source. A reported matrix builder reads uninitialized storage; Julia was unavailable. Glass and peroxide work was screened, not explained.
Closest comparator: A continuation of Astra N494/N496/N499 pulse and provenance work. This report does not validate or correct those historical claims. The cited 2026 growth-noise preprint was not fully reviewed; priority is UNKNOWN.
Open verification: Obtain the cited code/environment and raw data; independently reproduce the full pipeline on held-out cycles with trend, lineage and selection controls; then perturb the proposed delay without refitting. No biological mechanism should be inferred before these observations.

card_roles.text: Claim: Let a compact group G act orthogonally on a finite-dimensional real inner-product space V by pi, with normalized Haar measure. For independent Haar controls and an m-state Markov simulator whose row-stochastic update P_t(g) may depend measurably on time and the current control, set b_i(t)=E[pi(g_t...g_1)x 1{S_t=i}] and R_t=sum_i ||b_i(t)||. Define kappa_m(pi)=sup_{||v||=1} sup_{||w_1||=...=||w_m||=1} integral_G max_j <w_j,pi(g)v> dg. Then R_t<=kappa_m(pi)R_(t-1), hence R_T<=kappa_m(pi)^T||x||. The adjoint action-compatible transfer is (A_P z)_i=integral pi(g)^(-1)(sum_j P_g(i,j)z_j)dg and has norm at most kappa_m(pi).

Interface: The controls are independent Haar draws; the representation is orthogonal; the state is the only charged persistent record of past controls. Fresh randomness is allowed. The transition rule can depend on time and the current control. The theorem bounds unnormalized conditional means, not only pure or initially orbit-valued states.

Proof spine: The conditional-mean recursion expresses each next state vector as a sum of group-averaged stochastic transitions. Align one unit vector with each resulting integral. Row-stochasticity bounds their sum by the orbit-code maximum defining kappa; the triangle inequality and summation over states give the one-step contraction. The transfer operator is the corresponding adjoint map.

Costs: A state-retention theorem only. The description size of P_t, gate acquisition, precision, barycentric compilation and sampling costs are not bounded. Persistent seeds, correlated external noise and external continuous controllers must be charged or are outside the model.
Failure: This does not lower-bound signed-coordinate or unrestricted numerical simulators. Correlated external noise changes the memory contract. The Haar one-step coefficient cannot be applied unchanged to arbitrary finite control alphabets; see N546.
Closest comparator: The representation-valued transform and spherical quantization ingredients are known mathematics. The source presents the operational contraction/composition interface as its candidate contribution; novelty is UNKNOWN. N507 is a scoped comparison only and is not used as a proved premise.
Open verification: Independently verify the conditional-mean contraction for the stated measurable transition class and compare the transfer operator with prior representation-transform literature.

card_roles.text: Claim: For the standard SO(d) action, eta_(m,d)=sup_(v_1,...,v_m in S^(d-1)) integral max_j <u,v_j> d sigma(u) is the constrained spherical quantization coefficient. The source proves R_T<=eta_(m,d)^T with equality attainable for the retention problem; eta_(m,2)=m sin(pi/m)/pi; eta_(m,3)<=1-1/m (no equality claim); and 1-eta_(m,d)=Theta_d(m^(-2/(d-1))) for fixed d. For p_*(+|x,g_1,...,g_t,u)=(1+delta<u,g_t...g_1 x>)/2, 0<delta<=1/d and 0<epsilon<delta/(2d), the minimum number of positive Markov states uniformly simulating all preparations, readouts and gate words through horizon T is Theta_(d,delta,epsilon)(T^((d-1)/2)). The static positive factorization size is exactly d+1.

Interface: Fixed dimension d>=2; x,u range over the Euclidean unit ball; each supplied gate is in SO(d); controls in the retention experiment are independent Haar draws. The simulator has an m-state Markov memory, arbitrary time/current-gate measurable stochastic updates and uniform additive probability error epsilon. The exponent is fixed-d and the constants depend on d, delta and epsilon.

Proof spine: The spherical coefficient equals one minus half the optimal mean squared nearest-codeword distance. A conditional-mean argument gives the exact retention contraction and a nearest-codeword construction attains it. Cap covering and packing establish the fixed-d quantization rate. A bounded terminal score converts retention into the state lower bound; a circumscribed polytope and barycentric stochastic updates give the matching upper bound. A regular simplex gives the exact static d+1 factorization and rank lower bound.

Costs: The theorem counts states, not bits or runtime. Gate acquisition, net generation, triangulation, barycentric map size, probability precision, transition-table description and sampling are not bounded. For d=3, T-state order means Theta(log T) classical bits under ideal state encoding, not Theta(T) bits.
Failure: Continuous Haar controls are essential to the displayed coefficient. The result does not imply a lower bound for signed coordinates or an ordinary finite-precision simulator without charging its full persistent memory and numerical resources. Finite groups can admit bounded-state exact constructions.
Closest comparator: Spherical quantization and manifold approximation have established literature and are not claimed as inventions. The candidate contribution is the operational positive-composition retention law and its matching state-count construction; priority remains UNKNOWN.
Open verification: Independently check the exact attainment argument and the conversion from the bounded score to a uniform state lower bound; complete a focused prior-art comparison before any novelty claim.

card_roles.text: Claim: Fix D>=2, n=D^2-1, r_0=sqrt((D-1)/D), and H_0(D), the real Hilbert space of traceless Hermitian D by D matrices with Hilbert-Schmidt inner product. Let K_D={A_rho=(rho-I/D)/r_0: rho>=0, Tr(rho)=1}. For supplied unitaries U_1,...,U_t with V_t=U_t...U_1 and any B in the Hilbert-Schmidt unit ball, the target bit law is p_*(+|A,U_1,...,U_t,B)=1/2(1+delta Tr(B V_t A V_t^*)). For fixed D, 0<delta<=1/n and 0<epsilon<delta/(2n), the minimum number of classical Markov states that uniformly approximates all preparations, terminal queries, and words of length at most T is Theta_(D,delta,epsilon)(T^(D-1)). The static positive factorization size is exactly D^2; the quantum realization uses Hilbert-space dimension D; the state-count law corresponds to (D-1)log_2 T+O_(D,delta,epsilon)(1) classical bits.

Interface: The preparation rho=I/D+r_0 A ranges over all density matrices; B ranges over the Hilbert-Schmidt unit ball; controls are arbitrary supplied unitary words; the binary effect is E_B=1/2(I+delta B/r_0). The classical simulator must meet uniform additive error epsilon for all inputs and all word lengths <=T, with arbitrary measurable time/current-unitary stochastic transitions. Only the finite internal state stores history; no persistent seed, correlated external noise or stored continuous state is free.

Proof spine: For independent Haar unitaries, unnormalized conditional means contract by kappa_(m,D). A uniform small-ball bound for every unit traceless-Hermitian conjugation orbit follows by selecting a nontrivial eigenvalue gap and comparing nearby conjugates to complex Grassmannian projection balls. This yields 1-kappa_(m,D)=Theta_D(m^(-1/(D-1))) without claiming equality of repeated powers. A bounded terminal score gives the Omega(T^(D-1)) state lower bound. A projective net and an inflated convex polytope with barycentric stochastic updates give O(T^(D-1)); a regular simplex proves the separate exact D^2 static factorization size.

Costs: Fixed-D asymptotic state count only. The theorem does not bound the size or precision of the transition maps, construction of projective nets/polytope triangulations, barycentric evaluation, sampling, gate compilation or runtime. It is not a general computational quantum speedup and is not uniform jointly in D,T,delta,epsilon.
Failure: No sharp state law is established for the fixed five-gate qubit alphabet in N546. No lower bound follows for an unrestricted floating-point simulator unless all persistent numerical state is charged. The source explicitly does not assert R_T=kappa_(m,D)^T.
Closest comparator: The source identifies Montina 2008/2010 and correlated-noise models as important predecessors; detailed comparison with those full papers and the 2026 finite-memory preprint is incomplete. No priority claim is made. N507 is unreviewed context only, not an imported theorem.
Open verification: Independently audit the Grassmann small-ball and eigenvalue-gap argument, the weak-effect and uniform-score contracts, both asymptotic bounds, and the exact static rank argument. Then complete the prior-art review.

card_roles.text: Claim: For a probability law nu on SO(d), define eta_m(nu)=sup_(||v||=1,n_1,...,n_m in S^(d-1)) integral max_j <n_j,g v> dnu(g). The source derives R_T<=inf_(1<=k<=T) eta_m(nu^(*k))^floor(T/k). If nu has support size at most m, eta_m(nu)=1, so a one-step coefficient gives no contraction in that regime. A finite group of rotations nevertheless admits a uniform-in-horizon exact weak-readout realization using a finite invariant polytope. The sharp law m_*(T)=Theta(T) for A={I,R_x,R_x^(-1),R_z,R_z^(-1)}, with the two named-axis rotations having cosine 3/5 and sine 4/5, delta=1/3 and epsilon=1/72, is explicitly unresolved in this investigation.

Interface: Independent controls with law nu, finite-state Markov updates, and all persistent classical memory charged. The block bound is an interface for products of k controls. The five-gate question uses the same d=3 state-count contract as the sphere theorem. The stated unresolved status is local to this investigation and does not assert the question is globally open.

Proof spine: Apply the one-step conditional-mean contraction to k independent controls jointly, whose product has law nu^(*k), for floor(T/k) blocks; leftover steps have coefficient at most one. If support size is <=m, choose codewords containing the images of each state under every supported control, giving eta_m(nu)=1. The finite-group exact realization uses the group translates of a circumscribed simplex. These facts limit direct use of the continuous-Haar exponent.

Costs: The block profile is a state-retention bound. The finite-alphabet five-gate asymptotic state count is unknown here. Compilation, gate acquisition, precision, and runtime are not established.
Failure: The Haar one-step coefficient cannot be substituted for the fixed alphabet. The density of the specified gate group establishes density only, not a quantitative lower bound. Solving this question would still require separate significance and priority review.
Closest comparator: Finite-control block products, finite cyclic code formulas and invariant polytopes are the packet comparators. No global open-problem or novelty claim is made.
Open verification: Prove or refute m_*(T)=Theta(T) for the exact five-gate qubit alphabet at delta=1/3 and epsilon=1/72 under the charged Markov-memory interface; perform a dedicated prior-art review before calling it open.

card_roles.text: Claim: Let the same smooth unknown drift b and constant symmetric D≻0 govern controlled diffusions on R^d with vanishing boundary flux/integrability, or on a flat torus. Under known smooth controls u_i, strictly positive stationary C² densities p_i and divergence-free currents J_i=(b+u_i)p_i−D∇p_i, set r=p_i/p_j, w=∇log r and δu=u_i−u_j. For every admissible scalar q for which the integrations are justified, the source derives D:E_{p_i}[q(r)wwᵀ]=E_{p_i}[q(r)δu·w]. Thus full rank of the collected symmetric matrix features M_{ij,q}=E_{p_i}[q(r)wwᵀ], in dimension d(d+1)/2, identifies the constant D uniquely.

Interface: All regimes share b and constant state-independent D; intervention fields are known; stationary laws are exact and fully observed for the theorem. The feature-rank condition is a hypothesis to check, not a consequence of having multiple regimes. The test-function class for q and the required boundary/integrability conditions are not fully enumerated in the source.

Proof spine: Use J_i=rJ_j+p_i(δu−Dw). Choose f with f′(r)=q(r)/r, multiply the stationary divergence equation by f(r), cancel the J_j term as a gradient against a divergence-free current, and integrate the remaining divergence by parts. The resulting identity is linear in the symmetric entries of D.

Costs: No finite-sample or numerical acquisition bound. The features require density-ratio gradients and stationary expectations; acquiring or estimating these, waiting for each regime to mix, and calibrating controls are uncharged. An algebraic perturbation bound is conditional on the exact design singular value and feature errors.

card_roles.text: Claim: Let s_i=∇log p_i and T_i=∇²p_i/p_i for d+1 controlled experiments, and define W(x)=[s_1−s_0,…,s_d−s_0]. For i=1,…,d define h_i=D:(T_i−T_0)−∇·u_i−u_i·s_i+∇·u_0+u_0·s_0. Under the source’s smoothness and exact-law assumptions, if the pairwise matrix features identify constant D and W(x) is invertible almost everywhere, subtracting stationary Fokker–Planck equations identifies b(x)=W(x)^{−T}h(x) almost everywhere. Conversely, for a compatible pair of positive stationary densities on T², known D and controls do not identify general b: adding v(x)=p_0(x)^{−1}S∇(p_1/p_0), for a nonzero constant skew matrix S, preserves both stationary laws but changes their currents.

Interface: The sufficient theorem assumes full-state, exactly known positive stationary densities, common smooth b, constant D, known controls, full rank in the D-feature system and almost-everywhere pointwise rank of W. The counterexample is on the flat two-dimensional torus and retains the same D and controls. Neither statement is a finite-sample result.

Proof spine: Subtract the stationary Fokker–Planck equations to obtain d linear equations in b(x); invert W wherever it has full rank. For the obstruction, p_0v=S∇r has zero divergence, and p_1v=rS∇r also has zero divergence because S is skew and Hessians are symmetric.

Costs: The nonparametric formula uses density scores, second derivatives, pointwise matrix inversion and conditioning. Statistical error, regularization, regions where W is nearly singular, mixing, finite samples and partial observation have no guarantee.
Failure: A singular or poorly conditioned W prevents stable drift recovery. The two-regime gauge refutes unrestricted full-drift identification from those two laws, but it does not refute recovery of D or the d+1 rank-conditional theorem. A radial or latent projection does not satisfy the full-state interface.

Thus an arbitrary nonlinear log p_0 is allowed within this exact-tilt family and the circulation can be nonzero. Fewer than d independent tilt directions cannot guarantee full generator identification in the worst case within the family.

card_roles.text: Claim: The packet reports three synthetic diagnostics. In a three-dimensional non-Gaussian quartic exact-i.i.d. tilt model, 25 repetitions at 32,000 accepted draws per regime produced mean relative Frobenius errors 1.70% for B, 1.71% for D and 1.52% for K; local generation/fitting time excludes physical preparation and equilibration. A two-dimensional non-affine torus calculation used deterministic stationary-grid solutions, not random observed samples: at grid side 192, three-regime D error was 0.0288%, while the two-regime weighted system had condition number about 198 and 3.74% error. A quartic-family entropy-production estimate reported 1.63% mean relative error at 32,000 draws per regime over 12 repetitions, with the quartic potential family supplied and an independently sampled reference based on 750,000 additional baseline draws. These are source-reported synthetic outcomes, not empirical scientific validation or finite-sample theorems.

Interface: The 3D study uses exact independent synthetic stationary draws and a specified quartic potential; the torus study solves a discretized stationary PDE and computes grid scores/Hessians; the entropy-production study supplies the quartic potential family and draws a separate reference. None uses real physical data or charges physical stationary preparation.
Reported diagnostic scope: The handoff records generated sample populations, numerical stationary grids, estimates, errors, replication counts and selected controls. The finite proof-check output tests floating-point consistency only. The packet scripts/results are preserved; no script or experiment was rerun during repository intake.

Costs: Reported CPU timings omit physical perturbation, calibration, mixing/equilibration and instrument costs; the entropy-production reference uses 750,000 additional exact independent baseline draws (1,050,000 rejection proposals). Grid computation is exponential in dimension. No costed physical or noisy-correlated stationary-snapshot acquisition is demonstrated.

card_roles.text: Claim: Let T(ρ,σ)=½‖ρ−σ‖₁. For every finite recipient count m≥2 and ε,η>0, the source constructs finite d,L, a finite family F={ρ_{ψ_x}} on H=⊕_{r=0}^L Sym^{m^r}(C^d), and one fixed positive finite prior (w_x), such that a full-domain permutation-symmetric CPTP map B:H→H^{⊗m} has every one-recipient marginal error at most 1/L≤ε, while every common entanglement-breaking map E:H→H and every family of commuting replacement states diagonal in one common basis have worst-case error at least 1−η. The same lower bounds hold as averages under the fixed prior. For the corresponding classical–quantum state ω_XH=Σ_x w_x|x⟩⟨x|⊗ρ_{ψ_x}, each XH_j marginal can be broadcast within 1/L, yet its trace distance from every state classical on H is at least 1−η, even when the comparator may change its X marginal. Consequently the suprema of EB and commuting reconstruction error are one for every positive broadcasting tolerance at fixed finite m. The proof gives formulas a=(1/L)Σ_{r=1}^L(k_r+1)/(k_r+d), β=min{1,√(Σ_{r=1}^L D_{k_r}/D_{2k_r})}, with k_r=m^r and D_s=binom(d+s−1,s); choose L large and d sufficiently large (or d=m²m^{2L}) so a,β→0. One common finite weighted projective 2m^L-design supports all comparators and bases simultaneously.

Interface: All maps act on finite-dimensional full matrix algebras and are CPTP; T is half trace norm. The input family consists of rank-L mixed direct-sum states ρ_ψ=0_{H_0}⊕(1/L)⊕_{r=1}^L p_ψ^{⊗m^r}, p_ψ=|ψ⟩⟨ψ|, with a fixed finite design prior. The construction's input already contains a classically uncertain number of genuine unknown-state copies, up to K=m^L. The EB comparator is one common physical measure-and-prepare channel for all family states, with arbitrary finite outcomes. The commuting comparator must use one common basis. The cq comparator can choose a different X marginal but must be classical on H. The source's marginal error is exactly 1/L for its constructed channel; the optimal broadcast error is only bounded above by 1/L. Outputs need not be close to the product family and are highly correlated.

Source-reported proof spine: Let H_r=Sym^{k_r}(C^d), k_r=m^r. The explicit isometry partitions each symmetric k_r-copy block into m groups of k_{r−1}; the full-domain channel maps each sector down one level and sends H_0 to a fixed product output. Only the top and bottom blocks differ in each marginal, giving exact half-trace error 1/L. A fixed decoder extracts one qudit; composing it with any EB map and applying the pure-state estimation bound (k+1)/(k+d) yields the prior-average EB lower bound. For commuting families, the support projections Q_ψ=Lρ_ψ obey a second-moment bound summed over an arbitrary common orthonormal basis; the finite exact 2K design preserves the needed moments. A measurement of X and Q_{ψ_x}, followed by data processing and Cauchy–Schwarz, handles arbitrary changes to the comparator's X marginal. Explicit parameter choices make the bounds approach one while the marginal error tends to zero.

Costs: K=m^L genuine copies occur in the highest sector, dim H=Σ_{r=0}^L D_{k_r}, and the Carathéodory finite prior may require up to D_{2K}² points. The explicit algebraic cubature also has (ceil((2K+1)/2)(2K+1))^{d−1} points; the paper does not establish an efficient construction at large parameters. No cost is supplied for preparing the input from one unknown qudit; such preparation is not part of the contract. The channel is an explicit mathematical CPTP map on a very large space, not a demonstrated resource-bounded physical implementation. Global cloning error approaches one; for L≥2 the source also gives ‖Φ−Φ²‖_diamond=2. Small marginal trace distance therefore does not imply global product fidelity or near-idempotence.
Failure: This refutes only dimension-independent, statewise trace-distance stability without dimension/resource restrictions. It does not refute exact no-broadcasting, bounded-Holevo-capacity conclusions, small-Holevo-loss conclusions, or the pure-family theorem N534. The constructed states are mixed (choose L≥2), and dimension, copy number and Holevo capacity diverge. The exact capacity/loss boundary is routed separately in N553. No NPT bound-entanglement result, FEI solution, efficient one-qudit acquisition, practical experiment, or historic-scale breakthrough is claimed.
Closest comparator: Exact no-broadcasting and finite pure-state estimation/design results are cited as predecessors; the pure-state estimation inequality is reproved in the source. The source reports a targeted but non-exhaustive prior-art search, not historical priority. N534 assumes pure inputs and is not contradicted by this mixed, unbounded-resource family.
Open verification: Independently reconstruct the direct-sum CPTP map, the one fixed finite-prior EB bound, the basis-uniform commuting bound and the changed-X-marginal cq argument. Check all norm conventions, finite-design moment order, quantifiers and resource dependencies; then assess priority against the exact prior literature.

card_roles.text: Claim: For each integer d>=1, let Q_d identify U and U P for P in Sym(d), with q_d([U],[V])=min_P ||U-VP||_F/sqrt(d). Define Delta_copy e_i=e_i tensor e_i and Phi_d([U])=(U tensor U)Delta_copy U*/sqrt(d), viewed in the complex Hilbert space Hom(C^d,C^d tensor C^d) with Frobenius norm. The source proves q_d([U],[V]) <= ||Phi_d([U])-Phi_d([V])||_F <= 3 q_d([U],[V]). Thus this quotient metric has a Hilbert embedding with distortion at most 3 uniformly in d. For a finite irreducible reversible Markov kernel with spectral gap gamma, this yields the stated squared-distance Poincare bound with factor 9/gamma; a separate conductance bound controls unsquared distances with factor 3/h.

card_roles.text: Claim: For a nonexplosive stochastic mass-action CTMC with at most R non-null reactions, input order at most k, positive rates bounded below by known kappa_min, and the stated deterministic reset interface, let x(S)_i=M 1[i in S], M=max(k,1). The infinitesimal departure hazard is q(S)=sum_{A subseteq S} theta_A, hence q(b)=sum_A theta_A product_{i in A} b_i is a nonnegative sparse multilinear polynomial whose nonzero monomials identify exactly the distinct reactant supports. The source gives PositivePeel using O(R[(k+1)log(d+1)+2^k]) exact correlation/point-query types.

Interface: d labeled species; known bounded input order k, rate floor kappa_min, rate ceiling, and controlled exact molecule-count resets; complete labeled destructive endpoint states and calibrated short observation times. Duplicate reactions sharing a reactant support are aggregated at this stage. Randomized finite-sample recovery additionally assumes independent runs, known rate/resource bounds, and no hidden species or readout noise.

Proof spine: The t-downarrow-0 departure rate is a positive sum of enabled channel propensities. On binary occupancy masks it is a sparse nonnegative multilinear polynomial. Positive Fourier differences D(B,H) test for an extension support; binary peeling recovers a maximal support, and Boolean Möbius inversion extracts its aggregate coefficient before subtraction.

Costs: The query count is not experiment count: each correlation is estimated from short-time endpoint samples. Finite-sample guarantees depend on kappa_min, time bias, rates, R, k, ell and confidence. Very small rates, high order, reset fidelity, complete counting, computation, sample volume and raw-data retention may dominate.
Failure: Support recovery does not identify product complexes or separate channels with identical reactant and product complexes. It excludes null reactions; exact controlled resets and complete state observation are essential. The attached note provides no supporting code or run receipts, and does not establish realistic cell-scale acquisition.
Closest comparator: Positive sparse polynomial and weighted-hypergraph reconstruction are established neighboring problems; the attached note explicitly does not claim an optimal decoder or novelty of those ingredients.

card_roles.text: Claim: For each nonzero net jump nu, the infinitesimal endpoint intensity has the finite expansion j_nu(x)=sum_alpha kappa_(alpha,alpha+nu) product_i binom(x_i,alpha_i). For every candidate alpha with |alpha|_1<=k and alpha+nu>=0 coordinatewise, the aggregate coefficient is isolated by the multivariate forward difference (Delta^alpha j_nu)(0). Under bounded reaction orders and the source interface, this identifies observable directed reactant/product complexes and their aggregate rates.

Interface: Uses the same exact-reset, independent-run, complete labeled endpoint, calibrated-time stochastic mass-action contract as N559. It concerns infinitesimal jump intensities reconstructed through short-time endpoint laws; no reaction-event trajectory is assumed. Finite-sample rate recovery is epsilon-accurate under an explicit positive rate floor and known bounds.

Proof spine: Expand each jump intensity in the binomial/Newton basis. The identity Delta binom(x,a)=binom(x,a-1) makes evaluation at zero after Delta^alpha isolate the coefficient at alpha. The displayed alternating finite sum gives the inversion.

Costs: Candidate seed states scale as (k+1)^k per recovered support; endpoint sample costs depend on short-time bias, confidence, rate floors, number of possible jumps and full-state readout. The source provides conservative batch and arithmetic bounds, not a cost-free exact real-rate oracle.
Failure: Net-zero reactions are invisible, identical (alpha,beta) channels are only recovered through summed rates, and incomplete/latent species observation invalidates the contract. Theorem concerns non-null bounded-order channels; no simultaneous estimation of arbitrary hidden rates is claimed.
Closest comparator: Finite differences in the binomial basis are standard. The contribution claimed by the source is their use with positive-hazard support peeling and a fully charged active endpoint interface, not a new difference calculus.

The source candidate characterizes eventual entanglement breaking by nilpotence of the cross transfer at every proper invariant corner of Φ^L; testing the d^2-th power gives a finite real-algebraic criterion. Failure: This concerns one algebraic CP map and its powers, not arbitrary nonstationary words. No robust storage or positive-capacity conclusion follows from an NPT witness whose margin may decay.

card_roles.text: Claim: For d≥2 and a length-n serial word T of maps on M_d that are both completely positive and 2-copositive (CP ∩ 2-CoPos), n≥d−1, the source gives entanglement-breaking CP maps E,F with E=q_nT+F, E*(I)=T*(I), F*(I)=(1−q_n)T*(I), where q_n=[1+4√2 d²(1−1/(8d))^floor(n/(d−1))]^−(d−1). For every reference and positive joint input X, ||(id⊗(T−E))(X)||_1≤2(1−q_n) tr[(id⊗T)(X)]. For trace-preserving words, the source gives a sufficient O(d² log(d/η)) length for diamond error at most η.

Interface: Every counted serial factor must lie in CP ∩ 2-CoPos (both CP and 2-copositive); factors may vary and need not be trace preserving. The output effect is matched exactly. The conditioned-output guarantee is via the trace-relative bound for positive joint inputs, avoiding an inverse success-probability penalty.
Proof spine: A Gaussian concurrence gap supplies an explicit contraction; depolarizing repair constructs an EB component, and effect matching controls the successful output trace under postselection.

Costs: Explicit q_n above; for trace-preserving words the stated sufficient length is (d−1) ceil[8d log(8√2(d−1)d²/η)] for η∈(0,2). This is conservative and does not include an efficient measure-and-prepare decomposition cost.
Failure: An averaged PPT map does not imply each branch is CP/2-copositive. No arbitrary network or tensor-power impossibility follows. Earlier exactness barriers show approximate EB replacement alone does not settle exact EB for unrestricted nonunital words.
Closest comparator: The source credits Gaussian concurrence, Bell-flag/2-EB iteration and filtered prior results, while keeping exact arbitrary-word membership and approximation distinct.
Open verification: Independently check the concurrence contraction, CP/2-copositive branch condition, exact effect identities, trace-relative bound and constants. Compare against cited 2-EB and concurrence mechanisms before quantitative reuse.

card_roles.text: Claim: Let q be a prime power, A_1,…,A_m∈F_q^{p×n}, c_i∈F_q^n, and let g:F_q^p→F_q^m be efficiently evaluable. Suppose a certified integer R satisfies rank(Σ_i λ_i A_i)≥R for every nonzero λ∈F_q^m. For F(x) with rows xᵀA_i+c_iᵀ, the source derives an exact rejection sampler whose output conditioned on success is uniform over every pair in S_g={(x,y):F(x)y=g(x)}, including singular fibers. For R≥m+1, its expected number of trials is at most (1+α)/(1−α/(q−1))<3, where α=(q^m−1)q^(−R). In the pure bilinear fixed-target case c_i=0 and g(x)=b, R≥m suffices for fewer than four expected trials. For x=x_0+Pu of codimension a and a graph restriction Dy=h(x) with k independent rows, the source proves a transformed rank bound R−a−k; the <3 guarantee persists when R−a−k≥m+1.

Interface: Finite field F_q; matrices A_i and offsets c_i are supplied; g is evaluated as a supplied circuit/algorithm. The exact output domain is all satisfying joint pairs, sampled uniformly, not a chosen affine chart or only full-rank fibers. A valid collective-rank lower bound R must be certified. The stated closure covers affine restriction of x and a full-row-rank affine graph constraint on y with efficiently evaluable h; arbitrary added polynomial constraints are outside the interface.

Proof spine: For each dual λ and affine-kernel point x, the proposal/kernel factors give each admissible pair (x,y) the same one-trial probability q^(−p)/(1+α); counting the dual annihilator of F(x) yields the identical mass q^(m−p−n)/(1+α) for every solution pair. A projective union bound controls row-deficient x and supplies the expected-trial bounds. Under the stated conditioning, substitution through a right inverse and a basis for ker D transforms A_i to PᵀA_iQ and loses at most a+k rank.

Costs: Per trial: polynomially many finite-field operations in (m,p,n), one evaluation of g, exact linear-system solves, and O((m+p+n)log q) expected unbiased bits; the certified regimes give fewer than three or four expected trials. For square n×n matrices, the source gives a structured Moore-interpolation certificate R=n−s using O(n³+mn²) extension-field operations after a verified F_{q^n} representation. Field construction/search and verification are charged; the certificate is coordinate-dependent, and finding a favorable hidden basis is not included.
Failure: A high collective-rank certificate is a strong promise; individual A_i ranks do not suffice, and general minimum-combination-rank acquisition is not solved. The Moore certificate can weaken under an unknown basis scramble. Uncharged nonlinear identification can make a conditioned system empty (the alternating-matrix y=x example); rank loss and added constraints must be charged. Outside the certified regimes rejection may fail to terminate on an empty solution set, so this is not a general decision procedure or generic constraint solver.
Closest comparator: The source identifies Moore interpolation, linearized-polynomial/rank-metric bounds, and the pivot-chart triangular argument as established ingredients; it cites exact sampling for a single quadratic equation. The specific multi-constraint dual-kernel law and charged nonlinear conditioning are a targeted, unresolved prior-art question; absence from this search is not novelty evidence.
Open verification: Independently reconstruct the equal-mass law including singular fibers, the projective deficiency bound, exact random-bit allocation, the R−a−k conditioning charge, and the square-map Moore certificate. Check empty-set behavior, hidden-basis degradation, all cost terms, and the exact multi-constraint prior-art boundary before reuse.

card_roles.text: Claim: For π(λ)=2^(−wt(λ))/(3/2)^m on F_2^m, equivalently independent Bernoulli(1/3) bits, let Q be any mixture of at most K uniform laws on affine subspaces and assume π(λ)≤ρQ(λ) pointwise. For integers 0≤D<m and t with positive numerator, the source derives ρ≥[Pr(Bin(m,1/3)≤t)−K(2/3)^(m−D)]/Pr(Bin(D+1,1/2)≤t). For m divisible by 8 it gives the weakened bound ρ≥[1−exp(−m/288)−K(2/3)^(m/8)]exp(m/112) for a stated choice of D,t, when the bracket is positive; hence polynomial K entails exponential overhead in that regime. Separately, the simpler rank-bound affine-cover construction obeys C/Z≥(4/3)^m/K. The target itself is exactly sampled by independent bits, so this is an affine-mixture representation barrier, not intrinsic sampling hardness.

Interface: Target distribution π on F_2^m; proposal Q is a mixture of at most K uniform distributions on affine subspaces. The lower bound concerns pointwise domination π≤ρQ, the condition used for rejection sampling. The affine-cover inequality applies to the separately stated uniform-rank-cover construction.

Proof spine: For an affine subspace of dimension at most D, its target mass is bounded by (2/3)^(m−D). For higher-dimensional pieces, information-set coordinates are unbiased under their uniform law, which bounds their mass on the low-Hamming-weight tail by a Bin(D+1,1/2) probability. Remove the union of low-dimensional components from {wt≤t}, compare remaining target mass to proposal mass, and derive the displayed ratio.

Costs: No sampler cost lower bound follows: π is sampled exactly with m independent Bernoulli(1/3) bits. The source supplies an exact finite formula and reports enumeration of every affine subspace through m=6 plus exact rational examples at m=100,250,500; intake did not rerun that checker.
Failure: Applies only to mixtures of uniform affine subspace laws under pointwise domination and to the specified envelope construction. It does not rule out multiplicative factorizations, product sampling, dual-kernel sampling, or other compact representations; the example is deliberately easy to sample.
Closest comparator: The source distinguishes product sampling, affine stratification and weighted/code-like models. It makes no claim that these models or exact sampling are novel; the result is a scoped obstruction to this proposal representation.
Open verification: Reconstruct the low/high dimensional mass bounds and the finite domination formula, verify constants and rounding in the m divisible by eight corollary, and preserve the product-sampler escape when interpreting the asymptotic rejection lower bound.

card_roles.text: Claim: For every integer d≥2, the source constructs two matrices A_1,A_2 over F_2 with 2d+1 input coordinates and d columns such that rank(A_1)=rank(A_2)=rank(A_1+A_2)=d. At x_0=e_0 the 2×d matrix F(x_0) has rank 1; changing any one binary coordinate yields rank at most 1 (the e_0 flip yields zero), while the two-coordinate move x=e_0+e_1+e_2 yields rank 2. Thus a single-coordinate rank-ascent rule can stall despite minimum nonzero-combination rank d. The source reports exact script checks for d=2,3,5,8.

Interface: Finite field F_2; a two-output linear matrix map F:F_2^(2d+1)→F_2^(2×d), for each d≥2. The obstruction is only to procedures whose next move changes one input coordinate at a time while seeking a larger rank.

Proof spine: Use the explicit coordinate generators F(e_0)=E, F(e_j)=E+e_2e_jᵀ, and F(eʹ_j)=E+(e_1+e_2)e_jᵀ, with E=e_1e_1ᵀ, j=1,…,d. Direct row inspection gives rank d for each nonzero A-combination; evaluating at e_0 and each Hamming-neighbor gives rank at most one, whereas the displayed two-coordinate move has rank two.

Costs: The witness dimension is 2d+1 by d with two constraint matrices; the source includes exact finite checks for d=2,3,5,8. No algorithm benchmark or asymptotic runtime comparison is supplied.
Failure: This falsifies only single-coordinate rank-ascent for the stated family. A two-coordinate escape is explicit. It is not a lower bound against multi-coordinate or global algorithms, a hardness result, or a failure of dual-kernel sampling.

card_roles.text: Claim: For the single-mode thermal attenuator Phi_{eta,nu}, 0<eta<1 and nu>0, set G=1+(1-eta)nu and assume eta>G-1. Let R=(eta-(G-1))/(G-1)>0. For a normalized pure seed psi=sum_{j>=0} psi_j|j> satisfying sum_{j>=0}(j+1)R^j|psi_j|^2<infinity, the source constructs a nonzero normalizable vector g_* in the kernel of the full two-mode Stinespring-environment coefficient map. For every fixed distinct normalized pure finite-energy competitor phi, define q_phi=||T_phi g_*||^2/||g_*||^2>0, with T_phi the coefficient map for its complementary output. Then rho_p=(1-p)|psi><psi|+p|phi><phi| obeys limsup_{p down to 0} I_c(rho_p,Phi_{eta,nu})/[p log(1/p)] <= -q_phi < 0 (natural logarithms), hence has negative coherent information for all sufficiently small p. The source reports this sign without a finite receiver-relative-entropy assumption.

Interface: One use of a single-mode thermal attenuator with the full complementary output, including the thermal-environment purifier. The seed is pure, finite-energy and obeys the stated exponential-moment condition; the competitor is a fixed, distinct pure finite-energy state. The mixture weight tends to zero while both states remain fixed. This does not cover competitors depending on p or general entangled block-code inputs.

Proof spine: An explicit entangled Bargmann multiplier gives a normalizable vector in the seed complement kernel; its norm is an exact weighted photon-moment expression. Contracting the same vector with a competitor produces a Wronskian f h′-f′ h, nonzero exactly when the pure states differ, so an environmental measurement leaks probability q_phi>0 only under the rare component. A binary-label conditional-entropy continuity argument gives the asymptotic negative p log(1/p) term without a finite receiver-relative-entropy assumption.

Costs: No algorithmic or physical acquisition cost is claimed. The restriction is a weighted exponential photon-number moment depending on eta and nu; the sign conclusion is for each fixed seed/competitor pair and all sufficiently small mixture weights, with no uniform threshold in p supplied.
Failure: This excludes only the stated rare binary mixtures around seeds satisfying the moment condition. Sufficiently heavy tails outside the condition, varying seed/competitor limits, faithful complementary outputs outside this class, and general collective codes remain unresolved. It does not prove zero capacity or rule out a positive rate from another family.
Closest comparator: This is a single-letter rare-mixture obstruction for the thermal attenuator. It does not alter the cited primary paper reported positive witness at eta=0.7841 or establish the capacity threshold. The proof and diagnostics are source-reported internal work, not external validation.
Open verification: Independently reconstruct the normalizable Bargmann kernel and exact norm criterion, verify the Wronskian leakage and binary-label continuity argument with the full complementary channel, then map precisely which seed tails and mixture limits remain outside the result.

card_roles.text: Claim: For m uses of the single-mode thermal attenuator Phi_{eta,1}, any deterministic qubit encoder/decoder with total mean input photon number E obeys F_e <= 3/4 + |arccos(sqrt(eta))-pi/6| sqrt(3E+m). If E<=10m, eta=0.751 and target entanglement fidelity F_e>=0.99, the source reports the necessary lower bound m>=1392 channel uses. More generally, for E<=mN and F_e>=1-epsilon with epsilon<1/4, m >= (1/4-epsilon)^2/(|arccos(sqrt(eta))-pi/6|^2(3N+1)).

Interface: The channel is the memoryless thermal attenuator with bath mean photon number nu=1. The result applies to arbitrary deterministic qubit codes over m channel uses, with total average input energy E and entanglement fidelity F_e; it does not assume a maximum photon cutoff or a specific code family. The 1392 example additionally assumes average energy at most 10 photons per use and target fidelity 0.99.

Proof spine: At eta0=3/4 the channel is antidegradable, giving the qubit symmetric-extension fidelity ceiling 3/4 for every deterministic code. An angle-continuity estimate for the Stinespring beam-splitter dilation bounds the change in decoded entanglement fidelity by |theta-pi/6| sqrt(3E+m), yielding the displayed inequality and the necessary blocklength bound.

Costs: The resource variables are channel uses m and total mean input photons E; no decoder runtime, preparation procedure, maximum per-use energy, or sufficient construction is provided. The numerical threshold 1392 is a source-reported evaluation of the exact necessary bound.
Failure: This is not a quantum-capacity converse: it permits reliability with growing blocklength/energy and does not rule out positive coherent information or positive asymptotic capacity above eta=3/4. It applies to the stated deterministic qubit entanglement-fidelity task at nu=1, not arbitrary fidelity thresholds or assisted capacities.
Closest comparator: The primary source reports a positive finite-energy coherent-information witness at eta=0.7841 and antidegradability through eta=0.75; the exact threshold remains open. This finite-block resource lower bound does not extend that capacity bracket.
Open verification: Independently reconstruct the antidegradable symmetric-extension bound and angle-continuity estimate for arbitrary deterministic encoders/decoders; audit the energy convention and reproduce the 1392 rounding from the exact formula without treating it as a capacity converse.

card_roles.text: Claim: Let Lambda_0 be a full-rank symplectically self-dual k-mode lattice of volume (2pi)^k and chi:Lambda_0->Z_2 a nontrivial homomorphism. Choose t with exp(i t^T Omega lambda)=(-1)^chi(lambda), so 2t belongs to Lambda_0. The index-two lattice Lambda_n={(lambda_1,...,lambda_n) in Lambda_0^n: sum_j chi(lambda_j)=0 mod 2} is a valid commuting lattice encoding one qubit. For additive Gaussian noise with density f_v=N(0,v I_{2k}) per block and a fundamental cell C_0, define g_lat(s)=sum_{lambda in Lambda_0} f_v(s+lambda), f_chi(s)=sum_{lambda in Lambda_0}(-1)^chi(lambda)f_v(s+lambda), r(s)=f_chi(s)/g_lat(s), and g_t(s)=g_lat(s+t). Set rho(v)=integral_{C_0} f_chi(s)^2/g_lat(s) ds and beta(v)=integral_{C_0} sqrt(g_lat(s)g_t(s)) ds. For a uniform bit T with conditional iid syndrome densities g_lat or g_t, let H_shift(n)=H(T|Y_1,...,Y_n); let H_parity(n)=E_{S_j iid g_lat} h_2((1+product_j r(S_j))/2), with binary entropy in bits. The source-defined ideal analog stabilizer decoder obeys I_c(n)=1-H_parity(n)-H_shift(n) and I_c(n)>=rho(v)^n/(2 ln 2)-beta(v)^n, so rho(v)>beta(v) is sufficient for positive ideal coherent information at finite n. At bath occupation nu=1, sender preamplification maps v=2(1-eta); however, no lattice meeting the condition near v=1/2 is supplied.

Interface: The result concerns an ideal infinite-energy lattice-code family and analog syndrome decoding for a Gaussian additive-noise channel. The transfer to the thermal attenuator uses sender preamplification with v=2(1-eta) at nu=1. A physical finite-energy code additionally requires a charged envelope, Gram orthonormalization, syndrome instrument, finite precision and cutoff-error bound; these are not established by the integral criterion.

Proof spine: A nontrivial character of the self-dual base lattice defines a half-shift t. The parity-kernel sublattice has index two and its dual yields four logical cosets, giving a pure ideal qubit repetition family. Decomposing the decoded logical error into shift and parity bits gives I_c=1-H_parity-H_shift exactly. The binary entropy series lower-bounds 1-H_parity by rho^n/(2 ln 2), while a Bhattacharyya bound gives H_shift<=beta^n.

Costs: A block of n repetitions over a k-mode base uses kn physical modes per logical qubit. For the stated additive-channel simulation the source counts a sender preamplifier and a thermal-channel use per physical mode. No finite-energy preparation, decoder precision, outer coding or runtime bound is included.
Failure: The sufficient gate rho(v)>beta(v) is not met by the reported square, rectangular and tested hexagonal lattice seeds near v=1/2; the reported image-sum values are floating-point diagnostics, not a certified global search. No actual thermal-attenuator positive coherent-information witness near eta=0.75, finite-energy transfer, or complete decoder is proved. Failure of these examples is not impossibility for other lattices or codes.
Closest comparator: This is an ideal conditional construction route, distinct from the published finite-Fock positive witness at eta=0.7841. It neither improves the checked capacity frontier nor establishes an operational or physical code. The exact threshold remains UNKNOWN.
Open verification: Reconstruct the exact syndrome identity and entropy bounds; then find a rigorously certified self-dual lattice with rho(v)>beta(v) for v<1/2, or delimit the gate, and separately establish a finite-energy encoder/decoder transfer for the actual thermal channel.

card_roles.text: Claim: Let g(x)=(x+1)ln(x+1)-x ln x and N(X|R)=g^{-1}(S(X|R)) when the conditional entropy is nonnegative. Prepare R,A by a two-mode squeeze of parameter 1/4 applied to tau_{1/2} tensor tau_{1/2}; take an independent vacuum B and apply a one-mode quantum-limited amplifier of gain G=6/5 to A,B. The source reports outward interval bounds N(A|R)>0.3895 and N(C|R)<0.6607, whereas the proposed conditional extension would require N(C|R)>=(6/5)N(A|R)+1/5>0.6674. Both conditional entropies are positive. Thus this finite-energy product-with-vacuum example refutes that reference-conditioned strengthening. The A and B input marginals remain independent and the unconditioned candidate inequality is saturated by the thermal marginals.

Interface: One mode in each amplifier port; ancillary input B is vacuum and independent of the reference-correlated A. The reference R is correlated with A by a two-mode squeezed thermal state. Vacuum covariance is 1/2 and entropies use natural logarithms. Only the proposed replacement S(X)->S(X|R) followed by g^{-1} is refuted; the independent-input unconditional theorem has no shared-reference premise.

Proof spine: The RA covariance has blocks aI,aI,cZ with a=cosh(1/2), c=sinh(1/2). Under gain 6/5, the output covariance blocks determine two symplectic eigenvalues. The source encloses S(A|R) and S(C|R) with outward intervals, then uses monotonicity of g to establish inverse bounds separated by more than 0.0067. The retained receipt reports an interval check; intake did not run the supplied mpmath code.

Costs: No algorithm or acquisition cost is claimed. The certificate is for one fixed two-mode Gaussian input family and one amplifier gain; finite-energy preparation is a mathematical input specification, not a demonstrated physical experiment.
Failure: This counterexample invalidates only the proposed reference-conditioned amplifier photon-number inequality. It does not contradict the unconditioned independent-input amplifier candidate N557, which is saturated here at the marginals; nor does it refute the weaker conditional entropy power inequality. It gives no thermal-channel capacity bound.
Closest comparator: The source identifies the established conditional entropy power inequality as compatible with these data and of a different, weaker exponential-entropy form. Existing N15 concerns a different reference-conditioned beam-splitter photon-entropy counterexample; it is related context, not the same theorem or witness.
Open verification: Independently reconstruct the Gaussian covariance and symplectic-spectrum formulas, check the outward interval enclosure and inverse-g bounds from the retained source code, and preserve the distinction from N557 and from the weaker conditional entropy power inequality.

card_roles.text: Claim: Let {D_n}_{n>=1} be finite-valued nonnegative functionals on strictly positive finite probability simplices, normalized by D_n(q,q)=0. Assume data processing under rectangular stochastic maps whose input and output distributions have full support, and for each fixed q assume continuity in p on the open simplex and C^2 regularity away from p=q. The source states that universal convexity of t↦D_n(p exp(tL),q) for every finite alphabet, full-support p,q and irreducible q-reversible continuous-time Markov generator L is equivalent to one alphabet-independent Ψ in C([0,infinity))∩C^2((0,infinity)) with D_n(p,q)=Ψ(χ²(p||q)), Ψ(0)=0, Ψ'(s)>=0 and Ψ'(s)+sΨ''(s)>=0. No tensor-additivity or trace-form premise is needed. As separate corollaries, tensor additivity forces D_n=c log(1+χ²), c>=0 (the order-two Rényi divergence); within that additive class, requiring D'''(t)<=0 along every finite reversible relaxation forces D=0. Under the same data-processing and regularity assumptions, convexity along every irreducible finite stationary generator, including nonreversible ones, forces D=0 without tensor additivity.

Interface: Finite alphabets, full-support row distributions p,q and rectangular stochastic maps with full-support outputs. A generator has nonnegative off-diagonal entries, zero row sums and acts by p_t=p exp(tL); q is stationary, and q_i L_ij=q_j L_ji in the reversible theorem. For each fixed q, regularity is in p only: continuity on the open simplex and C^2 away from p=q. The source does not assume differentiability at equality or regularity in q. Here n indexes alphabet size; the additive conclusion is named “order-two Rényi divergence” and is not denoted D_2.

Proof spine: Sections 2–3 derive exact refinement invariance, transverse Hessian scaling and a rare-clone curvature identity; taking the clone mass to zero forces gradient chord slopes to agree. Section 4 makes the gradient affine in likelihood ratio and establishes global constancy on chi-square level sets, including rational and irrational references. Section 5 identifies exactly the scalar convexity conditions. Section 6 solves the tensor-additive functional equation and the third-derivative obstruction. Section 7 uses nonreversible cycle generators to force the zero functional.

Costs: No algorithmic or physical runtime claim. The source reports exact computations supporting the curvature witness and scalar examples; the cited checker was not supplied and was not rerun at intake.
Failure: The main classification is finite-state and depends on data processing plus the stated p-regularity. It does not classify arbitrary divergences without these assumptions. Section 8 of the attached note separately states a regularity-free additive result on bounded Polish-space experiments, but points to a companion proof file not supplied or located; this ancillary statement is not included in the registered theorem. External correctness and historical priority remain UNKNOWN.
Closest comparator: The main result gives a broader scalar Ψ family than its tensor-additive logarithmic member. N588 is a separate complete-monotonicity classification: its positive entire-series profiles fit the scalar conditions here, but its local smoothness and independent-augmentation assumptions differ, and it derives rather than assumes data processing. This relation is only a scoped comparison, not a proof dependency.
Open verification: Independently reconstruct the refinement/Hessian scaling and rare-clone limit, then audit the global level-set/reference argument, scalar sufficiency, additive functional equation and nonreversible cycle step with every assumption retained. Keep the missing Section 8 companion proof and the unsupplied Section 9 checker outside the established theorem.

card_roles.text: Claim: For every finite alphabet, let D_n be finite-valued and nonnegative on strictly positive probability distributions, with D_n(q,q)=0. Assume continuity in p throughout each open simplex, C-infinity regularity near each full-support q, and invariance under independent uninformative augmentation in both tensor orders: D_nm(p⊗r,q⊗r)=D_n(p,q) and D_mn(r⊗p,r⊗q)=D_n(p,q), without presuming relabeling invariance or full tensor additivity. If for every full-support p,q and every irreducible q-reversible continuous-time Markov generator L, t↦D_n(p exp(tL),q) is completely monotone for t>0, then and only then there is one alphabet- and q-independent power series Ψ(z)=Σ_{k>=1} a_k z^k, a_k>=0, with infinite radius of convergence, such that D_n(p,q)=Ψ(χ²(p||q)). Data processing follows from the classification and is not a premise. For s=χ²(p||q)>0 and every integer N>=1, the source gives D_{n^N}(p^⊗N,q^⊗N)>=((1+s)^N-1)/s · D_n(p,q), sharply attained by D=cχ². Thus no nonzero tensor-additive member, or member growing only O(N) under independent replication, lies in the class.

Interface: Finite-state distributions only. Each fixed q has continuity throughout the open simplex and C-infinity regularity in a neighborhood of q; no analyticity, nondegenerate Hessian or differentiability in q is assumed. Independent augmentation identities are explicitly required in both tensor orders; full tensor additivity is not assumed. Complete monotonicity means (-1)^k d^k/dt^k D_n(p exp(tL),q)>=0 for every integer k>=0 and t>0, for every irreducible q-reversible generator. The result does not cover nonreversible generators or a no-smoothness setting.

Proof spine: The proof represents each relaxation as a positive Laplace transform, then uses asymptotic spectral extraction and valid near-reset reversible generators to realize arbitrary q-orthonormal eigenbases. Positivity forces each smooth Taylor jet to be radial. A positive-measure argument recovers the global function without assuming analyticity. Independent augmentation identifies one alphabet-independent series and forces nonnegative coefficients; conversely, each monomial chi-square power is completely monotone along reversible relaxation, and the stated data processing and replication consequences follow.

Costs: No algorithmic, physical or runtime improvement is claimed. The source contains one illustrative exact third-derivative example, but its symbolic-check script was not supplied or rerun. No benchmark or empirical dynamics are involved.
Failure: Scope is finite-state and reversible, with C-infinity regularity near equilibrium and independent uninformative augmentation. It does not classify nonsmooth functionals, nonreversible relaxation, empirical or quantum dynamics, or Polish-space divergences. The exact example calculation is source-reported only; no formal proof-assistant verification or external correctness review is supplied.
Closest comparator: Compared with N587, this is a narrower profile class (nonnegative entire power series) with stronger complete-monotonicity and augmentation hypotheses; it does not assume data processing. card_roles.text: Claim: For simple random walk P=A/d on the infinite d-regular tree, d>=3, the Chebyshev polynomial T_k(P) has signed endpoint mass satisfying sum_y |T_k(P)(x,y)| >= [2(d-1)/d]^(k-1), for k>=1. The same witness applies in a finite d-regular graph when the radius-k neighborhood of x is a tree. Consequently any single signed-particle estimator W delta_Y with E[W 1{Y=y}]=T_k(P)(x,y) has E|W| at least this large and E[W^2] at least its square. This is a source-reported exact obstruction to the proposed signed-particle representation.

Interface: Classical simple random walk on a d-regular tree, Chebyshev first-kind polynomial, and an unbiased one-particle signed representation of the polynomial endpoint measure. The result concerns this estimator form and this local tree witness, not arbitrary access to a finite transition matrix or global algorithms.

Proof spine: At distance k, lower powers vanish and P^k(x,y)=d^-k. The leading coefficient of T_k is 2^(k-1), and there are d(d-1)^(k-1) vertices at distance k. Summing the absolute mass over that sphere gives the exponential lower bound. Unbiasedness forces E|W| to dominate the l1 norm, and Jensen gives E[W^2]>=(E|W|)^2.

Costs: For d>=3 the base 2(d-1)/d exceeds one, so the l1 mass and second-moment requirement grow exponentially with k for this representation. A positive universal-cover/nonbacktracking representation is also given, but its expected reduced path length remains linear in t for d>=3; the d=2 diffusive case is standard.
Failure: This is not a general classical fast-forwarding lower bound, a lower bound for all signed decompositions using multiple particles, or an obstruction to explicit global-state access. The separate bounded-radius locality observation applies only to local-output procedures. The broader proposed capability was stopped at this mechanism gate.
Closest comparator: The source credits established Chebyshev/nonbacktracking representations, including Apers–Sarlette quantum fast-forwarding, Alon–Benjamini–Lubetzky–Sodin nonbacktracking walks, and Biswas–Pyne–Rubinfeld local random-walk access. These works use distinct access models; the present obstruction does not subsume them.
Open verification: Test a different positive or global-access mechanism against this signed-mass obstruction without inferring a general no-fast-forwarding theorem from it.
