card_roles.text: Claim: For a finite-dimensional system xdot=-Kx-diag(alpha)x^{circ3}+e_1 u, y=x_1, x(0)=0, with real symmetric positive-definite K and unknown positive alpha_i, let W be the smallest linear subspace containing e_1, K-invariant, and closed under T(v,w,z)=alpha componentwise-multiplied by v,w,z. Under the source’s exact zero-initial ordered-pulse endpoint-germ interface, known physical dimension N is globally identifiable up to hidden signed permutations fixing e_1 if and only if W=R^N. If W is proper, changing K by a positive perturbation on W-perp can preserve all input-output responses. Without a supplied N, the complete exact input-output germ determines a unique minimum-dimensional realization within the same positive heterogeneous cubic class, of dimension dim W. The source also parameterizes all larger equivalent realizations by weighted signed coordinate blocks, inactive coordinates, and arbitrary positive-definite dynamics on the orthogonal complement. These are source-reported internal theorem candidates.

Interface: The port, input/output scales, zero initial state, exact cubic constitutive law, symmetric SPD K, and positive nodewise cubic coefficients are part of the model. Observations are exact endpoint germs of ordered positive-duration pulses with amplitudes 0 and 1; exact mixed derivatives/IO word coefficients and exact Hankel/Gram rank decisions are assumed. The full-model result is modulo hidden signed permutations fixing e_1. The all-dimension minimality theorem is only within finite-dimensional symmetric-SPD positive-heterogeneous-cubic models.

Proof spine: Directional cubic derivatives yield positive atomic moment sequences whose support projections identify active coordinates without observing hidden states. Lie-bracket/observable identities construct K action and weighted triple products on paired directions; exact Gram closure recovers W and proves necessity/sufficiency. After rescaling by diag(sqrt(alpha_i)), every ternary-closed subspace is a span of disjoint signed block indicators. The quotient coefficient is alphabar_B=(sum_{i in B} 1/alpha_i)^-1, and K restricts to the canonical quotient while an arbitrary SPD operator remains on W-perp.

Costs: The source gives finite exact word-jet and adaptive positive-Hankel/Gram certificates, including when N is not supplied, but exact real derivatives, rank/equality tests and root decisions are ideal information. Conservative jet-depth bounds grow rapidly; no stable finite-noise estimator or useful physical acquisition cost follows. In general physical dimension and residual hidden dynamics are not identifiable.
Failure: A proper W leaves K on W-perp invisible; all equivalent realizations can differ in inactive coordinates, block refinements and residual SPD dynamics. Exact flatness and zero Gram residuals are not statistical tests. The source’s focused internal audit found no blocking algebraic gap under its exact class, but this intake did not reconstruct the proof; external correctness, formal verification and priority remain UNKNOWN.
Closest comparator: Nonlinear input-output identifiability, Volterra methods and signed-permutation gauges have established predecessors, including Albertini–Sontag (1993) and Vanelli–Hendrickx, arXiv:2412.08472v4. The source distinguishes known-topology or local identifiability from its exact dense/sparse one-port closure criterion and cross-dimensional minimal quotient; this is not priority clearance.
Open verification: Independently reconstruct the positive-moment support recovery, paired K/T closure, cross-dimensional stopping certificate, and exhaustive weighted signed-block classification. Keep exact-word-germ identifiability distinct from finite-noise or physically acquired recovery, then assess the cited nonlinear-identification prior art.

card_roles.text: Claim: Assume the exact model and input-output germ of N594. If every physical node has the same unknown alpha>0, K is symmetric positive definite with K_ij<=0 for i!=j, and its off-diagonal graph is connected, then each active synchrony block B has reduced cubic coefficient alphabar_B=alpha/|B|, no physical coordinates are inactive, and |B|=alpha/alphabar_B is an integer. card_roles.text: Claim: The unrestricted target remains H(fhat^2)<=C I(f) for real Boolean f:{-1,1}^n->{-1,1}. The report gives the actual coordinate-restriction entropy increment Delta_i(f) in terms of the paired coefficients A_T=fhat(T), B_T=fhat(T union {i}), and observes that a dimension-free essential-coordinate bound Delta_i(f)<=C I_i(f) would close the usual induction; it explicitly does not prove such a bound. card_roles.text: Claim: For four independent two-state continuous-time Markov chains with stationary product initial law, dyadic target probabilities p=(1/8,1/16,1/32,1/16), relaxation rates (1,2,4,8), and one joint target, the source provides a Python-standard-library implementation that returns a nonnegative rational approximation to the stationary first-hitting time using integer and exact-rational arithmetic. Under its stated independent-unbiased-input-bits assumption, the source certificate gives the requested instance epsilon=1/4, delta=1/20 and conservative failure bound 59429/5242880 < 0.011336. For a deterministic recorded tape, the source reports an exact rational same-tape enclosure with relative discrepancy upper bound 0.001652145 for every extension of its accepted finite uniform cells. A separate q=2^-200 fixture reports all four strata compressed using 29,401 exponential cells; one OS-backed acquisition and its exact prefix replay are also recorded. The packet reports 17 passing implementation tests and an internal code-and-mathematics audit. This is an implementation supplement to N592, not a second general theorem.

Interface: The implementation gate accepts dyadic target probabilities strictly between zero and one, positive rational relaxation rates, rational epsilon and delta, and an independent stationary product initial law for one joint target. Component i has target-to-other rate (1-p_i)lambda_i and other-to-target rate p_i lambda_i. The moderate replay uses exactly n=4, p=(1/8,1/16,1/32,1/16), lambda=(1,2,4,8), q=1/65536, epsilon=1/4 and delta=1/20. The theorem-level rational-input contract remains the broader source-reported N592 construction. Randomized guarantees assume independent unbiased bit streams; the recorded SHA256 fixtures are deterministic, and the single OS entropy acquisition does not certify physical independence.

Proof spine: The implementation preserves the maximum-activated-rate strata and Brown/Cox representation used by N592. It encloses finite dyadic-cell exponential values by rational intervals using an atanh-series logarithm, makes branch decisions with explicit slack, samples small-stratum counts through bounded exponential-arrival cells, and compresses large strata with a fixed sample mean. The certificate separately accounts for cell rejection, branch ambiguity, count caps, large-stratum concentration, finite arithmetic and output error. The code and certificate are source-provided; intake did not independently reconstruct them.

Costs: For the specified moderate preflight, the source bounds expected exponential calls by 142,884. A deterministic SHA fixture records 15,849 exponential cells and 1,619,385 input bits; the same-tape reference uses 55,468 marks. The q=2^-200 fixture records 29,401 cells and 5,313,694 bits (about 0.91 seconds on the source environment). The single OS-backed acquisition records 14,769 cells and 1,514,177 bits. These are source-reported bounds and finite measurements, not uniform wall-clock guarantees or a statistical accuracy study.

The exact same-tape discrepancy is specific to the recorded finite-cell extension and is not a relative rare-tail or statistical failure-rate guarantee. The source presents its proposed distinction as a finite-bit rarity/rate-uniform guarantee and a concrete exact-arithmetic realization; this intake does not establish priority or a historic-scale capability.

card_roles.text: Claim: Use the source convention ||X||_{2,n}^2=Tr(X*X)/n even on a corner of C^n. For an orthogonal projection P, Q=I-P, U in U(n), A=QUQ restricted to Q C^n, and T=QU*PUQ restricted to Q C^n, the report gives inf_{V in U(Q C^n)} ||A-V||_{2,n}^2 = Tr((I_Q-sqrt(I_Q-T))^2)/n, between Tr(T^2)/(4n) and Tr(T^2)/n. With B=PUQ, T=B*B, so the cost is controlled by Tr((B*B)^2)/n, not rank alone. It also gives, for every integer q>=2, n=q^4 and a swap of two q^2-dimensional spaces for which an error of normalized size epsilon=q^-2 is killed by deleting an epsilon fraction, while the compressed unitary needs repair distance q^-1=sqrt(epsilon).

The scalar bound t/2<=1-sqrt(1-t)<=t gives the two trace bounds. In the example, QUQ has q^2 zero singular values and the rest equal to one.

Costs: No computational, acquisition, or runtime claim is supplied; this is an exact finite-matrix argument as reported by the source.

card_roles.text: Claim: The source states an exact sampler for the joint stationary law of any fixed finite batch of raw coordinates at specified times in a finite-depth, finite-field network whose same-level update is affine, whose deterministic forcing depends only on strictly lower levels, whose parent count is at most k, and whose site-time category has Haar-reset probability s>0. If m coordinates are requested, c is the fixed depth, h=kc^2, and Q is the number of distinct update categories exposed, its bound is E[Q] <= (m/s) sum_{j=0}^{c-1}(1+h/s)^j. The category oracle is shared across levels so reset/gate correlations are preserved. The source also gives an exponential backward-depth tail for fixed c,m,k,s. These are source-reported theorem claims, not independently reconstructed here.

Interface: States lie in F_q^c. At a site-time one shared category chooses independent uniform Haar values for all coordinates with probability s, a locally known residual reset with probability r, or a gate with probability 1-s-r. At level ell the gate is linear in level-ell parents plus a deterministic function of strictly lower-level inputs; same-level nonlinear feedback is excluded. Parent acquisition, forcing descriptions and their evaluation are charged. Rational s,r support ideal exact random-bit draws; the reference implementation covers prime q, while the note states a mathematical finite-field generalization.

Proof spine: Process same-level dependencies in descending time while tracking coefficient vectors and the span V generated by independent Haar contributions. If a coefficient lies in V, an independent uniform vector U_V absorbs any unknown contribution in V in distribution (U_V+vZ has law U_V); this is distributional masking, not pathwise coalescence. Otherwise expose the category, propagate affine coefficients, retain lower-layer forcing terms without expanding them, and recurse on lower levels using the same memoized category field. A layer induction yields exact joint laws; negative-binomial domination gives the displayed expected-query bound.

Costs: At most cQ site-layer visits and kcQ parent incidences are reported. For fixed c the source states expected arithmetic/bit cost polynomial in m,k,1/s,log q and the acquired forcing-description/evaluation costs; its exponent and constants may grow sharply with c. The source reports a failed costly million-site run at k=5,s=.09 and a completed source-reported run at k=3,s=.20. These demonstrations were not rerun by intake.
Failure: No same-level nonlinear feedback, unbounded parent access, arbitrary nonlinear cellular automaton, full-state efficient sampling, or general full-chain O(log N) mixing theorem is established. Fixed-depth is essential to the recursive bound; low reset probability and larger depth can be practically prohibitive. Exactness assumes ideal independent randomness and does not follow from the source's pseudorandom statistical checks.
Closest comparator: The source cites coupling from the past, perfect sampling for probabilistic cellular automata, algebraic decomposition of nonlinear cellular automata, and noisy-CA ergodicity results as overlapping prior art. The exact novelty of this rank-absorbing layered construction is explicitly unverified; citations were not independently checked.
Open verification: Independently reconstruct the adaptive memoized-category and cross-level conditional-independence arguments, verify the negative-binomial and exponential-tail bounds including forcing acquisition costs, and perform a full prior-art review before treating this as a theorem or novelty claim.

card_roles.text: Claim: As a corollary of the stratified sampler, the source claims that a countable network with uniformly bounded parent incidence and the same finite-depth, strictly lower-level nonlinear forcing has a unique stationary probability measure on (F_q^c)^Lambda. Every finite-dimensional local marginal converges to stationarity uniformly over the initial configuration, with a source-stated exponential-in-time bound C exp(-gamma T); a finite list of stationary coordinates is sampleable with finite expected local oracle work. Constants may depend on the fixed observable batch and model parameters.

Interface: This is a local/fixed-observable result for countable sites, finite state alphabet, positive Haar-reset probability, uniformly bounded indegree and fixed finite level count. For multiple requested observation times, their prescribed separation must be accounted for separately; the simple terminal-time local mixing bound is not a global joint mixing guarantee.

Proof spine: Compactness of the countable product and the Feller property yield existence. The finite-depth rank/masking certificate closes before a random ancestry horizon with exponential tail and makes a target cylinder's law independent of all initial values on that event. The remaining total-variation discrepancy is bounded by the tail event; hence invariant measures agree on every finite cylinder and are equal.

Costs: The source reuses the fixed-batch oracle-work bound in N610. It gives no efficient algorithm for the entire infinite configuration and no system-size-independent cost for arbitrary global observables.
Failure: Uniqueness and convergence are restricted to the stratified model. The source explicitly distinguishes this from general positive-noise nonlinear cellular automata, where counterexamples to universal uniqueness are known. It does not imply O(log N) convergence of the full q^(Nc)-state finite network in total variation.

card_roles.text: Claim: Under the report's fixed-observer-plane and constant-shear model, w_x=v_x-beta z and w_y=v_y, the source derives d/dt[g(y)L+beta z H(y)]=-W_g+g(y)tau, with L=xv_y-yv_x, tau=dot L, G'=g and H=yg-G. For a stationary ensemble with integrable terms and no boundary contribution, E[W_g]=E[g tau], so a central acceleration predicts zero. A directional choice g=-e_x e_y |y| gives the stated observable. The report also constructs an exactly Newtonian circular-orbit selection rule s(phi)=(1+epsilon sin(2phi))/2 whose selected mean is 2epsilon/(3pi), equal to 0.02122066 at epsilon=.1 despite zero physical torque.

Interface: The cancellation is exact only for the stated shear observation model, fixed beta and stationary unselected ensemble. The report's application to actual astrometry is not an instrument-level theorem; finite-angle geometry, time-varying observer geometry, systemic-motion estimates, sample selection, ordinary Galactic tides, encounters and companions require control.

Proof spine: Differentiate g(y)L and beta z H(y); use xw_y-yw_x=L+beta yz and H'=yg' to cancel the unknown-depth term. Integrate the derivative over a stationary ensemble. For the counterexample, weight uniform phase on a Newtonian circular orbit by the stated inclusion probability and integrate explicitly.

Costs: The source reports calculations on a public 36-pair archive and primary numerical tables for 32 HARPS pairs, with eight overlaps and 60 distinct pairs overall; a 33-pair clean-sample intersection was used. Reported means have descriptive standard errors only and cohorts are heterogeneous. No selection-calibrated likelihood or decisive torque evidence was obtained; intake did not reacquire inputs or recalculate these values.
Failure: The selection counterexample proves that a nonzero statistic need not identify a noncentral force. The observed statistics do not establish or exclude the external-field mechanism, and source data are not a homogeneous, selection-calibrated sample. The identity eliminates a leading hidden-depth term only under its observation assumptions.
Closest comparator: The source identifies angular-momentum conservation, projected-angular-momentum methods and external-field anisotropy as prior context. Those literature comparisons were not independently checked; no new force or historical priority is claimed.
Open verification: Reconstruct the identity and its observation model, then acquire a selection-complete astrometric sample with covariance and multiplicity controls and separate the predicted torque from tides, encounters, companions and projection systematics.

card_roles.text: Claim: For the report's exact midpoint-geometry and fixed-adopted-distance observation model, r^2=R^2+z^2 and v(z)=w+zb. Minimizing eta(z)=sqrt(R^2+z^2)|w+zb|^2/(2 G_N M) over admissible depth reduces interior extrema to 3Bz^3+4dz^2+(V+2BR^2)z+2dR^2=0, where B=|b|^2, d=w dot b, V=|w|^2; evaluating real roots and endpoints gives the minimum. At the source's adopted central inputs, four pairs in its harmonized 33-pair cohort have eta_min>1 (IDs 3,33,42,59; range 1.1468–1.3994), so no choice of line-of-sight depth alone makes those fixed inputs a bound isolated Newtonian two-body pair.

Interface: The inequality is conditional on the adopted central astrometry, radial velocities, component masses, exact perspective reconstruction and isolated two-body Newtonian model. It is a feasibility envelope over unknown depth, not a probabilistic orbit fit or a gravity test.

Proof spine: Differentiate eta(z), factor the positive denominator, and reduce its interior critical points to the displayed cubic. Compare all real critical points in the physically admissible domain with its limiting endpoints. The source reports agreement of this cubic method and numerical minimization on 100 constructed cases; intake did not rerun that check.

Costs: The source reports four central-input violations in the harmonized archive/primary intersection; in the separate primary 32-pair table only HD189739/HD189760 (archive ID 59) violates the envelope, matching a pair already flagged in the primary study. Error propagation over measurement covariance, unresolved multiplicity and stellar-model uncertainty is not a calibrated confidence procedure.
Failure: A violation does not falsify Newtonian gravity: the pair can be unbound or perturbed, or masses, velocities or astrometry can be wrong; an unseen companion can alter the model. The result reproduces a known observational issue and is not a new anomaly.
Closest comparator: The source relates the calculation to published wide-binary data and an already identified problematic pair. Source citations were not independently checked; no gravity-law conclusion is claimed.
Open verification: Independently derive the perspective vectors and cubic, then propagate the actual astrometric/radial-velocity/mass covariance and multiplicity uncertainty before interpreting any pair-level infeasibility.

card_roles.text: Claim: For a closed glutamate pool with symmetric isotope-independent racemization, each isotope-class handedness imbalance m_j contracts by the same factor e^(-2K), and positivity implies 2K <= -ln(max(|e_14|,|e_15|)). The report converts the three published central values to e_14=0.0527903 and e_15=0.0175575, giving at most 4.24 handedness-halving times under this model. For a racemic background plus one L-biased source followed by isotope-independent racemization, the source's heavy-nitrogen fraction is q_excess=(q_L-d q_D)/(1-d), with d=D/L; the central measurements imply delta15N_excess about -590.5 per mil. A fit with a typical-range source remains compatible with individual quoted spreads after modest shifts, so the central-value inference is not a calibrated exclusion.

Interface: Mix isotope delta values only after conversion to heavy-atom fractions q=R/(1+R), R=R_AIR(1+delta/1000). The racemization inequality assumes a closed pool without later formation, exchange, selective destruction or protected compartments. The one-source invariant assumes the stated background/source mixture and isotope-independent racemization. The printed measurement uncertainties use different definitions and raw replicate covariance was unavailable.

Proof spine: Write n_j=L_j+D_j and m_j=L_j-D_j. The closed symmetric racemization equations conserve n_j and solve m_j(t)=m_j(0)e^(-2K); requiring |m_j(0)|<=n_j(0) yields the positivity bound. In the source mixture, isotope-heavy fractions mix linearly in q, and solving the L/D-weighted mass balance for the excess source gives q_excess.

Costs: The source reports a typical-source compatibility fit with D/L=0.8124, D delta15N=275.82 per mil, L delta15N=220.29 per mil and source delta15N=-20 per mil, each within one quoted spread under its separate definition. It also describes an illustrative D/L standard-error interpretation. No joint likelihood was reconstructed from raw scans.
Failure: The -590.5 per mil source value is model-dependent and unstable as D/L approaches one; the uncertainty fit prevents treating it as a required exotic reservoir. The closed-pool racemization bound is not an age estimate and does not apply to open histories. This does not establish contamination, overturn the source paper, or identify a chemical history.
Closest comparator: The source notes precedents for static isotope-of-excess calculations and preserves published measurement controls; those source comparisons were not independently checked. No novel chemical mechanism is claimed.
Open verification: Independently verify the isotope-probability conversion and mixture algebra, then obtain replicate-level isotope scans/covariances and test source histories under explicit open-pool and racemization assumptions.

card_roles.text: Claim: For the source's restricted zero-field model—an initially singlet electron pair, one nitrogen nucleus, isotropic H=a I dot S_1, and separate singlet/triplet product rates k_S,k_T—the reduced populated sector gives Y_S=k_S(k_T+w)/(k_S k_T+w(k_S+k_T)), with w=2v^2 A/(A^2+a^2/4), v=a sqrt(I(I+1))/2 and A=(k_S+k_T)/2. The source derives the exact model-specific bound Y_15/Y_14 <=14/9. Under its additional rule that singlet events return glutamate with randomized handedness while triplet events destroy it, matching the published central isotope/chirality values requires initial enantiomeric excess e_0>=0.3829; a source numerical best constant-parameter survival is about 2.46e-6. This restricted model does not generate chirality from an initially racemic pool.

Interface: The Hamiltonian, initial singlet state, single nuclear coupling, zero field, reaction rates, returned-molecule handedness rule and destruction channel are imposed assumptions. Other nuclear couplings, exchange, relaxation, additional reactions, open-system reservoirs and the actual Bennu reaction path are not specified by evidence.

Proof spine: Reduce by conserved total angular momentum to the stated 2x2 sector; integrate its density-matrix reaction equations to obtain Y_S; clear positive denominators to express the isotope ratio inequality as a nonnegative-coefficient polynomial. The report says full density-matrix calculations agreed in five parameter cases, but neither algebra nor numerics were rechecked during intake.

Costs: The source reports parameter-mixture searches over more than 31,000 yield settings and an approximate survival optimum; this was not a certified global optimization. The small survival figure depends on the assumed returned-molecule chirality rule and is not a universal impossibility bound.
Failure: An identified glutamate radical, measured isotope-dependent reaction kinetics, and measured return-versus-destruction probabilities are missing. Separate published abundance and bulk-nitrogen measurements concern different aliquots, so the source's inventory comparison is a warning under a restrictive model, not an empirical refutation. The calculation is not evidence the reaction occurs in Bennu.
Closest comparator: The source states that nuclear-spin-dependent radical-pair isotope effects have theoretical precedents. It does not claim new physics; its chemical mechanism is unestablished, and citations were not independently checked.
Open verification: Independently derive the reduced density-matrix yield and 14/9 inequality; then identify an actual glutamate radical pathway and measure the isotope-dependent rates and product-return/destruction outcomes under relevant conditions.

card_roles.text: Claim: For the two native backbone carbon indicators, let p=E(X_1+X_2)/2, c=P(X_1=X_2=1), r=P_1/(2P_0) and t=P_2/P_0. The source gives the exact inversion p=(r+t)/(1+2r+t), c=t/(1+2r+t); thus the singly substituted ratio alone does not identify mean heavy-carbon abundance. Under a source-mixture model where molecules form independently within reservoirs with heavy-carbon fraction P, c-p^2=Var(P). If every source lies in [a,b], Var(P)<=(p-a)(b-p), a sharp endpoint bound. The report's equal-marginal correlated benchmark predicts P_2/P_0 23.71 times its independent-backbone alternative for Bennu and 6.18 times for Murchison; these are conditional native-isotope predictions, not observed peaks. For the stated Bennu organic-material interval, the source reports a maximum covariance 134.28 times below its benchmark requirement, excluding that bounded source class under the chosen interface.

Interface: All probability equations refer to corrected native carbon probabilities. The source uses the displayed VPDB-ratio-to-probability interface, but applying that correction to this pair model is unverified. A derivatization reagent adds carbon, so native double-substitution ratios require the stated generating-polynomial deconvolution. Two 13C substitutions and one 18O substitution are separated by only 0.00246468 Da; calibrated line shapes, standards and integration are needed.

Proof spine: Express P0=1-2p+c, P1=2(p-c), P2=c and solve the ratio definitions for p,c. In a reservoir mixture c=E[P^2], p=E[P], so covariance equals Var(P); the pointwise inequality (P-a)(b-P)>=0 gives the sharp interval bound. Independent-position unequal marginals alone move r in the opposite direction. The source reports additional LP and generated-distribution checks, not replayed by intake.

Costs: The source reports Bennu and Murchison benchmark quantities and says the bounded Bennu source interval permits covariance at most 1.40165e-5 while the candidate needs 1.88210e-3. Raw isotope spectra were not acquired; fragment/reagent contributions and mass-line overlap prevent interpreting a nominal mass-plus-two count as the native carbon-pair signal.
Failure: The equal-marginal correlation distribution is one feasible construction, not a unique source history. The interval bound applies only to the cited organic-material source class, not every historical carbon-bearing phase; extreme reservoirs remain possible but unconnected to the amino acid. The central mechanism of mixing-induced isotope clumping is acknowledged as known prior art. No β-alanine origin or chirality mechanism is established.
Closest comparator: The source identifies prior work on mixing-induced doubly substituted species and apparent site-specific isotope effects. It explicitly demotes the general mechanism as prior art; the quantitative application and instrument caveats are source-reported, not a novelty claim.
Open verification: Acquire replicate-level raw mass spectra and calibration standards; verify native/reagent isotope deconvolution and line shapes; test the predicted doubly substituted abundance with a calibrated likelihood; only then compare bounded and extreme source histories.

card_roles.text: Claim: Let A be a complete synchronizing deterministic finite automaton on m>=2 states with at least two letters a,b. The source constructs B by adjoining m-1 proxy states p_i and retaining every original transition, with p_i a=q_i a and p_i b=q_{i+1}b; every further letter maps p_i into the original image Qc. Every nonempty word has exactly the same image from B as from A, so their nonempty reset languages and reset thresholds agree. The pair-specific unit merges form a spanning path, forcing the pair-distance MST weight K(B)=|Q_B|-1=2m-2. Applied to the classical m-state Cerny family, |Q_B|=2m-1 and rt(B)=(m-1)^2=(|Q_B|-1)^2/4, so rt(B)/K(B)=(|Q_B|-1)/4 and no universal constant C gives rt<=C K (even with a fixed additive constant).

Interface: Complete deterministic automata; at least two alphabet letters; the core automaton is synchronizing. Pair distance is the shortest word merging a specified pair; K is the minimum spanning-tree weight using these distances. The construction is not strongly connected: the original states form a closed subautomaton.

Proof spine: For every letter c, the new states map into Qc while original states still have image Qc; induction on a nonempty word gives Q_B w=Q_A w. The pairs {q_i,p_i} merge under a and {p_i,q_{i+1}} under b, giving a unit-weight spanning path. Since every edge weight is at least one, this attains the |Q_B|-1 MST lower bound. The classical Cerny threshold then yields the unbounded ratio.

Costs: The extension is written with O(m times alphabet-size) transition assignments. Pair distances are polynomial-time computable by reverse search on unordered pairs. This does not provide a short-reset algorithm or improve general reset-word upper bounds; exact subset BFS appears only as a finite check in the source.
Failure: This refutes the specific proposal that a fixed multiplicative rescaling of pair-distance MST universally pays for a single common reset word. It does not refute the Cerny conjecture, all polynomial-size potentials, or the same claim restricted to strongly connected automata. Historical priority is UNKNOWN.
Closest comparator: The construction uses the classical Cerny family and the source cites established reset-threshold literature. The exact extension formulation was not independently checked against prior art during intake; no novelty or priority claim is made.
Open verification: Independently reconstruct the reset-language equality and MST calculation, audit the precise extension against automata literature, and separately test whether an analogous obstruction can satisfy strong connectivity without changing the claimed scope.

card_roles.text: Claim: The source gives an explicit strongly connected, oriented, triangle-free 52-outregular 0/1 digraph on n=160 vertices. For the stationary distribution pi of its uniform-outneighbor walk, with s(v) the number of exact two-step outneighbors excluding v and its first outneighbors, it reports E_pi[d^-(v)+s(v)] = 104 - 2493/485524 < 2r=104. Thus the proposed universal stationary joint inequality is false even under equal row degree, strong connectivity and directed-triangle exclusion. The same construction family at n=64,r=20 separately gives E_pi s=20-29/1186<r. Since 160>3*52, these examples do not contradict the directed triangle case of Caccetta–Häggkvist.

Interface: Finite oriented directed graphs with adjacency entries in {0,1}, equal outdegree r, strong connectivity, and no directed 3-cycles. pi is the unique stationary distribution of the uniform-outneighbor Markov chain. s(v) counts vertices reachable in exactly two steps but not at distance zero or one.

Proof spine: The source builds a 16-vertex row-4 block H and substitutes it into a triangle-free regular outer digraph F_q, adding complete inter-block arcs. It derives the stationary law from R sigma=q*1+H^T sigma and gives exact rational group masses. At q=3, n=160,r=52; direct rational evaluation yields the displayed deficit. The source reports a second exact implementation and full adjacency/stationary certificates.

Costs: The witness is finite and explicit; the report states that two exact-rational implementations verify adjacency, stationary coordinates, connectivity, triangle exclusion and neighborhood counts. This intake checked file hashes and routes only and did not run either implementation.
Failure: The counterexample falsifies only the proposed stationary second-neighborhood inequality and the specific indegree-paid joint repair. It is not a counterexample to Caccetta–Häggkvist, does not establish an impossibility theorem for stationary methods, and does not create a new CH barrier. The valid reverse-step entropy lemma is separate from the failed charging step.

card_roles.text: Claim: Under x'(t)=A x(t) with Metzler A, known positive initial population p, neutral inherited binary tags whose initial fractions W_ji are known, a sufficient declared-state model, and at most s off-diagonal incoming rates per state, the source derives f'_ji(0)=sum_{k!=i} lambda_ik(W_jk-W_ji), where f_ji=x_ji/x_0i and lambda_ik=A_ik p_k/p_i. With an (s+1)-disjunct code, lambda_ik is the minimum eligible derivative over rows W_ji=0,W_jk=1. Separately, for a time-homogeneous A and occupation-integrated tagged counts U_j=integral_0^T exp(-lambda t)x_j(t)dt, endpoint quantity H_j=exp(-lambda T)x_j(T)-x_j(0) satisfies (A-lambda I)U_j=H_j; the source derives a row equation Z_i a_i=D_i for the off-diagonal rates. If every at-most-2s-column submatrix of Z_i has full column rank, the s-sparse row is unique. The source reports exact rational finite examples, including recovery of 16,256 rates.

Interface: Requires known/observed initial abundances and tag fractions, tag neutrality and inheritance, all declared-state classification, calibrated measurements, and no tag-dependent dynamics. The finite-interval identity additionally requires one common time-independent A and occupation-integrated measurements, not just endpoints. Hidden heterogeneous subtypes can invalidate the mean model.

Proof spine: Apply the quotient rule to tagged and total population equations; the diagonal A_ii terms cancel. Nonnegative incoming rates plus disjunctness make the min decoder exact. For finite intervals, integrate the linear dynamics with exponential weight, integrate by parts, then subtract F_ji times the untagged coordinate equation so diagonal and lambda terms cancel. Uniqueness follows because the difference of two s-sparse solutions is a null vector on at most 2s columns.

Costs: The reported 128-state derivative example uses 49 tags and O(n^2 q^2) comparisons for the stated polynomial code. Finite-interval support enumeration is combinatorial in s; conditioning, population balance, discretization/assay error and independent replicate-population variation require separate accounting. Exact rational code tests are source-reported and were not rerun.
Failure: The derivation does not construct a physical state-dependent tag writer or establish neutral tags, lumpability, feasible destructive-cohort sampling, or acquisition advantage over ordinary barcoding/tracer tomography. Exact-real identifiability is not a finite-precision stability guarantee. No new coding theorem or transformative capability is claimed.
Closest comparator: The source explicitly places the construction alongside known prospective lineage barcoding, group testing, compressed sensing and tracer tomography and credits the polynomial disjunct-code construction to Kautz–Singleton. Those prior-art claims were not independently audited during intake.
Open verification: Independently derive both identities and verify the exact-rank assumptions; assess whether the required tag/occupation interface is physically available and compare charged resources with ordinary prospective barcoding and tracer methods.

card_roles.text: Claim: For the source's ideal model of a random bounded measurable classical signal with a constant clock channel, fixed reciprocal real couplings, coherent ladder evolution and endpoint preparations/readouts, define for each finite channel word w of length r the signed endpoint contrast D_w(lambda)=i^r E[U_w[a;lambda]_{r0}-U_w[a;lambda]_{0r}]. The source reports an exact reciprocity identity and a completeness theorem: the signal law equals its time-reversed law if and only if D_w(lambda)=0 for every finite word w and every positive coupling lambda. The proof route extracts all antisymmetric expected ordered integrals from analytic leading coefficients and uses the clock-augmented integrated path and Stone–Weierstrass to separate bounded signal laws. This is an unbounded hierarchy, not a finite-resource decision procedure.

Interface: The signal is not altered or replayed; the ideal theorem assumes reproducible windows, a noninvasive signal, known bounded channels including a clock, real calibrated reciprocal coherent couplings, phase reference and endpoint readout. A time reversal of increments is defined in the source using the clock-augmented path; it is not ordinary signed path inversion.

Proof spine: Real symmetric instantaneous Hamiltonians imply the propagator under reversed input is the transpose of the forward propagator. Endpoint swapping makes the contrast exactly odd under reversal. Its first nonzero Dyson coefficient is the difference between expected ordered integrals for w and reverse(w). If all contrasts vanish for every positive lambda, analyticity gives equality of all expected iterated integrals; the clock coordinate removes reparameterization ambiguity, and the shuffle algebra plus Stone–Weierstrass yields equality of the bounded path laws.

Costs: For any fixed word, the report gives a bounded-outcome finite-shot concentration bound and a finite-coupling remainder. The complete theorem quantifies over all finite words and positive couplings; it supplies no uniform first distinguishing word length, polynomial-time search, uniform sample complexity, or practical signal-to-noise guarantee.
Failure: The only demonstrated finite-strength separation is from constant commuting integrators. Existing time-resolved and nonlinear correlation sensors can distinguish suitable signals. No physical platform, native signal-to-coupling transduction, calibrated advantage, or new sensor capability was demonstrated. The rotating example is identified as a spin-1 Rabi-class calculation.
Closest comparator: The source cites Chen iterated integrals, sparse path-signature results, Rabi dynamics, SENSIT time-reversal sensing and quantum computational sensing as close prior work; it explicitly withholds novelty. Intake did not independently verify that literature boundary.
Open verification: Reconstruct the completeness proof with the exact path-law topology and reversal convention; check the relation to sparse path characteristic functions and prior time-reversal sensing; require a physical target and matched native-sensor baseline before any capability claim.

card_roles.text: Claim: Under the source's weak-Hall, local-diffusive model with the same scalar zero-field longitudinal conductivity in every domain and fixed single-domain coefficients a,c, tetragonal symmetry gives K0=diag(a,a,c) and K(n)=aI+(c-a)nn^T. First-order arithmetic averaging is exact under those assumptions: for Q=E[nn^T], tr Q=1, K_eff=aI+(c-a)Q and b_hat·K_eff b_hat=a+(c-a)E[(n·b_hat)^2]. For the three ideal SrTiO3 tetragonal variants and B along [111], every squared projection is 1/3, so the model predicts S_[111]=(2a+c)/3 independent of domain populations. Orthogonal full-tensor slopes sum to tr K_eff=2a+c, invariant under pure orientation redistribution in this model. These are conditional deductions, not measured values of a,c or evidence for a microscopic mechanism.

Interface: Assumes weak Hall response, local diffusion, a common scalar zero-field longitudinal conductivity, fixed a,c across intervention, and arithmetic averaging at first order. Arbitrary inhomogeneous anisotropic composites are outside scope. B projection and contact-normal geometry must not be conflated.

Proof spine: The axial-vector transformation laws make K transform as an ordinary rank-two tensor. Tetragonal D4h symmetry fixes diag(a,a,c); the domain director gives the rank-one form. The uniform zero-field corrector under common scalar longitudinal conductivity makes the first-order effective Hall tensor the arithmetic mean, from which the [111] and trace identities follow.

Costs: The source digitizes plotted vector markers from a published figure and reports descriptive finite-field statistics. Its +/- perturbation range for extraction is a sensitivity interval, not a confidence interval or experimental error model. No suitable matched before/after [111] or full three-axis raw dataset was located in the bounded search.
Failure: The analysis neither statistically rejects the microscopic scattering explanation nor establishes a new natural mechanism. Contact gains, temperature mismatch, heat-flow changes, spatially varying longitudinal anisotropy, domain walls and other scattering changes remain possible. A raw Hall angle is not automatically the zero-field slope.
Closest comparator: The source identifies prior SrTiO3 domain-orientation work and known Hall-sign-inversion examples in inhomogeneous media. It makes no novelty claim; citations and figures were not independently reanalysed during intake.
Open verification: Acquire matched-temperature full-tensor Hall measurements in [111] and three orthogonal geometries with calibrated contact/longitudinal response; then test the invariants against spatially inhomogeneous transport and the source-reported uncertainty.

card_roles.text: Claim: In the source's selected-trace analysis of 44 traces from 43 cells with a cell-identity-based discovery/validation split, the frozen primary OFF-window classifier labeled one resolved post-pulse onset among 16 validation pulse traces from 15 cells, alongside 15 immediate/unresolved traces. The identity of late events changed under the fixed 200-ms guard and threshold sensitivities; counts across the six fixed settings ranged from zero to two of 16. The report therefore does not identify a robust excess of delayed post-pulse activation over ordinary recovery. This is a source-reported negative analysis, not evidence that mechanical priming is absent.

Interface: The observable is first sustained autonomous rotation during the OFF interval, not stator attachment or occupancy. The report uses selected 4-kHz long-axis/PCA angles, cell-level discovery/validation separation, a fixed Savitzky–Golay derivative, thresholds, persistence rule and edge guards. The 44 traces cover 43 unique cells; one cell appears under both forcing directions within the validation grouping, but no cell crosses the discovery/validation split.

Proof spine: The candidate distinguishes instantaneous activation from a latent mechanically prepared state by comparing first sustained autonomous-motion onset during OFF intervals. Extraction rules were frozen before validation outcomes were parsed, with a documented pre-validation correction. The reported late-event identities are guard/threshold sensitive and ordinary unforced recovery is sparse, so the source closes the candidate as unidentified rather than claiming a mechanism.

Costs: The original multi-gigabyte source ZIP was not fully downloaded; selected entries were fetched by byte ranges and individually CRC/SHA checked in the source record. This intake did not reacquire data, rerun extraction, or fit a calibrated clustered-event model. Reported Poisson tails are explicitly descriptive, not calibrated tests.
Failure: The analysis does not rule out sub-100-ms priming, priming hidden inside the edge guard, mechanical pinning, or attachment masked by bearing/glass effects. It cannot observe molecular attachment. The selected records are too sparse and sensitivity-unstable to establish delayed priming; no causal or molecular claim follows.
Closest comparator: The source identifies Ito, Nakamura and Toyabe (2021) as the experimental source and notes prior hypotheses of rotation-enhanced assembly, gear activation and MotB stretching. card_roles.text: Claim: Let n>=1 qubits start in |0^n> and a reference with H_R=sum_{r>=0} r|r><r| start in any finite-mean state rho of mean mu. Under an arbitrary joint unitary commuting with H_S+H_R, retain all outputs and compare the final joint state with |+^n><+^n| tensor the same original rho, uncorrelated. If D is their trace distance, then for every s>0, D >= exp(-s mu)[1-((1+exp(-s))/2)^n], and D >= n/[8e(mu+n)]. Thus for 0<epsilon<=1/(16e), D<=epsilon requires mu>=n/(16e epsilon). A supplied sine-profile reference and explicit conserving interactions attain D<=min(1, pi sqrt(n(n+1))/(2(L+1))) with mean energy n+(L-1)/2, giving optimal Theta(n/epsilon) scaling for this exact joint-return task.

Interface: All system outputs and the reference are retained; the target contains the same uncorrelated reference. U may be arbitrary subject to exact total-energy conservation. Trace distance is 1/2 trace norm. The upper construction assumes the coherent sine reference is supplied; it is not constructed from free inputs.

Proof spine: The invariant bounded effect exp[-s(H_S+H_R)] has expectations L_rho(s) and L_rho(s)((1+exp(-s))/2)^n on actual and target states. Jensen gives L_rho(s)>=exp(-s mu), yielding the all-protocol lower bound. For the upper bound, sector Hadamards yield 2^(-n/2) sum_x |x> T^|x| eta; telescoping shift error and W~Bin(n,1/2) give the uniform overlap bound.

Costs: Mean resource scaling is Theta(n/epsilon) in the stated small-error regime, with a supplied sine reference of mean n+(L-1)/2; no gate-synthesis or reference-preparation complexity is bounded.
Failure: The lower bound is for the entire joint output/reference comparison, not the reduced system channel or a channel diamond norm. The construction prepares no reference and charges no arbitrary-unitary synthesis; initial-reference precision contributes additional error. A fixed-pure-reference overlap optimum is also source-derived but does not imply efficient synthesis.
Closest comparator: The source cites Chiribella, Yang and Renner (2021), “Fundamental Energy Requirement of Reversible Quantum Operations,” https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevX.11.021014, plus finite sine-reference and catalytic-coherence antecedents. Citation and exact priority comparison were not rechecked in intake; no novelty is claimed.

card_roles.text: Claim: There is a polynomial-time Turing reduction from the 0/1 permanent to exact evaluation of E[p(G)^2] for integer-coefficient arithmetic circuits p and independent standard real Gaussian inputs G. The proof builds 0/1 Gram factorizations B_t B_t^T=tI+A, uses the complex Wick identity to recover perm(tI+A) from the real and imaginary circuit norms, interpolates at N+1 positive integer t values, and takes an exact integer square root of perm(M)^2.

Interface: The oracle returns the exact rational/integer expectation with all output bits. The reduction makes polynomially many queries to circuits of polynomial size and degree over independent standard real Gaussians. It is a Turing reduction, not one-query or approximate evaluation.

Proof spine: For a bipartite adjacency matrix A=[[0,M],[M^T,0]], construct B_t from edge columns e_i+e_j and t-d_i singleton columns so B_tB_t^T=tI+A. Complex Gaussian moments give E|P_t|^2=2^N perm(B_tB_t^T); split into real/imaginary integer circuits. Interpolation recovers q(0)=perm(A)=perm(M)^2.

Costs: The construction uses N+1 integer parameter points and polynomial-size, degree-N circuits with O(N^2) real Gaussian inputs; outputs and interpolation operands have polynomial bit length.
Failure: No implication is claimed for approximate/additive norm evaluation, norm-zero testing, randomized polynomial identity testing, or general identity testing. The reported finite exact checker is not run by this intake.
Closest comparator: Uses the standard #P-completeness of the 0/1 permanent (Valiant, 1979); the source cites this antecedent. It does not make a new approximate-counting or identity-testing result.
Open verification: Independently reconstruct normalization, circuit construction, interpolation bit sizes, and the exact-query interface; verify the cited permanent-completeness input.

card_roles.text: Claim: Given T explicit trace-preserving instruments on C^d with Gaussian-rational Kraus matrices of at most B-bit numerators/denominators, a polynomial-bit algorithm decides whether every length-T history product has rank at most one without listing histories. For a repeated fixed instrument, eventual all-history collapse occurs iff it has occurred by D=binom(d,2) steps. Separately, the exact terminal channel after forgetting outcomes has a representation sum_{j<=d^4} c_j B_j X B_j*, where c_j are positive rationals and every B_j is an actual length-T branch product. If all products have rank at most one, this yields an exact measure-prepare form.

Interface: The instrument and Kraus matrices are supplied. Complexity is polynomial in dense Hilbert dimension d and input bit length, not in qubit count log2(d). Compression preserves only the terminal forgotten-outcome channel; it need not preserve histories, their probabilities, or intermediate intervention responses.

Proof spine: Lift each Kraus operator to the exterior square; the span of all branch images is propagated by V_t=sum_i (Lambda^2 K_i^(t))V_(t-1), and is zero iff every branch product has rank<=1. For a fixed instrument the descending subspace chain stabilizes within D steps. For compression, vectorize branch products into Hermitian Choi rank-one matrices in a d^4-dimensional real space and use exact rational conic elimination with positive weights.

Costs: The source gives polynomial bit complexity in dense dimension d, instrument length and input bit size, with O(sum_t r_t D^3) field operations for the span test and at most d^4 retained products.
Failure: This is not representation-independent entanglement-breaking recognition: the source gives an invertible-Pauli Kraus representation of a depolarizing entanglement-breaking channel that fails the test. d^4 is polynomial in d but exponential in qubits. No generic simulation improvement follows. Its exact combined novelty is unestablished.
Closest comparator: The source identifies exterior algebra, conic Caratheodory elimination and rank-one Kraus/measure-prepare equivalence as standard. It cites Horodecki, Shor and Ruskai (2003), https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/0302031. No broad entanglement-breaking theorem is claimed.
Open verification: Independently audit the exact rational bit-growth argument, history-span closure, fixed-instrument cutoff, positive elimination, and terminal-channel-only semantics.

card_roles.text: Claim: For each k>=1, an explicit connected path instance on 2k qubits with 2k-1 gates and positive rational weights has exact partition function Z=26^k(1+epsilon)^(k-1), epsilon=1/(100k), computable in O(k) rational arithmetic, while the specified iid I/C/D loop-selector estimator satisfies E[Y^2]/Z^2 >= exp(-0.02)(189/169)^k.

Condition on all bridges selecting I; pair-gate relative second moments multiply to (189/169)^k, while the bridge probability/normalization factor is bounded below by exp(-0.02). A parity check is required when evaluating selector loops.

card_roles.text: Claim: Define LY(r), r>1, by zero-freeness of the flattened polynomial f_K(z,w)=sum_xy K_xy z^x w^y when all variables lie in the open polydisk of radius r. For every complex 2^n-by-2^n K in LY(r), the maximum-modulus eigenvalue is unique, nonzero and algebraically simple, and every other eigenvalue obeys |lambda/lambda_*|<=r^-2; its rank-one spectral projector factors into LY(r) vectors. Also, if K_1,...,K_T each lie in LY(r), M=K_T...K_1, e=|0^n>, and a=e^T M e !=0, then B=(Me)(e^T M)/a has rank one and ||M-B||_F <= 2(1+r^2)^(n/2)r^(-2T)||Me||_2 <= 2(1+r^2)^(n/2)r^(-2T)||M||_2.

Interface: All matrices may be complex, nonnormal, non-PSD and varying; they share the same supplied whole-layer LY(r) promise. Products and contractions use bilinear transposes without conjugation. The estimate is conditional on the global zero-free promise for every factor.

Proof spine: Import two zero-free contraction/limit facts; establish eigenvector comparison via holomorphic diameter contraction, then use generic perturbation or the product theorem to obtain spectral separation. For varying products, propagate polynomial ratios and apply Parseval to bound the Frobenius residual from the explicit rank-one B.

card_roles.text: Claim: For a strictly positive column-stochastic finite-state transition matrix P with positive stationary vector h and a fixed strictly positive row-stochastic backward proposal Q, define K[j,i]=P[j,i]^2/Q[j,i]. The source proves ρ(K)≥1, with equality exactly at the Perron twist Q[j,i]=P[j,i]h_i/h_j. In a supplied two-state deterministic piecewise-affine response example, the proposed common-prefix single-term roulette has infinite absolute expectation (and second moment) for every independent full-support level law, while an exact transfer-operator solve gives the response directly. The source also reports four-state slow-mixing stress cases: for δ=10^-3 and absolute-bias target 10^-3, the exact finite-horizon bias requires n≥6212, while its fixed-proposal response-variance lower bound has log10 at least 486.666 and the stated independent-path count for standard deviation 10^-3 has log10 at least 492.666.

Interface: The proposal is fixed at the differentiation point; finite-horizon score estimators are distinguished from roulette estimators. The deterministic realization has a finite Markov partition and is not a claim about globally smooth expanding maps. The four-state family separates uniform inverse-branch contraction from mixing constants that degenerate as δ→0.

Proof spine: A Perron-vector/Cauchy–Schwarz argument gives the spectral radius and equality condition. The explicit map realizes the finite transition matrix exactly. Conditional increment bounds show divergence of the absolute roulette expectation; direct transfer equations provide the exact small-instance comparator.

Costs: The direct finite-state transfer calculation uses standard finite-dimensional linear algebra; the proposed path method samples O(n) transitions per path and has the reported unbounded/infinite roulette cost in this example. No scaling advantage is established. In the reported δ=10^-3 stress case, the variance/path-count lower bounds make this specific estimator impractical; the exact transfer solve remains available for the finite state model.
Failure: The generic eigenfunction-twist principle is prior work, as the source itself notes. The counterexample only defeats the stated fixed stationary proposal and common-prefix single-term roulette. It is not a lower bound for horizon-dependent/adaptive proposals, resampling, control variates, other couplings, all chaotic-response methods, or smooth systems.
Closest comparator: The source compares the Perron twist to Whiteley–Lee, “Twisted particle filters” (arXiv:1210.0220v4), and the single-term estimator identity to Rhee–Glynn/Vihola (arXiv:1512.01022). Generic twist and exact transfer methods are established; priority of this explicit example is unknown.
Open verification: Independently reconstruct the finite-state response and non-integrability calculation, and require any replacement estimator to be compared against an acquired transfer-operator baseline with all proposal, bias, variance, and acquisition costs charged.

card_roles.text: Claim: For a Boolean f:{−1,1}^n→{−1,1}, let Δ_i(f)=H(f)−(H(f_i^+)+H(f_i^-))/2 and let I_i(f) be coordinate influence under the stated Fourier normalization. With h(t)=−t log_2 t−(1−t)log_2(1−t) and D(t)=h(t)+1−h(1/2+√(t(1−t))), the source proves 0≤Δ_i(f)≤D(I_i(f)) for every coordinate. For every even m≥2 it gives F_m and a distinguished z with p=2^-m, I_z(F_m)=p, Δ_z(F_m)=p log_2(1/p)+(3/ln 2)p−(19/(6 ln 2))p^2+O(p^3), and D(p)−Δ_z(F_m)=2p^2/ln 2+O(p^3), so Δ_z/I_z=m+3/ln 2+O(2^-m), while H(F_m)≤2I(F_m). Thus no universal bound Δ_i(f)≤C I_i(f) can hold for all Boolean functions and all prescribed coordinates.
Interface: All quantities use the source’s Boolean Fourier normalization. The theorem concerns a specified coordinate; the family need not have every coordinate bad.

Proof spine: Pair Fourier coefficients across coordinate i, express the restriction entropy loss as a weighted binary-entropy comparison, derive the modulus, and evaluate the explicit even-m family to second order. The report states the family remains globally FEI-bounded.

Costs: Finite-dimensional exact mathematical construction; no algorithmic or physical cost claim.
Failure: It does not refute the Fourier Entropy–Influence conjecture, does not show that every coordinate in F_m is bad, and does not disprove existence of some coordinate with Δ_i≤C I_i. It only rules out an all-coordinate linear decrement inequality. The equality statement is one-way: upper-bound equality is possible only at influences 0, 1/2, or 1; influence 1/2 alone is not sufficient.
Closest comparator: The source treats coordinate restriction as an existing FEI proof strategy. N601 is a complex-valued relaxation obstruction; N529 concerns a different absolute-product coordinate criterion. Neither is invalidated, and the existential Boolean selection problem remains open.
Open verification: Reconstruct the sharp modulus and equality cases, then independently resolve the existential coordinate-selection question or pursue another FEI route. Do not infer a Boolean FEI counterexample from the prescribed-coordinate family.

card_roles.text: Claim: Let W=(W_ij) have the real Wishart law W_p(ν,Σ), with ν>p−1, Σ positive definite, and a block partition p=p_1+⋯+p_r. Under the source convention E exp(−tr(TW))=det(I+2ΣT)^(-ν/2) for T⪰0, the source reports that for all s_i≥0, E∏_{i=1}^r det(W_ii)^{s_i} ≥ ∏_{i=1}^r E det(W_ii)^{s_i}. It also proves the stronger one-block-versus-rest comparison. The statement covers arbitrary real ν in the stated range and arbitrary block count.

Interface: Finite real symmetric positive-definite Wishart scale; real degrees of freedom ν>p−1; disjoint diagonal principal blocks; nonnegative real powers. Expectations are finite under the stated domain. No computational algorithm is claimed.

Proof spine: Condition on one principal block and represent the complement by an explicitly constructed noncentral Wishart law. Prove determinant-product expectation monotonicity in its mean through a rank-one differential identity and a rank-saving decomposition; use determinant-weighted association of ordered Wishart eigenvalues and Wishart regression to finish. The FKG/MTP2 association and boundary steps require independent reconstruction.

Costs: A finite-dimensional analytic inequality; no runtime or sampling improvement is asserted.
Failure: The source’s proof is not independently checked here. This theorem does not supply a sampling algorithm or a new primitive. Historical novelty is unresolved; the two-block case was already known.
Closest comparator: The statement is Conjecture 1.1 in Genest, Ouimet, and Richards, “On the Gaussian product inequality conjecture for disjoint principal minors of Wishart random matrices,” arXiv:2311.00202v3. The authors state that d=2 was proved earlier; see also their two-minor result arXiv:2409.14512. The source reports the all-partition proof; correctness and priority remain UNKNOWN.
Open verification: Independently reconstruct the noncentral Wishart Laplace-transform representation, rank-one identity, exact rank reduction at ν>p−1, determinant/FKG association step, conditioning/regression, and limiting arguments. Compare the complete argument with the published Conjecture 1.1 and the known two-block theorem.

card_roles.text: Claim: In a homogeneous spatially flat GR model with separately conserved barotropic components p_i=p_i(ρ_i), ρ_i+p_i≥0, and 0≤c_{s,i}^2=dp_i/dρ_i≤1, allowing a separate constant vacuum term, set x=a^-3 and Y(x)=H^2(x). A source-reported BAO-only check found a sequence satisfying these radial shape restrictions within 0.781 marginal standard deviations of each of six radial measurements, with reported constrained-fit χ²=0.9542; it reports no compelling violation.

Interface: Assumes flat homogeneous GR, separate conservation, barotropic pressure response, the stated null-energy and causal sound-speed bounds, and the source’s DESI DR2 compressed radial-distance likelihood. The report evaluates the finite radial constraints in inverse-square distance coordinates without assuming Gaussian errors there.

Claim (conditional source-reported theorem candidate). Assume the N402 state-independent signed-lift certificate and N403 rectangular sharpness identity. For each finite channel \(\mathcal N:A\to B\), let \(J\) be its unnormalized Choi matrix and \(J^+\) its Moore–Penrose inverse. The manuscript claims that one Choi objective
\[
 M(\mathcal N)=\min_{\sigma\in\mathcal D(B)}\left\|\operatorname{Tr}_B[(I\otimes\sigma)J^+(I\otimes\sigma)]\right\|_\infty,
 \qquad \operatorname{ran}(I\otimes\sigma)\subseteq\operatorname{ran}J,
 \quad \eta=1-M^{-1},
\]
gives \(\eta_{D_f}^c=\eta_{D_f}^{\Delta}=\eta_{I_f}=1-M^{-1}\) for (i) nonaffine modular Petz generators normalized by \(f(1)=f'(1)=0\), operator convex, with \(f(0+)<\infty\), and finite \(\lim_{x\to\infty}f(x)/x\); the same equality is claimed for each fixed Petz Rényi order \(0<\alpha<1\) and quantum Chernoff divergence. An infeasible range constraint means \(M=\infty\). The conditional information is the manuscript's explicit difference definition; it is not an optimized or sandwiched Rényi CMI. Sharpness uses a reference of dimension at most \((\dim B)^2+1\) and a binary classical auxiliary.

Proof spine reported: integrate resolvent quadratic forms against the positive operator-convex representation for the upper bound; use N403's rectangular optimum and ordered rare-flag limits for a matching lower witness. Rényi and Chernoff follow through their stated Hellinger kernels. This is a finite-dimensional Choi-data capability conditional on N402/N403, not a formula for arbitrary channel pairs, adaptive channel discrimination, or fixed-equilibrium entropy decay.

Boundary/failure evidence: at Petz order zero, qubit depolarizing shrinkage \(1/2\) has all three coefficients zero, while each fixed interior order is claimed to give \(3/8\); the rare-flag limit is therefore nonuniform at zero. A proposed extension to all \(\alpha>1\) is false: the supplied diagonal Petz order-10 example has ratio \(0.3874364\ldots>3/8\), and order ten is outside the usual data-processing range. The classical multihypothesis exponent matches an established Chernoff result; the proposed noncommuting transfer fails on the supplied support-mismatch example. No historical-priority certification is claimed.

card_roles.text:
Claim (source-reported exact derivation). For an orthogonal unitary basis \(\{U_g\}_{g=1}^{d^2}\), \(\operatorname{Tr}(U_g^*U_h)=d\delta_{gh}\), and a full-support random-unitary channel \(\mathcal N_p(X)=\sum_g p_gU_gXU_g^*\), the manuscript solves its Choi objective exactly:
\[
 M(\mathcal N_p)=d^{-4}\sum_g p_g^{-1},\qquad \beta=M^{-1}=\frac{d^4}{\sum_g p_g^{-1}}.
\]
If any probability is zero, the range constraint gives \(M=\infty\) and \(\beta=0\). The algebraic identity for \(M\) is separate from N402; interpreting \(\eta=1-\beta\) as the complete contraction coefficient is conditional on N402.

For a finite projective-Weyl label group \(|G|=d^2\), generator \(L=\sum_{s\in S}\gamma_s(\operatorname{Ad}U_s-\mathrm{id})\), and fixed positive rates whose jumps generate \(G\), let \(\ell(g)\) be directed shortest word length, \(r=\max_g\ell(g)\), and \(c_g=(\ell(g)!)^{-1}\sum_{s_1\cdots s_{\ell(g)}=g}\prod_j\gamma_{s_j}\), with \(c_e=1\). The stated fixed-group asymptotic is
\[
 1-\eta(e^{tL})=\frac{d^4}{\sum_{\ell(g)=r}c_g^{-1}}t^r+O(t^{r+1}).
\]
If the jumps generate a proper subgroup, \(\eta(e^{tL})=1\) at every finite time. For one qubit with \(X,Z\) rates \(a,b>0\), the exact formula is \(1-\eta=(1-e^{-4at})(1-e^{-4bt})\). For \(n\) equal-rate qubits,
\[
\eta_n(t)=1-(1-e^{-4\gamma t})^{2n},\qquad T_n(\epsilon)=-\frac{1}{4\gamma}\log\!\left[1-(1-\epsilon)^{1/(2n)}\right].
\]
The source contrasts this exact transition with the CP-replacer Doeblin baseline; it claims a factor-two difference in the center for this family only. Weighted shortest paths and coefficients can be computed in \(O(|G||S|)\) arithmetic operations by breadth-first search and dynamic programming at fixed group presentation.

Scope: the shortest-path calculation is \(O(|G||S|)\) at fixed group presentation; \(|G|=4^n\) for \(n\) qubits, so this is not a polynomial-in-qubit-count result. The scalar tensor-product formula is exact for the stated family and does not claim a new general quantum mixing theorem.

Claim (source-reported obstruction). For qubit amplitude damping \(\mathcal A_\gamma\), with \(K_0=\operatorname{diag}(1,\sqrt{1-\gamma})\), \(K_1=\sqrt\gamma\,|0\rangle\langle1|\), the manuscript reports \(\eta=1\) for every \(0<\gamma<1\) and \(\eta=0\) at complete reset \(\gamma=1\). It states this for the regular Petz, fixed interior-order Petz Rényi, Chernoff and N402 KL/CMI coefficients. The lower bound is claimed from an explicit rare-sector local-Hessian construction; data processing supplies the upper bound. The manuscript further reports \(\|\mathcal A_\gamma-\mathcal A_1\|_\diamond\to0\) as \(\gamma\uparrow1\).

Operational implication claimed: no estimator using a uniformly bounded worst-case number of black-box channel uses can estimate this coefficient to additive error \(\varepsilon<1/2\) with success probability at least \(2/3\) for every channel. The manuscript gives \(\|\mathcal A_\gamma-\mathcal A_1\|_\diamond\le2\sqrt{2(1-\sqrt\gamma)}\to0\) and bounds the output trace distance of any adaptive \(N\)-use strategy by \(N\|\mathcal A_\gamma-\mathcal A_1\|_\diamond/2\), reducing estimation to distinguishing the near-reset channel from the reset.

Boundary: this is an information-access obstruction for unrestricted black-box channels. It does not apply to exact supplied Choi matrices, and does not rule out estimation under a promised support or spectral margin. This intake did not independently reconstruct the local Hessians or discrimination bound.

Interface: Finite channels with common input; ordinary measured-chi-square dominance for every input state pair. Arbitrary-prior k-letter ensembles, k>=2; each fixed encoding of a d-dimensional logical system, d>=2. Task-dependent physical decoders and average criteria.
Failure: The source refutes a common physical simulator and exact guessing-probability dominance. Worst-case or diamond-norm recovery, acquisition-efficient implementation and independent correctness/priority certification are not established here. Sharpness beyond k=2 and for quantum recovery remains unresolved.

Claim (source-reported, independent of N402/N403). Write M >=_SLD N when measured Pearson divergences satisfy chi_m^2(M rho || M sigma) >= chi_m^2(N rho || N sigma) for every input state pair, with extended support values. For k>=2 define
  h_k(p) = 1/k + (p-1/k)^2/(1-1/k) = p^2 + (1-p)^2/(k-1).
For any k-letter input ensemble, including arbitrary priors, the manuscript derives p_guess(M) >= h_k(p_guess(N)). For any fixed encoding E of a d-dimensional logical system (d>=2), it derives F*(M E) >= h_{d^2}(F*(N E)), where F* optimizes CPTP decoding and entanglement fidelity is overlap with the normalized maximally entangled logical state. Thus epsilon_M <= 2 epsilon_N - k epsilon_N^2/(k-1), using k letters or k=d^2 respectively. These are optimal average message error and maximally mixed logical entanglement infidelity, not worst-case input guarantees.

Mechanism and support contract. Let S_theta(X)=(theta X+X theta)/2 and q_theta(X)=<X,S_theta^{-1}X>_HS, with inverse taken on the effective output support. The integral S_theta^{-1}(C)=2 integral_0^infinity exp(-t theta) C exp(-t theta) dt gives a CP inverse there. For theta=sum_x p_x M(rho_x), G_x=S_theta^{-1}(p_x M(rho_x)) is a physical POVM on supp(theta), completed on its orthogonal complement. For logical channel L, theta=L(I/d), R_L=(1/d)L* o S_theta^{-1} is CPTP on the effective support and extends by a replacer, discarding cross blocks. The ambient Moore-Penrose superoperator alone need not be CP. Centering at 1/k or 1/d^2 and metric Cauchy-Schwarz give the bounds. Ordinary order suffices for each fixed task; the source's parallel-block extension assumes complete order (N660).

Sharp obstruction. For 0<a<1, let M reveal a classical binary input with probability a^2 and otherwise erase; let N be the BSC of bias a. The source gives an explicit complete signed-lift certificate and uniform-prior successes p_M=(1+a^2)/2=h_2((1+a)/2), p_N=(1+a)/2. Their error ratio 1+a tends to 2. Binary equality rules out a universal linear error factor below two, while p_M<p_N rules out a universal physical simulator and exact guessing dominance. This does not establish general-k or quantum sharpness.

Prior-art boundary (source-reported). The Bures metric-adjoint decoder and near-optimal recovery/discrimination have established antecedents; the source claims only their cross-channel order consequence. It does not claim a better decoder. Its internal reviews and six new replays are reported evidence, not repeated here.

N659 supplies an actual environment decoder with success at least h_k(1-epsilon) when 1-epsilon>=1/k; secrecy bounds every decoder's success by 1/k+delta. The positive-part bound is trivial outside that range. This uses N659's source-reported theorem, not the N402/N403 Choi coefficient formula.

Reported comparison. Under the same blockwise binary midpoint-MMSE dominance hypothesis, the manuscript compares the bound with delta >= (1-2 epsilon)^2/2 for epsilon<=1/2. It agrees for k=2; for k>2 its difference is (k-2)[1/(2k)-epsilon^2/(k-1)]>0 throughout that range. At epsilon=0 the bound gives delta>=1-1/k. The primary-source comparison and originality have not been independently checked by this intake.

Composition contract. Complete SLD dominance tensorizes by replacing one channel at a time and treating other outputs as an untouched reference. Hence N659's bounds apply to parallel block codes with the same encoder; the source reports transfer of vanishing decoding errors and no decrease in achievable reliability exponents. Ordinary one-use dominance alone is not asserted to tensorize. The code's environment-versus-receiver order must be established separately; a scalar self-contraction coefficient does not supply it.

Counterexample to broader wiring (source lines203-204). For the binary erasure/BSC pair in N659, mapping the erasure flag to a fair bit yields BSC bias a^2 on the source side while the target remains bias a. SLD order reverses at the uniform input. Arbitrary common adaptive output controls are therefore excluded. Retained memory may be an untouched reference for a one-use inequality without suffering multiplicative contraction.

Boundary. Capacity monotonicity and zero-capacity consequences are not claimed new. The source distinguishes this finite-code bound on separate decoding/secrecy errors from an existing asymptotic private strong converse using an ideal-key criterion.

card_roles.text:
Interface: Arbitrary finite-dimensional channels with common input; complete order quantifies every finite untouched reference and all state pairs with extended modular-Petz support values, allowing infinity. Finite certificate uses supplied unnormalized Choi matrices.
Failure: Pairwise dominance does not identify linear contraction coefficients. A common signed lift is only sufficient absent extra span assumptions; no finite-reference bound or general polynomial membership algorithm for the unsmoothed order follows. Matrix size may be exponential in qubit count.

Claim (source-reported, independent of N402/N403). For finite channels the following are equivalent: (i) complete measured-chi-square/SLD dominance; (ii) complete modular Petz dominance for f_1(x)=(x-1)^2/(x+1); (iii) simultaneous complete dominance for every operator-convex modular Petz divergence D_f. Complete means every finite untouched quantum reference. Affine tangents at one are immaterial. Standard extended Petz support values permit infinity.

Proof interface. For faithful rho,sigma, X=rho-sigma and s>0, append an untouched qubit and set Omega_s=diag(rho,s sigma)/(1+s), H=[[0,X],[X,0]]. The source derives q_{Omega_s}(H)=4(1+s)<X,(L_rho+s R_sigma)^{-1}X>=4(1+s)D_{f_s}(rho||sigma), f_s(x)=(x-1)^2/(x+s), where L and R are left/right multiplication. Positive operator-convex representation, endpoint limits and integration give the forward order; a local second-order expansion for f_1 gives the reverse. The PSD-boundary argument uses the spectral perspective, omits 0/0 and applies positive integration/Tonelli. This is an equivalence of pairwise orders, not equality of their linear contraction coefficients or a new operational simulator.

Finite sufficient certificate (source-reported formulation of an established criterion). For M:A->C and N:A->B, a state-independent HP unital observable lift J:L(B)->L(C) obeying M*J=N* and complete square domination certifies complete SLD order. In row-major Hilbert-Schmidt coordinates with unnormalized Choi matrices, D_N=C_N tensor I_B, D_M=C_M tensor I_C and T=I_A tensor [J]. The CP outer-defect inequality D_N-T* D_M T>=0 is equivalent to the affine PSD block [[D_N,T*D_M],[D_M T,D_M]]>=0, including singular D_M. Add the linear HP, unitality and reconstruction constraints. The main block order is d_A(d_B^2+d_C^2). A Stinespring formulation is also reported.

Unresolved distinction. Necessity of a common signed lift for unrestricted complete unsmoothed SLD order is open; the source reports a known full-output-span structural case. The certificate's finite reference bound cannot be transferred to the weaker general order. No general polynomial algorithm for arbitrary complete entropy-order membership, polynomial-in-qubit-count guarantee, or rigorous generic numerical decision without conditioning/exact certificates is established. The source says its CVXPY builder was not solved and its qutrit Stinespring reconstruction is diagnostic. No companion builder, replay scripts or certificates were supplied with this attachment.

Relation to existing capital. N656's equal-coefficient extension still depends on N402/N403; this all-f channel-order equivalence neither proves that formula nor closes their review gates. The source assesses the equivalence as a short extension of existing coherent-block/integral machinery, with priority unestablished.

card_roles.text:
Interface: Explicit rational irreducible local CTMC generators, finitely many reset channels with additive nonnegative coordinate hazards and product reset laws. The theorem candidate treats product-sum observables and exact stationary configurations; the implemented acquisition path is narrower: two-state local chains with a positive total-hazard floor.
Failure: The general nonreversible multistate construction is not implemented. The 64-component receipt is one finite interval computation, not proof validation. The sampler receipt is one n=3 path and assumes independent ideal fair bits for its mathematical law; software randomness is not a certified physical bit source. No superiority over renewal methods, empirical acquisition of physical parameters or historical originality is established.

For n explicit rational irreducible local generators, form their independent product chain. Each of finitely many reset channels has a nonnegative additive local hazard a_l(x)=sum_i a_li(x_i); when it fires, it redraws the entire state from an explicitly supplied product law nu_l. The packet derives a positive-resolvent/tree-weight formula for stationary expectations of explicitly represented product-sum observables and an expected-polynomial-bit exact stationary sampler under ideal independent fair bits, without enumerating the product state space. These are internal theorem candidates. The general multistate construction is not implemented; the acquired interval oracle is restricted to two-state local chains and a positive statewise total-hazard floor.

The packet reports one 64-component, 2^64-configuration run enclosing the stationary all-ones probability near 5.83e-11 with relative width below 4.55e-13. Its receipt records 42,544 positive quadrature nodes, 328-bit precision, about 391 seconds and 39,485,440 bytes peak RSS on the reported macOS host; it does not enumerate the product states. An acquired-probability sampler completed one n=3 path. This is not a distributional validation.

The model parameters, reset structure and local rates are supplied rational inputs. Separate acquisition results require active local clock probes, known hazard zero patterns and forced labelled reset draws. Passive observation does not provide those controls for free. The exact sampler assumes ideal independent fair bits with expected, unbounded refinement. The source acknowledges classical renewal-reward and Markov-chain tree ingredients and makes no claim of advantage over renewal methods; originality and strongest specialized-baseline advantage remain UNKNOWN.
