card_roles.text:
Interface: Explicit independent two-state CTMC coordinates with rational parameters, a finite explicit list of target configurations and an explicit product initial law. Additive CDF queries; finite-bin transcript and finite-support sampling guarantees have separate error metrics.
Failure: The continuous first-hit CDF result is an additive approximation, not an exact continuous-time sampler or total-variation guarantee for continuous hit times. Finite-support sampling has an absolute Kolmogorov guarantee. Marked-event transcript results require supplied bins and policy restrictions. The finite interval receipt is one diagnostic; no priority or independent proof certification.

For n independent two-state CTMCs with rational parameters, a list B of m distinct explicit configurations and a product initial law, the source reports a deterministic finite-bit algorithm approximating Pr(H_B<=t) to additive epsilon in time polynomial in input length, m and log(1/epsilon), without enumerating 2^n states. A separate finite-support distribution approximates the full CDF uniformly in absolute Kolmogorov distance, with support size and bit cost polynomial in 1/epsilon; it can be sampled with expected polynomial cost. At fixed rational t>0, a relative approximation for lower-tail CDF values is also claimed. These guarantees do not imply relative accuracy for arbitrarily small upper survival tails, total variation for continuous hit times or exact continuous-time sampling.

The marked-event construction additionally approximates hit-label sub-CDFs and distributions over explicitly supplied time bins. For K-event feedback observing only past labels and those bins, it reports a transcript total-variation guarantee with charged approximation error. It excludes finer continuous-time observations, hidden trajectories and arbitrary nonproduct posteriors.

The packet reports a positive-quadrature boundary-resolvent implementation and one 32-component, two-target Laplace-transform enclosure with width 2^-48; this is not a full exact continuous-time sampler or a full CDF implementation.

Related Astra record N592 covers a single joint target from stationary product initialization. This packet states multi-target additive CDF and marked-bin interfaces from arbitrary product starts. Their proof relationship and comparative novelty require review; this record does not supersede or validate N592.

Interface: Explicit finite-dimensional rational local generators and product start, finite explicit targets; one extension adds finitely many global gate states with a compatibility condition and optional synchronized product-stationary reset. A separate stationary sampler permits arbitrary unbalanced finite gate generators.
Failure: The source reports internal proofs and small floating checks, not an implemented general certified solver. These are distinct interfaces; they do not combine into one unrestricted interacting-chain theorem. The stationary sampler assumes fair bits and expected polynomial work, not a worst-case time bound; its fixture uses a small exact-state oracle, not the scalable acquired oracle.

The packet contains separate internal candidates built around finite-rank boundary resolvents. The unbalanced-gate stationary-observable theorem used by the exact-sampling corollary is a distinct interface and has its own source record. First, for independent irreducible finite-state local CTMCs with explicit rational generators, a product start and a finite explicit target list, it gives an additive CDF approximation with polynomial bit complexity in the explicit input and log(1/epsilon), without enumerating the product state space. The proof uses a sector bound for nonreversible local generators.

A further model permits recurring transitions on a finite list of global gate configurations and synchronized resets, subject to an explicit compatibility condition preserving the product stationary law. These interactions recur and may change multiple coordinates. Separately, a corollary claims exact stationary samples with expected polynomial bit cost for an arbitrary unbalanced finite gate generator under an ideal fair-bit interface.

The general nonreversible quadrature theorem is not implemented as a certified solver. The exact-sampler fixture uses a small exact-state oracle and does not demonstrate the scalable acquired-prefix oracle. No worst-case termination bound, generic succinct interactions, independent correctness certification or novelty conclusion follows. The statements have distinct assumptions and are not one general interacting-chain theorem.

card_roles.text:
INTERFACE
Let S be a finite commutative semigroup, m=|S|, with no identity assumed. For x in S let e_x be its unique idempotent power, and define x R z iff e_x z=z. Let μ be a full-support probability law on S, α=min_x μ(x)>0. Let T(μ) be the laws ν for which there is a transport γ(x,z) with source marginal μ, target marginal ν, and γ(x,z)=0 unless x R z. Let P_n(μ) be the product laws of n arbitrarily dependent variables, each with marginal μ.

SOURCE-REPORTED CLASSIFICATION
Set n0=max{3,ceil(1/α)}. For every ν in T(μ) and n≥n0, the report claims there is an exchangeable coupling with each coordinate marginal μ and product law ν. Its normal form uses n−1 copies of a random B and one exceptional E, placed uniformly among n positions. At most m² weighted atoms (B,E,product) are needed.

card_roles.text:
SOURCE-REPORTED INTERFACE
Each test is finite-dimensional, with dimensions not bounded uniformly over instances. A POVM E=(E_i) on C^a has positive effects summing to I_a; “strictly positive” means every E_i>0. The classified inputs are pairs of rational-complex strictly positive POVMs on a common input, where real and imaginary matrix entries are rational and the input dimension and outcome counts are part of the finite description.

For channels P,Q with common input, the note defines complete SLD order by comparison of the SLD quadratic forms for every finite untouched reference R, faithful input state rho, and traceless Hermitian tangent H. It defines unrestricted complete Umegaki relative-entropy order by D(P_R(alpha)||P_R(beta)) >= D(Q_R(alpha)||Q_R(beta)) for every finite R and every input-state pair alpha,beta; there is no equal-reference-marginal condition.

SOURCE-REPORTED THEOREM CLAIMS
1. For the rational strictly positive POVM-pair class above, complete SLD dominance is coRE-complete under computable many-one reductions; failure is RE-complete.
2. For every finite-dimensional channel pair, complete SLD order is equivalent to the stated unrestricted complete Umegaki relative-entropy order. Consequently the same coRE/RE classification applies to that POVM class and entropy order.
3. No total computable function of a valid rational POVM pair bounds a reference dimension sufficient to witness every failure of complete SLD order.
4. For strictly positive POVMs the manuscript defines a finite bounded entropy defect V(E,F). It claims no total algorithm approximates V at every requested rational additive tolerance, and that even additive error 1/4 is impossible uniformly over the same rational-complex strictly positive POVM class. The fixed-error claim uses a computable positive witness margin and finite tensor amplification; it is not presented as an efficiency result.

REPORTED PROOF SPINE AND EXTERNAL PREMISE
The note reduces a halting promise through a finite nonlocal game attributed to MIP*=RE. It reports a construction on the actual normalized two-factor Jordan domain, a quantitative Pauli anchor, local completely positive smoothing, a finite gap penalty, an ordered-word inverse-Jordan compiler, rational positive measurement effects, and dimension-independent global completion. It then enumerates rational faithful states, tangents, and reference dimensions to obtain the RE upper bound for failure. The bounded-defect strengthening uses a perfect-strategy Schmidt-sector argument, dimension-independent normalization, a Fisher-to-entropy margin, and tensor amplification. These details are available by exact page ranges in the package extraction; the intake has not checked their validity.

BOUNDARIES
The source limits the hardness claim to generic complex POVMs with variable dimensions. It does not assert hardness for transpose-compatible/restricted subclasses, fixed input dimension, equal-reference-marginal entropy order, numerical contraction coefficients, or a general Hermiticity-preserving-lift characterization. It gives no efficient witness-finding procedure. The status is a source claim, not an established or historically original theorem.

RELATION TO EXISTING RECORDS
Context only: N661 and the earlier DD complete-information-order package concern the same broad family. The reported N661 finite sufficient lift is not a general decision procedure; the present source claim neither depends on nor refutes N661's stated certificate. No N661 status or earlier DD evidence was changed.

EVIDENCE ROUTE
Original PDF: updates/DG/package/channel_order_undecidability/channel_order_undecidability.pdf. Extracted text is non-authoritative and page-separated. The source SHA-256, extraction hash, page count, source status and intake limits are recorded in SOURCE_MANIFEST.json. See the package README for source scope and the cited external premise.

card_roles.text:
INTERFACE
Finite-dimensional channels P,Q share an input. Complete comparison quantifies every finite untouched quantum reference and every faithful input-state pair; reference marginals need not agree. D_f is the standard modular Petz divergence, not the sandwiched Rényi divergence. Claims below are campaign-reported proofs; this intake did not independently reconstruct them.

FIXED-GENERATOR CLASSIFICATION
For each single fixed continuous operator-convex generator f with finite f(0+) and nonzero interior resolvent measure, the report proves the equivalence

    P >=_complete,D_f Q  iff  P >=_complete,SLD Q.

This is a one-generator-at-a-time statement, not a requirement to compare all f simultaneously. The proposed reverse mechanism appends a coherent finite reference and uses rational resolvent filters concentrating at a support point of the representing measure; the argument is reported to include atomic, diffuse, and singular measures. Affine terms do not affect state-pair order. Zero/affine and pure quadratic generators are separate cases.

Consequences reported for every fixed standard Petz Rényi parameter 0<alpha<2, Umegaki relative entropy, and state-pair quantum Chernoff divergence: the complete channel preorders coincide with complete SLD order. This concerns qualitative order only; numerical divergence values and contraction coefficients are not thereby equal. It does not cover sandwiched Rényi divergences.

QUADRATIC ENDPOINT
For standard Petz D_2(A||B)=log Tr(A^2 B^{-1}), if P does not dominate Q in complete D_2 order, the report gives a faithful witness with untouched-reference dimension at most 1+b^2, where b is Q's effective output dimension. If Q is a POVM with v nonzero outcomes, the bound is 1+v. The report derives an exact finite real-quantifier-elimination decision procedure for rational strictly positive POVM pairs; it makes no efficiency claim. It notes that generic endpoint decidability already follows from Volcic's rational Positivstellensatz, so the specific candidate advance is the small target-only cutoff and its elementary proof, not decidability in isolation.

An explicit rational qubit measurement instrument is reported to preserve complete D_2 relative to the identity channel while reducing SLD information from 1 to 16/25 on the stated tangent. This unconditionally separates the orders for general channels. Separation when both compared channels are restricted to POVMs is only conditional on the Dots reduction in N675.

CONDITIONAL CLASSIFICATION AND BOUNDARIES
If the Dots complete-SLD hardness reduction recorded in N675 is valid, the fixed-order problem is coRE-complete for each 0<alpha<2 on rational strictly positive POVM pairs, while alpha=2 is decidable independently of that reduction. The main analytic equivalence and finite cutoff do not depend on Dots. This consequence is not an unconditional undecidability result, an efficient algorithm, or an ordinary capacity theorem.

A separate complete proof in the same packet reports, for a finite-dimensional channel N with its full Stinespring complement N^c and fixed qubit half-erasure channel S_2,

    N^c >=_complete,RE N  iff  P(N tensor S_2)=0  iff  Q(N tensor S_2)=0.

Arbitrarily long finite codes are allowed. Transferring the Dots reduction to ordinary capacities still requires a complement-preserving construction; that gate remains open. This operational result is retained in this family card, not split into another card.

AUDIT AND PRIORITY
The campaign reports 16 Luna Max literature investigations and five Sol Max mathematical investigations. Targeted reviews found no remaining fatal gap in the selected proofs; finite diagnostics passed but are not universal proof checks. The source report identifies a repairable conjugation convention in the Dots bridge: the physical pairing is \(\zeta=\sum_\alpha\overline{v_\alpha}Z_\alpha\), using the conjugated coefficient (see report page 9). The original manuscript bytes were not edited. The full global reduction remains a candidate requiring independent specialist validation. A cited primary predecessor establishes the SLD-to-entropy direction; Volcic supplies generic rational endpoint decidability. Exact priority for the fixed-generator localization and explicit cutoff remains UNKNOWN.

RELATION TO EXISTING RECORDS
N661 records simultaneous all-modular-Petz order and a finite sufficient lift certificate. N676 reports the stronger one-fixed-generator criterion plus an independent quadratic cutoff; it does not validate N661's manuscript or change its lift limitations. N675 records the Dots-dependent hardness claim; the new audit gives a scoped convention repair and internal review status, not hardness certification. N656 concerns quantitative contraction extensions; order equivalence here does not imply equality of contraction coefficients.

card_roles.text:
INTERFACE
Let M in Q_{>=0}^{k x m} and N in Q_{>=0}^{k x n} be explicitly supplied row-stochastic matrices with the same k-symbol input alphabet. They describe finite classical channels, but complete SLD comparison permits every finite untouched quantum reference, including noncommuting conditional reference states. The source reports no full-output-span, invertibility, symmetry, or strict-positivity assumption on transition probabilities.

PROVISIONAL CLASSICAL CHARACTERIZATION
The transcript reports the equivalence

    M >=^c_SLD N  iff  there exists a real J in R^{m x n} such that
        M J = N,
        J 1_n = 1_m,
        diag(N_{x,:}) - J^T diag(M_{x,:}) J >= 0 for every input x.

J is a signed observable reconstruction and may contain negative entries; it is not required to be a stochastic post-processing. The reported certificate removes the arbitrary finite quantum reference from the classical-channel comparison. If the target channel has n outputs, reference dimension n+1 suffices to test the complete order.

The source's proposed contribution is the necessity of one common signed variance-dominating lift for arbitrary finite classical channels, together with the reference bound. Sufficiency of this kind of lift is prior work. This does not establish the common-lift converse for arbitrary noncommutative quantum channels.

BINARY-INPUT ALGORITHM
For a two-row channel W, define

    I_W(p) = sum_y (W_{0y}-W_{1y})^2 /
                    (p W_{0y} + (1-p) W_{1y}),  0 < p < 1,

omitting identically zero columns. The transcript reports

    M >=^c_SLD N  iff  I_M(p) >= I_N(p) for every p in (0,1).

After clearing positive denominators, exact Sturm sign counting decides the resulting rational polynomial inequality in time polynomial in the rational input length. This algorithm is specific to binary-input channels. The general finite characterization yields a polynomial-size SDP, but the source does not claim a polynomial-time exact feasibility algorithm at arbitrary singular boundaries.

QUANTUM-REFERENCE SEPARATION
An exact rational three-input example in the transcript shows that testing only scalar input distributions can miss a failure witnessed by a finite quantum reference. The reference-assisted reversal and exact source construction are routed below; this prevents replacing the complete comparison by ordinary classical testing.

RELATED NEGATIVE RESULT: FULL-SPAN PERTURBATION ROUTE
The same transcript reports an exact qubit-channel obstruction to proving the unrestricted common-lift converse by density or continuity from full-output-span sources. At a rank-deficient endpoint M_0, complete dominance of a fixed target N holds; no full-output-span qubit channel M within diamond distance 1/1000 of M_0 completely dominates that N. This rules out the proposed nearby full-span completion route, not the unrestricted common-lift conjecture. Under its separate promise distinguishing M_0 from M_t, the source reports that even revealing Pauli error labels leaves a 2/3-success acquisition lower bound k >= 10/(63 t^2); this is not a computational lower bound for algorithms given exact matrices.

BOUNDARIES AND STATUS
The exact source text reports seven binary decision cases, nine polynomial-sign fixtures, and additional finite diagnostics. The pasted transcript contains no standalone code package or proof manuscript, so intake did not replay those checks. The source itself credits prior work for signed-lift sufficiency and related channel-order results; exact priority of the necessity theorem and binary algorithm remains unresolved. The three-input separation does not prove the general quantum common-lift converse. No claim of a new general quantum-channel algorithm or historic-scale breakthrough is made.

RELATIONS
N661 is the existing general quantum-channel order record and retains the open necessity question outside the classical setting; this card neither updates its immutable dossier nor promotes its claims. N675 is a separate general-channel complexity candidate; adjacency here is context only and does not validate its hardness reduction. The Gaussian sampling strand in the same transcript is not a new claim here because N417 already records the principal count-compressed Gaussian capability.

card_roles.text:
INTERFACE
Work over C. For a three-tensor T = sum_i e_i tensor A_i, define T[d] = sum_i e_i tensor (A_i tensor I_d), equivalently placing the unnormalized bipartite maximally entangled vector Phi_d = sum_a f_a tensor f_a on the second and third parties. Write T >= S when three separate local complex-linear maps send T exactly to S, and T >=_cat S iff some finite d >= 1 has T[d] >= S[d]. The source describes this as a stochastic exact branch with nonzero success probability, potentially arbitrarily small; the bipartite catalyst is returned exactly and uncorrelated with the target. It is not deterministic conversion, approximate conversion, or a three-party catalyst.

THEOREM FAMILY CLAIM A — REPRESENTATION COMPILER
For a finite presentation A = Q<X_1,...,X_t>/(p_1,...,p_m), the report claims an effective compiler to integer three-tensors T_A,S_A such that, for every integer d >= 1,

    A has a unital (not necessarily faithful) representation in M_d(C)
        iff T_A[d] >= S_A[d].

The encoding size is polynomial when the relations are supplied as arithmetic circuits. The reported construction first reduces relations to quadratic/linear gate equations and encodes them as two-sided matrix equations. It adds marker blocks for forms x_*, x_*+x_i, 2x_*+x_i with block sizes h_j=(s+1)j. Rank monotonicity forces an arbitrary first slice map to permute the marker hyperplanes; the size gaps force the permutation to be the identity, and the forms' incidences force the map to be scalar. A distinguished full-rank marker slice then separates core from marker coordinates, yielding the represented algebra relations. This is the report's proposed cancellation-resistant proof spine, not an independently verified one.

THEOREM FAMILY CLAIM B — FIXED-AFFINE RE-COMPLETENESS
The report claims fixed integer three-tensors U,V,S, with U,V of one fixed format, tensor-rank(V)=1, and U,V,S entrywise strictly positive, such that

    { n in Z_{>=0} : U+nV >=_cat S }

is RE-complete under computable many-one reductions. The target and formats are fixed; n is binary encoded and the varying source coefficients have bit length O(log(n+1)). The reported hardness reduces integer polynomial solvability to finite-dimensional algebra representations and then applies Claim A; for each fixed d, conversion is a finite polynomial-system question, so enumeration over d gives RE membership. The unbounded catalyst dimension is the source of undecidability. No efficient catalyst-finding or conversion-execution algorithm is claimed.

The same source derives, as consequences of Claim B rather than separate cards: no computable uniform bound on sufficient catalyst dimension; no sound, complete, effectively enumerable finite certificate system for all impossible conversions; and a nonsemialgebraic real-parameter conversion set on the fixed affine line. Retain these only under the same assumptions and proof-status limitations.

EXPLICIT TWO-DIMENSIONAL CATALYST WITNESS
For X^2=Y^2=I and XY+YX=0, no one-dimensional complex representation exists, while Pauli matrices give a two-dimensional representation. The report's compiler gives formats 7x367x367 and 7x365x365 (s=3,q=7,K=364) and claims T not >= S but T[2] >= S[2]. This witnesses genuine catalysis under the stated exact stochastic tensor-restriction semantics, if the compiler proof and construction are correct.

REPORTED FINITE CHECKS — ARTIFACTS UNAVAILABLE
The source reports exact-integer checks of amplified slice identities at d=2 and d=4, a scalar-equation Groebner basis [1], marker-stabilizer checks for q=2,...,7, and integer-enforcing identities for z=+/-1,...,+/-6. The report links `verify.py` and `verification_results.json`; neither is present in the supplied packet. The checks are therefore source-reported only and were not replayed. No formal proof-assistant certificate is supplied.

PRIOR ART AND LIMITS
The source distinguishes its candidate from established stochastic multipartite catalysis (Chen et al., arXiv:1003.3059) and related partial degeneration/aided-rank work (Christandl, Gesmundo, Lysikov, and Steffan, arXiv:2212.14095). It cites a 2023 Steffan thesis that posed an honest-catalysis question addressed by the example; this does not establish present-day priority. The source's own targeted search did not establish priority for the compiler or fixed-positive-affine theorem. Historical originality remains UNKNOWN.

The claims concern exact conversion only. They give no approximate-conversion theorem, dimension-independent lower bound on success probability, deterministic catalysis, three-party catalyst, efficient construction of a catalyst/local maps, practical execution guarantee, or new matrix-multiplication exponent bound. Correctness, proof completeness, formal verification, and historical priority have not been independently established.

RELATIONS
N329 (finite-presentation encoding into symplectic fixed loci) is adjacent algebraic-encoding context only; the target structures and interfaces differ, and no transfer is established. N675 (complete quantum-channel information order) is computability context only; it is a distinct decision problem, not a premise or validation. Neither card is superseded or updated.

card_roles.text:
INTERFACE
Let sigma be an unknown finite-dimensional state on A, available through independent copies. A channel C:L(A tensor B) -> L(A tensor C) is physically available once through identified input/output A ports; B may be entangled with an arbitrary untouched reference. Source copies are independent of B and the device environment. Clean ancillas and controlled swaps are available. This is sample-plus-routed-device access, not observation of a probability table alone.

For any Kraus representation {K_alpha} of C, define

    M_alpha = Tr_A[(sigma tensor I) K_alpha],
    F_sigma(rho) = sum_alpha M_alpha rho M_alpha^dagger,
    G_sigma(rho) = Tr_A C(sigma tensor rho).

The source report states that F_sigma is the purification-return success operation and R_sigma := G_sigma - F_sigma is completely positive. The construction is independent of the Kraus representation and purification choice.

PROVISIONAL ONE-QUERY IDENTITY
For every integer n>=1, a routing superposition over n independent source copies, controlled swaps around one ordinary invocation of C, and a |+_n> return test realizes the successful operation

    F_(sigma,n) = (1 - 1/n) F_sigma + (1/n) G_sigma
                = F_sigma + (1/n) R_sigma.

The channel itself is not controlled. The report's proof attributes the exact 1/n term to the n diagonal replica terms and the F_sigma contribution to the n(n-1) off-diagonal terms.

FLAGGED ERROR AND COST
With a distinguished failure flag completing each trace-nonincreasing operation to a channel, the report states

    (1/2) || Fhat_(sigma,n) - Fhat_sigma ||_diamond
       = (1/n) ||R_sigma^dagger(I)||_infinity <= 1/n.

For L adaptive uses with fresh replicas, its telescoping bound is sum_j 1/n_j. A reported universal lower bound is epsilon >= 1/(n+2), already for a known two-qubit SWAP channel and pure qubit program states. Thus the worst-case sample order is reported as Theta(1/epsilon), independent of dimension. The L-use allocation O(L^2/epsilon) is an upper bound; replica reuse and better multi-use costs are unresolved.

SCOPE AND LIMITS
This does not reconstruct sigma, its purifier, Kraus matrices or hidden effects from observed probabilities. It requires independent quantum samples and physical access to the specified channel ports. It does not implement the earlier trace-preserving square-root isometry, provide unrestricted purification access, enable retry on an unknown destroyed input, or make rare conditioning cheap: the report gives conditional-error scale 1/(n p) at success probability p. Its canonical-purification lower bound is specific to that representation, and the live-purification latency obstruction is only for the stated no-prefetch contract. The source itself identifies prior quantum-filter, programmable-measurement and random-purification machinery; exact novelty of the combined formula and a consequential end-to-end application remain open.

SOURCE-REPORTED CHECKS
The report states 72 arbitrary-channel trials, 24 SWAP specializations, 12 weighted-routing trials, 30 full-purification overlap trials, and 80 exact rational scalar fixtures; maximum direct-routing discrepancy is reported near 1.14e-15. No code or receipts accompanied the supplied report, so these checks were not independently reproduced. No quantum hardware or formal certification is reported.

RELATION
The source identifies the earlier Genesis source-isolation/quantum-triangle investigation as motivation. N678 in open PR #41 is the relevant pending route, not currently present on main. Context only: that work concerns source-local replacement from its stated source-isolation information; N681 instead assumes independent quantum samples and a routable channel. Neither result supplies the other's access model, and N681 does not claim reconstruction from outcome probabilities. No implication or proof transfer is asserted.

PROOF ROUTES
Exact source lines: definitions and CP decomposition 46-100; one-query construction and proof 101-172; flagged diamond guarantee and composition 173-238; source-isolation relation and operational boundary 239-280; sample lower bound 281-356; limitations and representation cost 357-462; prior-art boundary and reported diagnostics 463-490. The full source report, not this summary, controls.

SOURCE-REPORTED INTERFACE
The classified inputs are finite-dimensional channels supplied by valid rational-complex Choi matrices, with positivity and trace preservation exact. Individual references, code blocks, and blocklengths are finite but have no uniform bound. Q and P denote the usual unassisted regularized quantum and private capacities, respectively; the source allows finite ensembles of mixed states entangled across channel uses. It makes no catalyst, preshared-entanglement, feedback, or postselection assumption.

SOURCE-REPORTED MAIN CLAIM
Assuming the source's uniformly gapped channel-order reduction and complete-order equivalence, exact-zero quantum-capacity and exact-zero private-capacity sets for finite rational channels are each coRE-complete under computable many-one reductions. Their positive-capacity complements are each RE-complete. The claimed reduction maps a machine M and input x to a rational channel T(M,x)=C(M,x) tensor E_{2,1/2}, with

    M(x) does not halt  =>  Q(T(M,x)) = P(T(M,x)) = 0,
    M(x) halts          =>  Q(T(M,x)) > 0 and P(T(M,x)) > 0.

This is an exact zero-versus-positive claim. The source does not claim capacity approximation hardness, a fixed-gap promise result, an efficient reduction, a computable bound on a positive witness blocklength, or a practical code construction.

SOURCE-REPORTED KERNEL INTERFACE
The assumed wrapper data has finite sector spaces H0,H1; finitely many positive rational effects A_i and B_i summing to the identities on their respective sectors; and rational rectangular cross-numerators O_i^s for s in {E,B}. For fixed positive rational gamma, finite rational B, and a common quadratic seminorm V, the companion source supplies the following uniform alternatives. In its nonhalting case, for every finite reference, positive definite baselines R0,R1, and complex cross-coordinate Z, the forms obey F_E-F_B >= gamma V and F_E+F_B <= B V. In its halting case, some finite faithful R0,R1 and some Z satisfy F_E-F_B < 0. The source says these gap parameters do not depend on a halting-witness dimension. N684 reports a physical completion only for this supplied, uniformly gapped family.

REPORTED NEW BRIDGE
The source reports a genuine rational Stinespring completion for the uniformly gapped inverse-Jordan kernel family supplied by the companion N675 channel-order construction. In the positive-source case it claims complete environmental SLD dominance for coherent inputs, arbitrary Hermitian tangents, and every finite reference, without a reference-size or state-conditioning bound; in the negative-source case it transfers a strict finite witness. The proposed construction combines coherent hub-channel control, exact purification duality for the physical leaf scores, sector-copy padding, and rational Gram/Stinespring factors. It is specific to the uniformly gapped source family, not a completion theorem for arbitrary ungapped POVM pairs.

The source also reports a zero-rate compilation of each fixed finite-dimensional half-erasure helper into repeated uses of the fixed qubit half-erasure channel. Random isometric encodings, an input-independent erasure-mask threshold, receiver decoders, and explicit failure flags are claimed to converge to the logical helper in diamond norm as blocklength grows. This removes a finite-helper-dimension dependence for positivity, but supplies no computable or efficient code-length bound. The proof applies continuity after private-to-quantum activation; it does not identify the physical erased subsystem with an ideal helper complement.

The final chain additionally uses the N675 complete-SLD/complete-relative-entropy source equivalence and the N676 fixed-qubit half-erasure capacity criterion. N675 and N676 remain source-derived and unreviewed. Their inclusion here is a reported proof dependency, not validation of either source.

LIMITS AND NEXT REVIEW
The source reports finite-dimensional rational channel descriptions and an exact qualitative classification only. Its positive-capacity witnesses may require arbitrarily large blocklengths; no uniform witness bound, practical implementation, resource advantage, or external correctness certificate is supplied. A specialist review should first reconstruct the rational complementary-channel completion and its unrestricted-reference SLD inequality, then verify the zero-rate helper compiler and the dependency chain from N675/N676 to the exact capacity classification. The source cites MIP*=RE, Smith-Yard activation, and Devetak's capacity formulas; the intake did not independently verify their stated applications.

RELATION TO EXISTING RECORDS
N675 supplies the companion channel-order hardness candidate and unrestricted complete-order equivalence used by the source. N676 already records the fixed-qubit half-erasure zero-capacity criterion and historically noted that a complement-preserving hardness bridge was missing. N684 reports a candidate construction addressing that bridge. This scoped follow-up does not certify the construction or close the mathematical gate. No earlier card or checkpoint was overwritten; the current dossier records the added source and its exact scope.

Original PDF: updates/DN/package/exact_zero_quantum_private_capacity/Exact_Zero_Quantum_and_Private_Capacity.pdf. Searchable extraction is non-authoritative; consult the PDF for equations. The source manifest records hashes, the intake base revision, rendered pages, absent ancillary artifacts, and status limits.

card_roles.text:
INTERFACE
For a pure bipartite reservoir c, let C(c) be the finite-dimensional bipartite channels N for which a finite-round LOCC instrument has a success branch S satisfying S(X tensor |c><c|)=p N(X) tensor |c><c| for every input operator X, including reference extensions, with p>0 independent of X. The complete instrument is trace-preserving; the reservoir is returned exactly and uncorrelated on success only. Failure may damage it without restriction. Communication rounds are finite but have no uniform bound; finite or countable outcomes and bounded local Kraus operators are allowed. No uncharged entangled ancillas, infinite-round closure or nonnormal operations are included. This is not deterministic LOCC.

THEOREM CANDIDATE — COMPLEMENTARY SPECTRA
The report constructs computable pure states c_P,c_Q on countable-dimensional local spaces, each with finite entanglement entropy and finite mean energy for H|n>=(n-1)|n>, such that for every finite k>=1,

    C(c_P^{⊗ k})=C(c_Q^{⊗ k})=SEP,
    C(c_P⊗c_Q)=all finite-dimensional bipartite channels.

The first equality requires exact return of the supplied reservoir on success. SEP channels remain available by the source's stated stochastic implementation. The joint reservoir can emit one Bell pair with probability 1/4 and return both reservoirs exactly on that successful branch; m repeated extractions succeed with probability 4^-m. A finite number of Bell pairs then implements any fixed finite-dimensional channel by teleporting its input and output. The protocol permits failure-branch loss and is not deterministic extraction.

PROOF MECHANISM
For squared Schmidt coefficients lambda_1>=lambda_2>=..., write t_n=sum_{j>=n}lambda_j. The report proves that inf_{n:t_n>0} t_{2n}/t_n=0 implies C(c)=SEP, using convex-roof strong monotones E_r and an entangled Choi-state test; it therefore excludes channels with any entangled Choi state, not only distillable outputs.

For a computable partition P,Q of the primes, set M(P)={a>=1: all prime factors of a lie in P}, Z_P=sum_{a in M(P)}a^-3, and |c_P>=Z_P^-1/2 sum_{a in M(P)}a^-3/2 |a,a>. Unique factorization makes c_P tensor c_Q locally equivalent on their supports to |Z>=zeta(3)^-1/2 sum_{n>=1} n^-3/2 |n,n>. A bounded relabelling, parity split and diagonal contraction implement |Z> -> (1/2)|Z> tensor |Phi_2>. An alternating finite-prime construction protects tail bottlenecks for every finite tensor power of each separate state. The report gives exact arithmetic termination arguments and finite energy/entropy bounds.

CONSEQUENCE FOR N680 — DISTINCT RESOURCE CONTRACT
The report further claims that placing this fixed countable-dimensional state Z between B,C gives, for nonzero finite three-tensors T,S, exact bounded local-map conversion T tensor Z >= S tensor Z iff rank(T_{A|BC})>=rank(S_{A'|B'C'}). This is a scoped extension of N680's exact tensor-restriction context, not a change to N680: N680 uses a finite maximally entangled catalyst and separate tensor maps, whereas this consequence uses an infinite-support bipartite pure reservoir, finite-round LOCC, and the exact success-branch/failure-loss contract above. Neither result validates the other.

LIMITS AND REVIEW
Exact infinite support is essential: every finite-support truncation loses the self-returning extraction property. The construction gives no efficient prime-partition runtime, finite exact-state preparation circuit, bounded-time physical realization, positive lower bound for repeated success, or approximate finite-resource theorem. The report supplies a mixed-reservoir counterexample to an unrestricted all-or-nothing extension. It identifies substantial prior work on infinite-dimensional SLOCC, finite-energy tail effects, embezzlement and superactivation; priority for this exact complementary-prime construction remains unresolved. Linked verification code and result files are not included in the supplied files; the report's finite checks are source-reported only.

card_roles.text:
INTERFACE
Let σ_AB be a finite-dimensional bipartite state. A preparation uses a finite-dimensional catalyst τ_{C_A C_B}, separable additional inputs, and a successful branch S of an LOCC instrument such that S(τ)=p Ω_{AB,C} for p>0, tr_C Ω=σ, and tr_AB Ω=τ. The catalyst is returned exactly in its success-conditioned marginal; Ω may correlate output and catalyst. Failure is unrestricted. This is state preparation, not a universally reusable channel implementation.

THEOREM FAMILY — FINITE SUPPORT CRITERION
The report claims these are equivalent:
1. σ admits the stated stochastic marginal-return preparation.
2. range(σ) contains a nonzero product vector.
3. σ=wω+(1−w)χ for a separable state ω and 0<w≤1.

When the criterion holds, the construction uses local catalyst dimensions at most d_A+1 and d_B+1. The necessity proof applies to every finite catalyst and every p>0, and remains valid for separable operations. A stronger reported version allows any fixed source state whose support is spanned by product vectors. All claims remain source-derived and unreviewed.

PROOF SPINE AND SUPPORTING RESULTS
For the positive direction, subtract a sufficiently small separable component from σ, flag the residual state in an active catalyst sector, and use shared randomness to either keep that residual in the catalyst or swap it into the output. The successful joint state has exactly the required two marginals. The construction does not clone the input resource.

For the converse, a product-free target support U admits a strictly positive product informationally complete measurement with a uniform one-copy relative-entropy separation κ_U>0. Data processing then gives E_R(ρ_n)≥nκ_U for every, possibly correlated, output supported on U^{⊗n}. Repeated success preserves this support while every successful branch has Schmidt number at most the finite initial catalyst's Schmidt number r, hence E_R(ρ_n)≤log r. These inequalities contradict each other for sufficiently large n, independent of how small p is. The report extends the iteration argument to product-spanned source supports.

NONCOMPOSABILITY AND ERROR BOUNDARY
The state-level marginal-return relation is not transitive: a flagged Bell/vacuum state is reachable from a free input with correlated marginal-return catalyst, and its active sector yields a Bell state, although the Bell state itself fails the support criterion. Physical postselection consumes the catalyst, despite the state-level marginals.

The report's finite capped reservoir keeps success probability q fixed and bounds output error and unconditioned output–catalyst trace distance by q^K. The stored resource and catalyst dimension grow with K; the catalyst already contains copies of the target. Thus this is not free generation and it does not give return guarantees after every later postselection. The source reports that requiring the catalyst marginal to remain τ after every nonzero product-effect outcome is equivalent to Ω=σ⊗τ; with finite catalysts this stronger product-return condition cannot generate an entangled state from a separable input.

SCOPED CONNECTIONS — CONTEXT ONLY
- N680, rank-drop catalytic tensor restriction: exact tensor restrictions use a different input and an exact uncorrelated product-return contract. N691 is finite-dimensional state preparation from separable inputs with only success-conditioned marginal return, allowing output–catalyst correlations. No implication or contradiction is asserted. The N680 card currently resides on open PR #42.
- N683, protocol-preserving catalyst removal: channel-level protocol replacement and sequential resource-cost conditions differ from N691's state-level success branch. Context only; no proof dependency. The N683 card currently resides on open PR #44.
- N685, early-flag causalization obstruction: a channel/protocol timing and resource-preservation question; related postselection concerns do not make it the same theorem. Context only. The N685 card currently resides on open PR #46.
- N686, complementary Schmidt spectra: exact channel superactivation with infinite-dimensional pure reservoirs differs from N691's finite-dimensional state-preparation criterion. The finite Schmidt-number converse in N691 does not apply to that infinite-support setting. Context only; no contradiction. The N686 card currently resides on open PR #47.

EVIDENCE AND LIMITS
The complete supplied response, including its proof narrative, is preserved at updates/DK/package/finite_support_marginal_return/Pasted text.txt (SHA-256 and exact byte count in SOURCE_MANIFEST.json). It reports exact rational checks of five flagged protocols and 24 capped-reservoir instances. The referenced verify.py and verification_results.json were not supplied as standalone files and were not recreated or run. The exact initiating prompt and runtime were not supplied. The attachment is 527 newline-delimited lines and 21,701 bytes; the accompanying intake description says 1,842 lines, so the manifest records that discrepancy without modifying the source.

The report identifies separable-approximation geometry, Schmidt number, and restricted-measurement relative entropy as established ingredients and cites broader quantum-catalysis literature. These are source-reported antecedents; intake did not perform a literature audit. Independent correctness, formal verification, and historical priority remain unresolved.

1−F(ρ,Λ_B(ρ)) ≤ 2800 [1−F(B(ρ),ρ⊗ρ)],

where F is squared Uhlmann fidelity. The stated measurement has at most 2d rank-one outcomes (d is the summary's dimension parameter). The exact dimensional and channel-model assumptions are not recoverable from the summary alone.

MECHANISM AND BOUNDARY
The summary attributes the proof to a quadratic discrimination-risk gap, deletion induction, constrained amplification, and spectral polar rounding. It says the independent-product target is essential: a counterexample has marginal broadcasting error tending to zero while every classical reconstruction has average infidelity tending to one. This does not establish a marginal-only or arbitrary-output version.

INTERFACE
Let Q be a d-state set, A a finite alphabet, q0 an initial state, and f:Q×A→Q a supplied total deterministic transition table. The supplied input law μ on A is rational; zero-mass letters are deleted, r=|supp μ|, and α=min_{μ(a)>0} μ(a). At horizon n≥1, R_n is the set of terminal-state laws generated by arbitrary joint laws on X_1,…,X_n with every one-coordinate marginal X_t~μ. Arbitrary correlations, including dependence on the past state, are allowed. No independence, fixed stochastic kernel, blind-control, or exact accepting-support condition is assumed.

HORIZON-UNIFORM FINITE-POPULATION THEOREM (source-reported)
For integer P≥1, let H=binom(P+d−1,d−1), a_P=d/(2P), and b_P=d/(Pα+d). Vertices are state histograms x∈N^Q of total P. An allocation z∈N^{Q×A} gives an edge x→y when x_s=Σ_a z_{sa}, y_u=Σ_{s,a:f(s,a)=u}z_{sa}, and |Σ_s z_{sa}−Pμ(a)|≤d for each letter. Let G_{P,n} be the terminal histograms divided by P reachable in exactly n graph steps. Then, for every n,

    sup_{p∈R_n} dist_TV(p,G_{P,n}) ≤ d/(2P),
    sup_{g∈G_{P,n}} dist_TV(g,R_n) ≤ d/(Pα+d).

The same constants are independent of n. Also d_H(cl(⋃_{n≥1}R_n), ⋃_{1≤n≤H}R_n)≤a_P+b_P. The argument applies to every finite semigroup, including noncommutative ones, by adjoining a formal initial identity and using f(s,a)=sa; no mixing or semigroup-structure premise is needed.

PROOF MECHANISM
Scale any exact-marginal joint path law to an n-layer labelled flow of total P, add terminal-to-sink flow, and round the whole integral-balanced flow edgewise within its floor/ceiling intervals. The rounded complete paths have terminal TV error at most d/(2P); the error does not accumulate over time. Conversely, any relaxed population path has per-position letter frequencies μ'_t. A filler law with marginals q_t=[μ−(1−b_P)μ'_t]/b_P is nonnegative, and mixing this one global filler branch with the population path in weights 1−b_P,b_P restores every input marginal to μ exactly. The terminal error is at most b_P.

COMPUTATIONAL AND SAMPLING CONSEQUENCES
- For supplied rational target ν, exact rational graph distances give an interval for min_{p∈R_n} dist_TV(ν,p); P=ceil(2d/(αε)) gives a reported ε-accurate approximation. The arbitrary-positive-horizon optimum is a computable real, with the finite graph cutoff H.
- A fixed positive-gap promise (v_n≤a versus v_n≥a+γ) is in PSPACE for binary-supplied n and for arbitrary positive n. This is a membership result only: no PSPACE-hardness, exact cutpoint decision, or exact finite-horizon attainment algorithm is claimed.
- After graph acquisition, binary-horizon reachability/optimization uses O(H^3 log(n+1)) Boolean operations. The number of histogram vertices is H; candidate allocations number B_P=binom(P+dr−1,dr−1), with acquisition cost B_P·poly(d,r,b,log P) for rational input bit length b.
- A witness DAG gives a succinct exact-marginal joint law, exact terminal evaluation, and consistent adaptive coordinate queries in O(log(n+1)) lookups after compilation. Its reported atom bound is P+(r−1)E+1, E≤H². Printing all n letters still costs Ω(n); exact integer rejection sampling has expected finite random-bit cost but no bounded worst-case number of flips.
- For a stationary rational k-block law κ on A^k whose (k−1)-prefix and suffix marginals agree, an augmented-history construction preserves every overlapping k-window exactly and excludes zero-probability local patterns. Its filler uses F=dM² slots for denominator M, so costs can be exponential in the binary length of M. This extension has proof text but is not implemented by the one-coordinate diagnostic solver; it does not impose a conditional Markov kernel.

Proof spine: measurement covariance excess N=V-V_q is positive and exactly zero between disjoint supports, preserving long-range quantum correlations; overlap counting bounds its row sums. The established Brooks-Harris inequality bounds V_q-C by beta/12 times the thermal double commutator. Support/weighted-strength Schur counting gives W<=4g k(k+ell)Delta I. Gibbs response Cov(Y,score)=-beta C and a Schur complement transfer covariance to actual information. C(C+R)^(-1)C-(C-R)=R(C+R)^(-1)R>=0 needs no commutation. These ingredients are credited prior work; the assembled theorem and its priority remain unreviewed. The main proof uses no Gaussian locality or covariance-floor lemma from N711.

For u with ||u||_2^2=O(n), additional optimal quantum readout information is at most O(n). If u^T F_Q u/||u||^2 diverges with beta,g,k,ell,Delta,eta fixed, the local/optimal information ratio tends to one; enhanced scaling itself is not guaranteed. With f=u dot Y, v=Var(f), q=||u||^2, (v-nu q)_+<=u^T C u<=v. Thus beta^2(v-nu q)_+^2/v<=u^T F_loc u<=u^T F_Q u<=beta^2 v, lower endpoint zero if v=0. BOUNDARY. The displayed lower bound is nonoptimal. It is not a minimizer proof, a universal variance optimum, or a sample-complexity lower bound for arbitrary nonlinear estimators. No arbitrary-tuple or higher-dimensional compiler is established.

IMPLEMENTATION GATES. The compiler assumes exact draws from w, uniform continuous axes, evaluation of a(r) in [-1,1], and ideal projective rotations/readout. No certified CDF, inverse-CDF or rejection sampler, bit-complexity bound, finite-resolution POVM error bound, or hardware calibration is supplied. Numerical radial quadrature gives CDF about 0.99655446 by r=12 and 0.99999887 by r=20; these are diagnostics only, not certified tail bounds. A finite digital implementation must state its output bins and bound the induced POVM error; a discrete grid is not automatically close in total variation to the continuous law.

card_roles.text: EXACT CLAIM | For arbitrary physical initial density operators, number-conserving hopping/density interactions, ordinary equal pure loss at a fixed rate d>0, and calibrated sparse observation with detected fraction O(theta), the canonical physical Husimi law gives a finite positive predictor for the complete permitted record under the same implemented feedback policy, with explicit truncation, tail, event-mass, grid/particle, numerical and calibration costs.

PROOF SPINE | A backward-effect argument starts from the physical Husimi law and avoids derivatives of the preparation amplitude. Ordinary loss bounds accumulated nonlinear sensitivity and the remaining count budget. The result predicts classical records; it does not reconstruct the quantum state from a classical mixture and does not claim an exact positive diffusion.
LIMITS | Grid cost is O_m((1+R/delta)^(2m)); particle needs can depend exponentially on the record alphabet. Mean energy alone gives no uniform O(theta) bound. Initial Husimi weights and phase reference require a fresh calibrated acquisition. The generic bound can be vacuous on the source's exact nonlinear benchmark and is not an economical many-mode theorem.
EXACT BENCHMARK | The separate source reports an outward exact-arithmetic certificate for a two-mode open-Kerr first-port record: TV from the correctly damped nonlinear limit <=0.000538488; TV from the old phase clock >=0.072192509; TV from the unchanged weak-bath predictor >=0.280862244. Equal pooled count-path laws for Kerr-on/off models are also reported, while marked first-port records separate them. These are finite model calculations, not laboratory data; no historical novelty is claimed.
DISTINCTION | The older P1 weak-bath result is N927. It uses theta-scaled bath rates and a different purification/amplitude-distribution contract. This result fixes the loss rate independently of theta and uses a physical Husimi law. It does not invalidate, generalize, or inherit the earlier assumptions.

EXACT CLAIM
For arbitrary finite-dimensional quantum channels P,Q with the same input, the uniform conditional Umegaki relative-entropy order with constant c is equivalent to the complete equal-reference SLD metric order with the same c. Taking Q to be identity identifies the conditional Umegaki contraction coefficient with the complete equal-reference SLD coefficient.

SOURCE-REPORTED INTERFACE
Finite-dimensional channels, arbitrary finite references, faithful states and faithful baselines; output supports are restricted to effective support and finite boundary cases use common faithful regularization.

BOUNDARIES
No equality with complete equal-reference Umegaki for arbitrary quantum channels follows. The N675 source contributes only its selected Section 2 saturated-reference filter; hardness and compiler claims remain unreviewed.

PRIOR ART AND TRANSFER LIMIT
The coherent-qubit SLD-to-BKM integral is prior work by Hirche, in Quantum estimation, channel orders, and private capacity, arXiv:2610.03706v1, Proposition 3.5 / Eq. (3.18). The conditional reference-score gauge, saturated-reference reverse filter, and state-pair interpolation in this result are distinct receiving steps. The integral alone supplies no general positive equal-reference Umegaki witness.

COST AND INFORMATION BOUNDARY
Finite-dimensional operator and relative-entropy calculations; no physical implementation is claimed.

NEXT OBLIGATION
External priority and any extension beyond the stated finite-dimensional contract remain open.

EXACT CLAIM
For a finite-dimensional channel N, a fixed arbitrary finite reference R, and a >= 1, the reference-adapted Gibbs functional has the exact variational identity sup_X log Phi(X) = sup_rho F(rho). For each faithful X, the Gibbs state Y = exp(G_X)/Phi(X) is a positive input witness, and a violation transfers between the entropy and exponential formulations without a min-max swap. The alternating update X -> N(Y) is monotone under the stated premises.

SOURCE-REPORTED INTERFACE
Finite-dimensional channel; fixed finite reference R; a >= 1; normalized faithful X on the effective output support, with boundary states obtained by faithful approximation.

BOUNDARIES
This is an equivalent positive-state reformulation and witness transfer. It does not prove the W3 target, classify all stationary points, or make monotone ascent a global certificate. No complexity, speedup, novelty, or acquired experiment is established.

COST AND INFORMATION BOUNDARY
Matrix logarithms and exponentials, reference dimension, conditioning, and stopping tolerances are real resources. No universal complexity guarantee is given.

NEXT OBLIGATION
Use the identity for exact witness transfer or a bounded search; any global upper bound still requires an independent certificate.

EXACT CLAIM
For the W3 Gibbs update at parameter 2 < a < 4, the product fixed-point manifold has an open locally attracting basin although its objective is strictly below the maximally entangled witness. At a = 3, the retained exact interval certificate gives a faithful witness gap greater than 1.03 nats. Therefore monotone ascent and smooth convergence are not global certificates. At a = 2, this comparison is not a disproof: the product and maximally entangled boundary values tie.

SOURCE-REPORTED INTERFACE
The exact local-basin theorem uses the W3 channel and source parameter range 1 < a < 4; strict suboptimality relative to the maximally entangled input holds for 2 < a < 4. The faithful interval witness is the stated a = 3, epsilon = 1/100 case.

BOUNDARIES
This does not disprove the a = 2 squashing target or prove a general Blahut-Arimoto failure theorem. The exact interval certificate supports the faithful a = 3 gap; the open basin is proved analytically in the source.

COST AND INFORMATION BOUNDARY
The interval output certifies a stated finite logarithmic gap; it is not a runtime or global-search certificate.

NEXT OBLIGATION
Any use of ascent for the a = 2 target needs a separate global bound or proof excluding other basins.

EXACT CLAIM
Let rho = B direct-sum C be a normalized state for a physical C^3 = C^2 direct-sum C decomposition, where B is positive on C^2 tensor R and C is positive on R. For every finite reference R, 2 S((W3 tensor id)rho) - S(rho) - S(rho_R) >= ln 3, with equality exactly at rho = I3/3 tensor tau. The B block may be entangled.

SOURCE-REPORTED INTERFACE
An actual physical 2+1 qutrit decomposition with no cross-sector coherence; arbitrary finite reference and positive B,C blocks with total trace one.

BOUNDARIES
The result does not extend to arbitrary coherence between the two- and one-dimensional sectors and does not settle the unrestricted W3 entropy inequality. No separability premise or reference-dimension bound is used.

COST AND INFORMATION BOUNDARY
An exact entropy decomposition into three nonnegative information terms; no physical measurement or implementation is reported.

NEXT OBLIGATION
A global proof must account for cross-sector coherence rather than discard it by pinching.

EXACT CLAIM
The physical 2+1 pinching map is not a monotone reduction for the W3 entropy objective. A faithful coherence perturbation gives a local BKM quotient above 1/2; one exact interval result is 0.5659667... at epsilon = 1/100, and a stronger example keeps both input marginals exactly I3/3 with quotient 0.7182625... at the same epsilon. This refutes the pinching proof step, not the W3 entropy target.

SOURCE-REPORTED INTERFACE
The source's faithful baselines and physical cross-sector tangents have vanishing reference partial trace; for sufficiently small nonzero perturbation the states remain faithful and retain the stated marginals.

BOUNDARIES
The coherence gain can consume the block theorem's safety margin, but the source does not show that it exceeds the margin or violates the target. This is a counterexample to a half-contraction/pinching mechanism only.

COST AND INFORMATION BOUNDARY
Exact local BKM metric formulas plus interval enclosures at epsilon = 1/100; no physical experiment is involved.

NEXT OBLIGATION
Any global argument using block pinching must account for both the finite block slack and the coherence gain.

card_roles.text:
EXACT CLAIM
Under the supplied CIR model, thermal initialization and complete aggregate count-time interface, a positive acquired gamma-root filter pays explicit Bernoulli-to-Poisson reset errors. Finite-horizon pruning bounds the joint count-record/terminal-radius law with logarithmic expected retained-factor count. A different summable anytime schedule bounds the entire count-record law with logarithmically growing expected factor count. Neither result bounds worst-case bits or conditions uniformly on rare histories.

SOURCE-REPORTED INTERFACE
Let S follow dS = kappa(m nu - S)dt + sqrt(2 kappa nu S)dW from the supplied thermal Gamma(m, rate 1/nu) law. The observer receives every fine aggregate-count time with known predictable efficiency 0 <= c_t <= c_max and intensity c_t S. It does not receive the latent radial path. For a Gamma-mixture posterior with common rate beta and index PGF P(z), beta' = kappa beta - kappa nu beta^2 + c_t; an observed count updates P_+(z) = z[mP(z)+zP'(z)]/(m+P'(1)). The exact finite-polynomial filter and its CIR/gamma-mixture ingredients are established prior art.

ACQUIRED ROOT OPERATION
Represent P(z) = exp(lambda(z-1)) product_j(1-p_j+p_j z), with lambda >= 0 and 0 <= p_j <= 1. The stored state is beta, lambda and the finite Bernoulli-factor list. A count is processed from these known parameters by a real-rooted secular equation with monotone intervals; no unknown posterior is queried. Count interlacing creates at most two fresh lifetime tags, while every inherited p-factor decays at least as exp(-kappa elapsed_time). Replacing a known Bernoulli(p) factor by Poisson(p) preserves positivity and the represented conditional first moment and pays TV(Bernoulli(p),Poisson(p)) = p(1-exp(-p)) <= p^2.

FINITE-HORIZON GUARANTEE
For the same predictable control functional in the exact and shadow processes, pruning factors at tag age L = kappa^-1 log(1/tau) gives
  TV(law(Y_[0,T], S_T), shadow law) <= 2 c_max m nu T tau^2,
  E[M_t] <= (2 c_max m nu/kappa) log(1/tau).
The expected factor-count bound also holds when the algorithm is driven by the true physical count record. For 0 < epsilon < 2 c_max m nu T and T,c_max > 0, choosing tau = sqrt(epsilon/(2 c_max m nu T)) in (0,1) makes the joint full-count-record and terminal-radius error at most epsilon and gives E[M_t] <= (c_max m nu/kappa) log(2 c_max m nu T/epsilon). These are bounds on expected stored real parameters, not total bits or worst-case work; an external long-history controller's memory is separate.

ANYTIME GUARANTEE
With a per-tag threshold tau(b)^2 = [epsilon/(2 c_max m nu t0)](1+b/t0)^(-2), where t0,c_max > 0 and 0 < epsilon < 2 c_max m nu t0, every finite record horizon jointly with its terminal radius has TV error <= epsilon, and the count-record laws on the full infinite time axis also have TV <= epsilon. The expected stored roots grow only logarithmically in time:
  E[M_t] <= (2 c_max m nu/kappa)[(1/2)log(2 c_max m nu t0/epsilon) + log(1+t/t0)].
This differs from fixed tau: fixed tau has time-uniform expected size but a finite-horizon error growing with T. Neither theorem gives constant worst-case memory or rare-history conditional error.

PRIOR ART AND CREDIT
The exact CIR gamma-mixture filter and dual-process methods are established work: Leijdekker–Spreij (2008, arXiv:0802.1407); Papaspiliopoulos–Ruggiero (2014, arXiv:1305.4571); Kon Kam King et al. (2023, arXiv:2310.00599). The scoped contribution is the acquired positive real-root factorization, tag lifetime accounting, paid reset and resulting entire-record/expected-memory bounds. No priority claim is made.

BOUNDARIES
The filter requires complete fine aggregate count times. A binary nonempty-bin record already leaves the Poisson-times-Bernoulli class because its PGF has an uncancelled pole; unexposed event times cannot be inserted. The stationary scalar CIR count process has infinite exact linear predictive Hankel rank, so a scalar physical state does not imply a finite exact linear filter. The result does not predict port marks, interferometric/coherence observables, the full quantum state, or arbitrary controller memory. Rare bursts can exceed the expected-size bound. Root, event-time and likelihood precision and work remain charged; no finite-bit end-to-end record certificate follows from floating diagnostics.

COST AND INFORMATION BOUNDARY
Expected retained real-parameter count is not a bound on total bits, root-solving work, event-time precision or arbitrary external policy memory. All compared laws use the same predictable control functional. Multi-bin floating diagnostics elsewhere in the report are not an outward end-to-end certificate.

NEXT OBLIGATION
Before finite-bit execution, certify rate integration, likelihoods, count times and root/sampling error together. A port-sensitive extension needs separate angular/coherence closure, not an invented fine record.

card_roles.text:
EXACT CLAIM
The source proposes encoding distinct nonstandard peptide products on separate mRNA templates, using established ribosomal elongation and mRNA-display linkage, then applying a downstream chemical-state-negative filter to a completed genotype-linked library. In its example, an uncyclized hydrazinoester product retains an exposed hydrazinyl nitrogen that can react with aldehyde, while the desired cyclic product has consumed that nitrogen. Marking/removing the linear products could qualify library members before functional selection. The source proposes adapting known hydrazone chemistry to intact mRNA fusions; selective capture in an RNA-compatible environment, fusion survival, side-reaction rates, and false tagging have not been demonstrated. The immobilized aldehyde scavenger is speculative.

SOURCE-REPORTED INTERFACE
Proposed completed genotype-linked library, credited ribosomal cyclic-backbone synthesis and puromycin display; selective removal must distinguish the exact linear/cyclic products while preserving their attached nucleic acid. This combined selective capture/display interface remains unacquired.

DECODING AND REUSE CONDITIONS
Two different chemical instructions in one common pool need distinguishable codon/charged-tRNA decoding registers. Mixing distinct monomers on the same tRNA species or codon is not individually addressable merely because there are two mRNA programs. Lee's established AUG/GAC/CGU assignments demonstrate prescribed placement, not arbitrary late per-chain rewriting. The puromycin-linked mRNA/product fusion is a consumed library object; translation catalysts can be reused, but the fusion is not a reusable assembly catalyst.

BOUNDARIES
The proposed purge happens after synthesis of the full product. It does not make each ribosomal elongation step wait for a product-state certificate, guarantee chemical identity, or correct ring closure on the ribosome. The donor-empty aliasing failure is recorded separately in N989. Correct transfer onto the next tRNA distinguishes transfer from hydrolysis for the stated two-state comparison; it still does not certify the later intramolecular ring-closing reaction. Chemical-state-negative library selection is therefore a distinct mechanism from product-gated progression at every assembly step.

SUBSTRATE-SPECIFIC PURITY ARITHMETIC
The cited approximately 22% cyclic / 78% linear result is for one tested six-membered-ring substrate, not the different Lee et al. Figure 8 double-ring experiment. If p=0.22 and a later filter retains fractions t and w of correct and incorrect products, respectively, then q=pt/[pt+(1-p)w]. Reaching q>=0.99 requires w/t<=0.002849, or at least 351-fold relative discrimination. If t=0.9, at least 99.744% of incorrect molecules must be removed. The source's multi-motif p^2 calculation assumes independence that was not measured; do not apply the 22% example to the double-ring substrate. The companion Python performs Bayesian and sampling arithmetic only; it was not executed during this intake.

COST AND INFORMATION BOUNDARY
Credit the existing ribosomal cyclic-backbone chemistry of Lee et al. (2025), established mRNA display linkage from Roberts and Szostak (1997), and the 2026 genetically reprogrammed cyclic glycopeptide mRNA-display result of Johansen-Leete et al. These sources already demonstrate substantial chemistry and genotype-linked selection; this intake did not independently audit their literature. Lee's example is substrate-dependent, and other substrates reportedly cyclize much more efficiently, so those are stronger comparators before adding a filter. Specialized monomers, charged tRNA, flexizyme, GTP-driven translation, puromycin linkage, chemistry-compatible purification, and product recovery remain costs. No integrated synthesis/display/filter machine, measured RNA-compatible capture, or practical advantage is established.

NEXT OBLIGATION
Test whether selective aldehyde marking/removal works on the exact uncyclized and cyclized products while intact puromycin-linked mRNA survives; control false tagging at other nucleophiles and identify truncations by product mass. Then test two separately encoded products in one common translation pool with correct mRNA/product identity and quantify the retained library. The source's stated comparison is high-diversity discovery against matched automated synthesis and current mRNA-display/ribosomal methods; no such matched experiment has been run.

card_roles.text:
EXACT CLAIM
For upstream 3'-O-acylated DNA donor U-O-CO-P_n, the listed productive transfer to a downstream aminated adaptor and hydrolysis of the acyl linkage both leave the upstream carrier in state U-OH. A downstream polymerase that senses only U-OH cannot distinguish the two outcomes. Thus donor-empty is not, by itself, a completion certificate. The failure is observational: an adequate next-address rule must also read a product-qualified receiving state, or the hydrolysis leakage must be separately bounded for the intended use.

SOURCE-REPORTED INTERFACE
Only the empty upstream donor is observed under the two supplied reaction-state alternatives; no receiving-adaptor occupancy or free-product observation is supplied.

RIBOSOME CONTRAST
For the source's ribosomal two-state comparison, peptidyl transfer leaves tRNA_P empty and places the chain on A-site tRNA_A, whereas donor hydrolysis leaves tRNA_P empty, releases free chain, and leaves tRNA_A unchanged. Checking the next carrier's product occupancy distinguishes these two listed outcomes. This does not imply the ribosome independently senses perfect chemical identity or that correct transfer certifies the later cyclization step.

BOUNDARIES
The source does not claim that the described DNA apparatus experiences substantial hydrolysis; it establishes only that the single empty-donor observation cannot identify which of the two transitions occurred. The same aliasing pattern is reported for PKS ACP-SH after productive translocation or failed hydrolysis. Physical reaction rates, sensor performance, product fidelity and integrated assembly remain unacquired.

COST AND INFORMATION BOUNDARY
This is exact non-identifiability in a supplied two-transition observation model, not measured chemistry, hydrolysis prevalence or sensor performance.

NEXT OBLIGATION
Supply a product-qualified receiving observation or a justified leakage bound for the intended decision; neither is obtained merely from an empty donor.

EXACT CLAIM
For a finite-dimensional lattice with a supplied block partition of maximum size B maintained by visible local measure-and-prepare cuts, apply independent private full-rank onsite replacement noise after each sweep. Under the stated finite-operation and model conditions, a positive block-state observer maintains a uniform trace-distance allowance for every supported current record and for future physical experiments started from the encoded state. The state uses at most (N/B)d^(2B) independent real coordinates, with sufficient precision growing logarithmically in N and inverse tolerance when d, B and noise strength are fixed. Dependence on B remains exponential.

PHYSICAL CONTRACT
The cut is part of the physical protocol: it separates the measured site while retaining the conditionally updated remainder of its former block as one component. Remote entanglement is not split by assuming spatial adjacency. Private noise labels are not observer inputs. The initial state, local operations, maximum block size, finite work between sweeps and noise lower bound must satisfy the source contract. Future-from-encoded-state reuse also assumes a fresh Markov environment with no inaccessible memory that later reconnects.

SOURCE-REPORTED FINITE EXAMPLE
The selected report describes an N=4, B=2, b=34 two-qubit control with 512 sweeps, 2048 weak marks and 510 visible endpoint cuts, with a uniform current-state allowance 31/67108864. Its independent audit text reports 48 exact noise/rounding cases. No producer code was selected or replayed in this intake. The 10,000-site, 4.8 MB coordinate payload is a theoretical scaling calculation, not an execution; it excludes partition, model, controller, cache and working-array costs.

LIMITS AND COMPARATORS
A fixed current-state error does not give a fixed error for the whole infinite record; that requires a separate summable error schedule with growing precision. The theorem is exponential in B and the cuts/noise change the experiment. The positive finite-dimensional cone floor does not transfer to the unbounded bosonic thermal space using mean energy alone. Conventional density filters and tensor methods receive the same information and are direct comparators; exclusive advantage is not established. This result is distinct from N959's classical local-preparation record and does not validate that claim.

The uniform bound is for each supported current record. Reuse for a common future physical experiment from the encoded state additionally assumes a fresh Markov environment with no inaccessible memory that later reconnects. It does not imply a whole-infinite-record guarantee or apply to the uncut protocol.

EXACT CLAIM
The product-rooted PNA growth/read/reactivation proposal still needs an actual bond-discriminating reader and compatible separated reset. The earlier reader model retains P_step=p*v/(p+w+h*alpha), h=1-p-w, only when every harmless failure restores the same parent. The new two-state imine/hydrolyzed-donor model has exact slow loss gamma(u)=2*r*u/[r+c+u+sqrt((r+c+u)^2-4*r*u)], with 1<=gamma(u_w)/gamma(u_c)<=u_w/u_c for fixed r,c>0 and u_w>=u_c>0. The exponential effective-hazard model separately gives a finite damage-limited optimal wait and eventual correct-stage probability p/(p+w+d). Composition-only full mass cannot certify sequence order: 256 canonical tetramers have only35 composition classes. Reversible recognition followed by amide-forming commitment is a candidate, not an acquired compatible PNA operation.

INTERFACE AND ASSUMPTIONS
Preserve the actual covalent product root, clear donors, distinguish joined/wrong-site/unjoined material, and acquire compatible read/release/reactivation/reset. The kinetic bounds additionally require the declared fixed rates and actual state model; the renewal optimum requires mutually exclusive correct/wrong/damage outcomes, identical recoverable misses and constant per-attempt probabilities. Sequence readout needs observations beyond composition-only mass.

BOUNDARIES
The earlier empty-carrier and copied-sequence aliases remain. Active electrophiles may acylate enzymes; polymerase displacement is not product proof, and lambda-exonuclease reset retains its end/geometry/selectivity requirements. A slow eigenvalue is not an exact short-time survival law; enrichment/retention uses a separate exponential effective-hazard assumption, not every multistate network. Hypothetical favorable rates, unlimited retries and reported numerical optimizations establish neither measured PNA behavior nor practical throughput. The source flags residual secondary-amine reactivity after reductive amination and proposes Ugi/oxidative amide reset, with compatibility, site selectivity and stereocontrol unresolved; its cited primary chemistry is not independently reverified here. Full-product mass ambiguity does not invalidate sequence-dependent fragmentation/ladders or other richer readouts. Earlier PNA synthesis/translation precedents are retained as source-cited prior context, not a new Astra priority claim.

COST AND INFORMATION BOUNDARY
Original whole-chain displacement plus local reading costs b*L*(L+1)/2+b*L nucleotide incorporations; the conditional local cassette count2*b*L still needs its real interfaces. Effective-hazard purification by factor E takes ln(E)/(gamma_w-gamma_c); correct retention is E^(-1/(m-1)) for m>1. Renewal pays all attempts and irreparable damage; unlimited retries are not a finite completion-time certificate. The detailed source-reported favorable100-step model gives about.99644 eventual fidelity and at least25.2hours chase/reduction alone, with unmeasured rates; a changed fast-detachment model reports about.00181. Neither numerical result is replayed. Quenching, recycling, donor/background competition, aging, spatial register, actual precision and reset work remain additional.

NEXT OBLIGATION
Acquire measured correct/wrong rate and parent-recovery laws, irreversible-error accounting, sequence/junction-resolving observations and a compatible amide-reset or other progression operation. Establish finite-time/yield behavior with equally informed conventional synthesis/readout controls. No integrated factory, chemical measurements or practical advantage is established.

EXACT CLAIM
For faithful positive A,X on the same finite-dimensional space, with no commutation assumption, the positive measure mu=h'' of h(t)=Tr(A-tX)_+ represents the positive and negative traces of every real pencil alpha A+beta X by the scalar densities alpha r+beta against mu. Consequently, for nonnegative mixture coefficients alpha_j,beta_j and real c_j satisfying both sum_j c_j alpha_j=0 and sum_j c_j beta_j=0, the balanced entropy combination of the mixtures equals its scalar integral against mu. Every scalar inequality of this balanced form, with optional linear trace terms, holds for all such operator pairs iff it holds for all nonnegative scalar pairs. Singular finite matrices follow by the stated epsilon-identity regularization and entropy continuity.

SOURCE-REPORTED INTERFACE
Two fixed positive operators on the same finite-dimensional space; nonnegative mixtures; both coefficient-balance equations; singular inputs only by the stated continuity extension.

BOUNDARIES
Does not cover three or more independent sources, arbitrary products or log-Euclidean means, partial transposes, general matrix-valued functional calculus inequalities, or unbalanced entropy combinations. The testing measure is abstract and does not represent one physical measurement.

COST AND INFORMATION BOUNDARY
An exact finite-dimensional identity in nats with natural logarithms. Matrix dimension and numerical precision are not assigned an algorithmic or experimental cost by the source.

NEXT OBLIGATION
Any use with three or more sources needs a separate proof; the retained trine obstruction rules out a blanket three-source scalar-to-matrix lift. General WH3 remains open.

EXACT CLAIM
The scalar balanced third finite difference s(a+b+c)-s(a+b)-s(a+c)-s(b+c)+s(a)+s(b)+s(c), for s(t)=-t log t, is nonnegative for all a,b,c>=0. For the three real qubit trine projectors P_0,P_1,P_2, the corresponding balanced matrix trace-entropy expression is (3/2)log(3/4)<0, since the sum has spectrum (3/2,3/2), each pair has spectrum (3/2,1/2), and each individual projector has spectrum (1,0). The scalar-to-matrix transfer therefore fails in this explicit three-source case, and negativity persists under sufficiently small positive epsilon-identity perturbations.

SOURCE-REPORTED INTERFACE
Three positive semidefinite operators on C^2; entropy S(Y)=-Tr Y log Y with natural logarithms; compare the same balanced coefficients as the scalar third finite difference.

BOUNDARIES
This is an obstruction to one universal balanced three-source entropy lift. It is not a W3 counterexample, does not contradict the older arbitrary-classical-channel/qubit-reference global mutual-information theorem, and does not establish a t log t fixed-prior matrix-SDPI separation.

COST AND INFORMATION BOUNDARY
Exact 2x2 spectral evaluation and a continuity argument for faithful perturbations; no channel construction, physical measurement, or computational advantage is asserted.
