EXACT CLAIM
For a fixed finite-dimensional exact-rational linear interface exposing vector and transpose actions for A and B, a declared bounded word/rank/degree search can acquire a relation such as AB=q BA+cI+UV^T, then retain its defect factors and degree-filtered left/right modules. Fresh exact-vector checks give a randomized all-input identity certificate with a stated false-accept bound. Conditional on that accepted identity, the retained representation produces exact corrections for later bounded-degree word and polynomial programs and computes their validity domains without new native acquisition calls. A separate shared-probe route can instead acquire a small faithful operator algebra when closure fits its dimension budget. Unsupported or non-unique cases remain UNKNOWN; full rank in the tested quadratic library excludes only a nonzero rank-one law in that library.

METHOD
1. Query exact vector and transpose actions under the supplied fixed linear-map contract and declared word/rank budget.
2. Recover a scalar and low-rank residual candidate, or linearize the rank-one condition over the fixed library (I,A,B,A^2,AB,BA,B^2). A one-dimensional decomposable minor-kernel gives uniqueness only within that library; fresh native checks separately test existence.
3. Factor the residual R=UV^T and acquire degree-filtered left/right modules. Their row space gives the maximal common protected domain for bounded-degree uses of the ideal law.
4. Normalize later words to ideal normal forms plus retained defect corrections. New bounded-degree procedures can be synthesized with no further native acquisition calls; corrected execution remains all-input conditional on the accepted law. If a small closure is acquired instead, checked multiplication tables represent all finite polynomial programs in those same primitives.

COST AND INFORMATION BOUNDARY
The n=64 degree-eight differentiation control acquired sigma=1, c=7/3 and rank-one defect in 68 primitive actions versus 128 for dense tomography; its common protected domain has dimension 57. The unlabelled q=2, degree-five example synthesized with zero new native calls and executed in four B actions versus twelve direct actions, after 96 acquisition actions versus 64 for tomography. Other source controls did not save total acquisition actions: kinetic 250 versus 192, Chebyshev 86 versus 80, and fermionic finite-algebra acquisition 96 versus 40. The vector width, returned field elements, arithmetic, bit growth, storage and primitive costs remain part of an application budget. These examples establish no universal cost win or superiority over an equally informed retaining method.

BOUNDARIES
Linearity, exact arithmetic, transpose access, bounded search grammar and source stability are supplied assumptions, not inferred physical properties. Noisy, nonlinear, drifting, or unacquired physical interfaces are outside scope. For the Chebyshev projection, P x^2 P differs from (P x P)^2; the learned procedure does not acquire a physical force law. A scalar-query lower bound does not transfer to the richer vector/transpose API. QuickSpec, MinRank, block Krylov, randomized range finding, displacement methods, and reusable-program systems are established comparators; no priority, general-intelligence, physical, or whole-project advantage is claimed.

NEXT OBLIGATION
The procedure is conditional on the supplied fixed exact-rational vector/transpose API and its bounded grammar and degree or closure budget. Rank-one exclusion is only within the tested quadratic word library; higher-degree or higher-rank cases and closure beyond budget remain UNKNOWN. The saved finite controls are source-reported; producer scripts/data were not replayed here. External/formal certification, physical measurement, a working device, priority, or practical advantage remain unestablished. The Chebyshev projection mismatch blocks interpreting that computational procedure as an acquired physical force law.

DISTINCTION
This record is distinct from N929's stationary-adjoint residual acquisition and N938's correlated reaction-entrance interface. It records an exact operator-law-plus-defect acquisition route for constructing later computational procedures. The separately supplied 24 October campaign closeout is already preserved in the run-closeout packet; this record does not revise its NOT_ACHIEVED or paused-goal status.

Capital's receiving review checked the cited derivation, uniqueness conditions, domain argument, procedure identity, selected implementation paths and cost/boundary passages at the copied versions. Producer scripts were not executed here; their saved finite-control results are source-reported. No external specialist review, formal certification, physical measurement, practical advantage, or historical-priority determination is claimed.

Periodic evaluations need Fourier l1 control at physical time. Changed native CP/PEC models use their actual eigenstates/energies/source response, not inherited Morse witnesses.

card_roles.text:
claim. The q-uniform extension is a deduction of the release mechanism,
with broader novelty unresolved.

Pairwise independence of child coordinates is essential. Uniform
marginals alone permit an exact 2×2 example with local trace −1/8 and
energy gap 3/4−√2<0. This records a concrete obstruction to transferring
the dyadic proof to arbitrary correlated or geometric refinements.

The second result is a generalized capacity decomposition. The entire
diagonal restriction manuscript (September 24, 2026) was read. Its
Lemma 3.2 extends to any positive-density exponent r>1: for n weighted
atoms and a legal geometric test capacity, there are at most
`min(n,2+floor((1+1/(r−1))log₂ n))` disjoint coordinate pieces with

```
Σ_j m(u^j)K(u^j)^{r−1}
 ≤ [4^{r−1}C_geo^{r−1}+1] ∫H^r.
```

The bound has no dependence on coefficient dynamic range. If weights
are squared complex coefficients and the oscillatory map is linear,
the output norm power is 2r and the resulting grouping loss is
J^{2r−1}; r=3/2 reproduces the source's log² loss. The capacity oracle's
acquisition cost remains separate from the logarithmic piece count.

The full sharp restriction claim remains conditional in this report on
the sphere packet propagation Theorem 6.4 and the 3D Kakeya maximal
Theorem 1.1. I read the exact packet interface and targeted portions of
its extremal/time-profile argument. At the pinned version the packet
interface explicitly allows transition-annulus frequency labels, so the
diagonal paper's insertion of arbitrary elliptic graph germs has the
advertised legal domain; an objection based solely on sphere-only
labels would be incorrect. The complete underlying geometric
propagation and refined quartic packet estimates were not independently
checked. The strict restriction conclusion also supplies no p=3
endpoint and no polynomial bound on its full constant as p↓3, because
packet/Kakeya loss-constant growth is unspecified.

The source ledger verified selected manuscript authors and dates from
main/README files, and older primary titles, authors, version histories,
and precise relevant statements. KTZ 2015 equations (1.5)–(1.6) and
Theorem 1.7 verify the earlier cyclic trace model and restricted input
interface; Kovač 2011 Section 6.2 verifies the older non-bipartite
obstruction. Wang–Wu arXiv:2411.08871v3, dated December 19, 2024,
Theorem 0.2 provides the closest cited p>22/7 comparator. This is not
a complete search of every later primary restriction result.
